issue.title: [Fix] qwen3_coder: don't constrain non-strict tools under tool_choice="auto"
issue.body:
Thank you @cmlccie for the extraordinarily detailed report and root-cause analysis — the GPU-free grammar reproducer made this very actionable.

## Summary

Under `tool_choice="auto"`, a single tool with `"strict": true` put **every** tool under the model-native structural tag, including non-strict ones (`function_call_parser.py`: `any(tool.function.strict ...)`). For `qwen3_coder`, that tag cannot produce the chat template's own zero-argument form (`<function=NAME>\n</function>`), and a non-strict tool compiles to an open parameter zone — so the model invents arguments for non-strict zero-argument tools (4/4 runs in the report).

A structural tag is triggered per tool call and lists every allowed tool name, so it cannot enforce per-tool strictness. This PR constrains under `"auto"` only when **every** tool is strict (or `SGLANG_TOOL_STRICT_LEVEL >= FUNCTION`, which is documented as "constraints for all tools"). A mixed set now leaves generation unconstrained, exactly like the no-strict case — matching OpenAI's per-tool `"strict"` semantics. Trade-off, as noted in the issue: in a mixed set, the strict tool's schema is not enforced under `"auto"` (it still is under `"required"`/named `tool_choice`, which is unchanged).

## Change

- `python/sglang/srt/function_call/function_call_parser.py`: `should_constrain_auto` now requires `all(...)` instead of `any(...)` for the tool set (with an empty-tools guard preserving prior behavior); comment documents the rationale and trade-off.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`: 3 new tests covering the mixed-strict scenario from this issue (`qwen3_coder` and `kimi_k2` auto → no constraint; all-strict auto → structural tag).

## Before / after (copy-paste-runnable, xgrammar==0.2.7, no GPU)

This drives the **real** `FunctionCallParser.get_structure_constraint` from this repo against `xgrammar.get_model_structural_tag(model="qwen_3_coder", ...)` with the issue's exact tool set (`get_schema`: no args, `strict: false`; `query_database`: required `sql`, `strict: true`):

```
=== FunctionCallParser.get_structure_constraint('auto'), mixed strict set ===
BEFORE (any strict -> constrain):  ('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)   # the buggy tag
AFTER  (all strict required):       None                                  # unconstrained, = no-strict control

=== Grammar acceptance of the tag SGLang requested BEFORE the fix ===
  template-native zero-arg  "<tool_call>\n<function=get_schema>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"  accepted=False
  invented <parameter=sql>  "<tool_call>\n<function=get_schema>\n<parameter=sql>\n\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"  accepted=True
```

Unchanged behavior, verified against the real code:
- `all strict + auto` → `('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)`
- `no strict + auto` → `None`
- `mixed + required` → `('structural_tag', <StructuralTag>)` (strict schemas still enforced for required/named calls)

## Tests

- New unit tests in `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestGetStructureConstraint` (mixed → `None` for `qwen3_coder`/`kimi_k2` under `auto`; all-strict `qwen3_coder` under `auto` → `structural_tag`): 3 new + 4 neighboring existing assertions pass.
- The GPU-free grammar reproducer above reproduces the reported acceptance table for the pre-fix tag.

Fixes #45235.

issue.title: [Bug] rust-server: /generate text prompts get no BOS when the tokenizer relies on add_bos_token
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. (Measured on v0.5.22. On main at b2616cabbf the Rust code path is the same; see below. I have not rerun on main.)
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, a text prompt sent to `/generate` is encoded without `<bos>` for Gemma 4. The Python frontend adds it. Same model, same server args, same request:

```
Python: prompt_tokens 14, first tokens ['<bos>', 'Question', ':', ' What']
Rust:   prompt_tokens 13, first tokens ['Question', ':', ' What', ' is']
```

This changes model output. `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` (400 questions, raw `/generate`) gives 0.938 to 0.940 on the Python frontend and 0.797 on the Rust server. Chat requests are not affected, because the Gemma 4 chat template writes `<bos>` itself.

**Cause.** Gemma 4's `tokenizer.json` post-processor adds no special tokens:

```json
"post_processor": {"type": "TemplateProcessing", "single": [{"Sequence": {"id": "A", "type_id": 0}}], ..., "special_tokens": {}}
```

and `tokenizer_config.json` has `"tokenizer_class": "GemmaTokenizer"` with no `add_bos_token` key. Transformers v4 defaulted this class to `add_bos_token=True`. Transformers v5 drops the flag, so Python's `get_tokenizer()` restores it in `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` (`python/sglang/srt/hf_transformers/tokenizer.py`), and the server logs:

```
Restoring add_bos_token=True for RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block (was False after v5 loading)
```

The Rust tokenizer has no equivalent. `DynamoTokenizer::load` (`rust/sglang-processor/src/tokenizer/mod.rs`) builds its `with_specials` handle from `tokenizer.json` alone, so `add_special_tokens=true` adds whatever the post-processor adds, which for Gemma 4 is nothing. `configured_bos` reads `bos_token` from `tokenizer_config.json`, but only so chat encoding can strip a duplicate BOS. It is never added.

The same gap should apply to any model that `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` repairs (the Llama, CodeLlama, Gemma and Cohere tokenizer classes, when `tokenizer.json` does not add BOS). I only measured Gemma 4.

Related: #41204 fixed the same missing restore for processor-owned tokenizers on the Python side. #46158 passes Python's `bos_token_id` to Rust for chat input alignment, but not `add_bos_token`.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Gemma 4 is multimodal and the Rust server has no Gemma 4 multimodal pipeline,
# so it needs --language-model-only (#49511). Use the same flag on both sides.
SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block \
  --tp 1 --language-model-only --port 30000
# then the same command without SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1 for the Python frontend

curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "text": "Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:",
  "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0},
  "return_logprob": true, "logprob_start_len": 0, "return_text_in_logprobs": true
}' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; m=json.load(sys.stdin)["meta_info"]; print(m["prompt_tokens"], [t[2] for t in m["input_token_logprobs"][:4]])'
```

The tokenizer files alone show it, with no server:

```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer        # what the Rust server encodes with
from transformers import AutoTokenizer  # 5.19.0

text = "Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:"
print(Tokenizer.from_file("tokenizer.json").encode(text).ids[:3])  # [14977, 236787, 2900]
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(".")
tok._add_bos_token = True; tok.update_post_processor()       # what _fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token does
print(tok.encode(text)[:3])                                        # [2, 14977, 236787]
```

A possible fix: have the Rust loader apply the same rule (read `add_bos_token` from `tokenizer_config.json`, with the v4 default for the listed classes) and prepend `bos` in `encode` when `add_special_tokens` is set and the post-processor did not add it. Another option is to pass Python's resolved `add_bos_token` through the same config as `tokenizer_bos_token_id` in #46158.

### Environment

- SGLang v0.5.22 (release image), transformers 5.19.0
- `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block`, 1x H200, `--tp 1 --context-length 32768 --attention-backend fa3 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --language-model-only`
- Code references checked against main at b2616cabbf

comment.body:
Thank you for the detailed report and root-cause analysis — it made this straightforward to fix.

I've opened a fix in #49525: `DynamoTokenizer::load` now applies the same rule as Python's `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` (same tokenizer-class list; missing/null `add_bos_token` takes the v4 default of `true`), and `encode()` prepends the configured BOS when `add_special_tokens` is set and the post-processor didn't already add one. Chat encoding is unchanged — `encode_chat` still strips exactly one BOS from the continuation.

Verified at the tokenizer level with the real Gemma 4 files (no GPU on my machine, so I couldn't rerun the server-side GSM8K comparison): `encode(text, true)` now gives 14 ids starting `[2, 14977, 236787]`, matching Python, while `encode(text, false)` stays at 13. The PR includes the verbatim before/after outputs and the new Rust unit tests.

issue.title: [Fix] rust-server: Prepend BOS for text prompts when tokenizer relies on add_bos_token
issue.body:
## Motivation

Thank you to the reporter for the detailed analysis in #49519.

With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, a text prompt sent to `/generate` is encoded without `<bos>` for Gemma 4, while the Python frontend adds it. The reporter measured `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` (400 questions, raw `/generate`) at 0.938–0.940 on the Python frontend vs 0.797 on the Rust server. The root cause: transformers v5 dropped `add_bos_token`, and Python restores it in `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` (`python/sglang/srt/hf_transformers/tokenizer.py`), but `DynamoTokenizer::load` (`rust/sglang-processor/src/tokenizer/mod.rs`) builds its `with_specials` handle from `tokenizer.json` alone, whose post-processor adds no special tokens for these models. The same gap applies to any model `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` repairs (Llama, CodeLlama, Gemma, Cohere tokenizer classes) when `tokenizer.json` does not add BOS.

## Modifications

- `rust/sglang-processor/src/tokenizer/mod.rs`: `DynamoTokenizer::load` now reads `tokenizer_config.json` once and applies the same rule as Python's `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` (same 7-class list; a missing or null `add_bos_token` takes the v4 default of `true`; an explicit `false` opts out). `encode()` prepends the configured BOS when `add_special_tokens` is set and the post-processor did not already add one (checked against the first encoded id, so a leading BOS is never duplicated).
- Chat encoding is unchanged: `encode_chat` still strips exactly one BOS from the continuation, so chat requests — whose templates write `<bos>` themselves — are unaffected.
- Out of scope: `add_eos_token`. Python restores `add_eos_token=False` for fast tokenizers, so there is no EOS change on either side.
- Tests: 4 new Rust unit tests in the same module (Gemma-like fixture with bos id 2 and a post-processor that adds nothing; chat still drops exactly one BOS; unlisted class unaffected; explicit `add_bos_token: false` respected), plus no-duplicate assertions in the existing chat test.

## Reproduction

Tokenizer files only — `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` `tokenizer.json` + `tokenizer_config.json` (`tokenizer_class: GemmaTokenizer`, no `add_bos_token` key, `bos_token: <bos>`, post-processor adds no specials). Text: `"Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:"`.

What the Rust server encodes with (`tokenizers` library):

```
>>> from tokenizers import Tokenizer
>>> tok = Tokenizer.from_file("tokenizer.json")
>>> enc = tok.encode("Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:")
>>> enc.ids[:3]
[14977, 236787, 2900]
>>> len(enc.ids)
13
>>> tok.token_to_id("<bos>")
2
```

What Python does (transformers 5.19.0, same files — the property setter rebuilds the post-processor, which is what `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token` triggers):

```
>>> from transformers import AutoTokenizer
>>> tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(".")
>>> tok.add_bos_token
False
>>> tok.encode("Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:")[:3]
[14977, 236787, 2900]
>>> tok.add_bos_token = True
>>> tok.encode("Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:")[:3]
[2, 14977, 236787]
>>> len(tok.encode("Question: What is 2 + 3?\nAnswer:"))
14
```

Rust unit test, before this fix (Gemma-like fixture, bos id 2):

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: [1]
 right: [2, 1]
```

After this fix, the same test passes: `encode("Hi", true)` is `[2, 1]`, `encode("Hi", false)` is `[1]`, and chat encoding is still `[1, 3]`. Verified against the real Gemma 4 files through `DynamoTokenizer::load` (temporary integration check, not shipped): `encode(text, true)` gives 14 ids starting `[2, 14977, 236787]`; `encode(text, false)` gives 13 ids.

## Accuracy Tests

I have no GPU on this machine, so I could not rerun the reporter's server-side GSM8K comparison — the 0.938–0.940 vs 0.797 numbers above are the reporter's from #49519. Verification here is tokenizer-level (see Reproduction): the Rust encoding now matches Python's token-for-token on the real Gemma 4 files.

```
cargo test -p sglang-processor
```

All suites pass: 68 lib tests (including the 5 tokenizer tests) plus the integration test targets. `cargo fmt -p sglang-processor -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p sglang-processor --lib` are clean, and `cargo check -p sglang-server` passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — no model code changed; the fix is one integer comparison and at most one id insert per text encode.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing behavior change beyond the bug fix.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Tokenizer-level verification above; server-side GSM8K numbers are the reporter's, as I have no GPU here.)

Fixes #49519

issue.title: Fix Tool.from_gradio wrapper missing is_initialized
issue.body:
## What

`Tool.from_gradio` builds a `GradioToolWrapper` whose `__init__` sets metadata, `inputs` and `forward` but never runs the base `Tool` initialization — `Tool.__init__` (which sets `self.is_initialized = False`) is never called, and unlike the sibling `LangChainToolWrapper`, the attribute is never set either. So calling the wrapper raised `AttributeError` in `Tool.__call__` (`if not self.is_initialized:`) before the underlying `run` method was ever reached.

The fix sets `self.is_initialized = True` in `GradioToolWrapper.__init__`, matching the existing convention in `LangChainToolWrapper` (which sets it the same way). The wrapper is fully configured at construction time (`forward` is already bound to the gradio tool's `run`), and it does not override `setup()`, so marking it initialized is correct — no lazy setup work is skipped.

Fixes #2944.

## Reproducer (copy-paste runnable)

```python
from smolagents import Tool


class LocalGradioTool:
    name = "double_value"
    description = "Double a number."

    # Use the string annotation accepted by the adapter's existing type mapping.
    def run(self, value: "int") -> str:
        return str(value * 2)


source = LocalGradioTool()
assert source.run(4) == "8"
wrapped = Tool.from_gradio(source)
assert wrapped(value=4) == "8"
print("OK")
```

## Before (on main, before this fix)

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/repro-2944.py", line 16, in <module>
    assert wrapped(value=4) == "8"
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/tmp/smolagents/src/smolagents/tools.py", line 232, in __call__
    if not self.is_initialized:
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'GradioToolWrapper' object has no attribute 'is_initialized'
```

## After (with this fix)

```
OK
```

## Tests

- Added `test_from_gradio_wrapper_is_initialized` in `tests/test_tools.py`: builds a local gradio-style tool, wraps it with `Tool.from_gradio`, and asserts `is_initialized` is set, the inputs mapping is correct (`{"value": {"type": "integer", "description": ""}}`), and repeated calls delegate to `run` (`wrapped(value=4) == "8"`, `wrapped(value=7) == "14"`).
- Ran `tests/test_tools.py`: 69 passed (was 68 before my change; +1 is the new regression test), 3 skipped. The 3 failures + 1 error in the file (`test_launch_gradio_demo_does_not_raise[boolean_default_tool_class]`, MCP-related tests) also fail on pristine main without this change — they are pre-existing environment issues unrelated to this fix.

Thanks very much to @yifanxiong272 for the thorough report — the minimal reproducer, full traceback, and root-cause analysis made this straightforward to verify and fix.

issue.title: Markdown backend: a list item without text that holds only a nested list is dropped
issue.body:
### Bug

In the Markdown backend, when a list item has no text of its own and contains only a nested sub-list, the backend creates no `ListItem` for it. The nested list is attached directly to the outer list container, and subsequent numbered items are re-indexed as if the parent list item never existed.

This pattern is common in legal outlines, technical specifications, and structured documents where a numbered section immediately begins with sub-clauses (for example, `1.` followed directly by `1.1` or `a)`).

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from io import BytesIO
from docling.datamodel.base_models import DocumentStream, InputFormat
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

source = """1.
   1. Sub-item A
   2. Sub-item B
2. Second item
"""

converter = DocumentConverter(allowed_formats=[InputFormat.MD])
doc = converter.convert(DocumentStream(name="nested.md", stream=BytesIO(source.encode()))).document

print("Exported Markdown:")
print(repr(doc.export_to_markdown()))

print("\nTexts in document:")
for item in doc.texts:
    print(f"- label: {item.label.value}, marker: {repr(getattr(item, 'marker', None))}, text: {repr(item.text)}")
```

### Actual output

```text
Exported Markdown:
'1. Sub-item A\n2. Sub-item B\n1. Second item'

Texts in document:
- label: list_item, marker: '1.', text: 'Sub-item A'
- label: list_item, marker: '2.', text: 'Sub-item B'
- label: list_item, marker: '1.', text: 'Second item'
```

### Expected output

The outer item `1.` must be preserved as a list item containing the nested sub-list, and the subsequent item must retain its correct marker `2. Second item`.

### Cause

In `docling/backend/md_backend.py`, line 860:
```python
elif (
    isinstance(element, marko.block.ListItem)
    and len(element.children) > 0
    and isinstance((child := element.children[0]), marko.block.Paragraph)
    and len(child.children) > 0
):
```
The condition requires `element.children[0]` to be a `marko.block.Paragraph`. When a list item starts directly with a nested sub-list, Marko produces a `marko.block.List` node as `children[0]`. Because it is not a `Paragraph`, the condition evaluates to `False`. The backend falls through to `else`, completely skipping the creation of the parent `ListItem`.

### Impact

- **Structural data loss:** Parent outline items disappear from the document hierarchy and AST.
- **Corrupted numbering:** Downstream items are renumbered incorrectly in text exports, changing document semantics.
- **RAG & Chunking damage:** Hierarchical chunkers cannot associate sub-clauses with their parent numbered section.
- **Severity:** Medium (reproducible silent data loss in document structure).

### Docling version

- Docling: 2.149.0
- Docling Core: 2.106.0
- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.10

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report and the clear reproducer! I'll take this on — the Markdown backend should preserve the parent list item when it holds only a nested sub-list.

issue.title: Markdown backend: a list item without text that holds only a nested list is dropped
issue.body:
### Bug

In the Markdown backend, when a list item has no text of its own and contains only a nested sub-list, the backend creates no `ListItem` for it. The nested list is attached directly to the outer list container, and subsequent numbered items are re-indexed as if the parent list item never existed.

This pattern is common in legal outlines, technical specifications, and structured documents where a numbered section immediately begins with sub-clauses (for example, `1.` followed directly by `1.1` or `a)`).

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from io import BytesIO
from docling.datamodel.base_models import DocumentStream, InputFormat
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

source = """1.
   1. Sub-item A
   2. Sub-item B
2. Second item
"""

converter = DocumentConverter(allowed_formats=[InputFormat.MD])
doc = converter.convert(DocumentStream(name="nested.md", stream=BytesIO(source.encode()))).document

print("Exported Markdown:")
print(repr(doc.export_to_markdown()))

print("\nTexts in document:")
for item in doc.texts:
    print(f"- label: {item.label.value}, marker: {repr(getattr(item, 'marker', None))}, text: {repr(item.text)}")
```

### Actual output

```text
Exported Markdown:
'1. Sub-item A\n2. Sub-item B\n1. Second item'

Texts in document:
- label: list_item, marker: '1.', text: 'Sub-item A'
- label: list_item, marker: '2.', text: 'Sub-item B'
- label: list_item, marker: '1.', text: 'Second item'
```

### Expected output

The outer item `1.` must be preserved as a list item containing the nested sub-list, and the subsequent item must retain its correct marker `2. Second item`.

### Cause

In `docling/backend/md_backend.py`, line 860:
```python
elif (
    isinstance(element, marko.block.ListItem)
    and len(element.children) > 0
    and isinstance((child := element.children[0]), marko.block.Paragraph)
    and len(child.children) > 0
):
```
The condition requires `element.children[0]` to be a `marko.block.Paragraph`. When a list item starts directly with a nested sub-list, Marko produces a `marko.block.List` node as `children[0]`. Because it is not a `Paragraph`, the condition evaluates to `False`. The backend falls through to `else`, completely skipping the creation of the parent `ListItem`.

### Impact

- **Structural data loss:** Parent outline items disappear from the document hierarchy and AST.
- **Corrupted numbering:** Downstream items are renumbered incorrectly in text exports, changing document semantics.
- **RAG & Chunking damage:** Hierarchical chunkers cannot associate sub-clauses with their parent numbered section.
- **Severity:** Medium (reproducible silent data loss in document structure).

### Docling version

- Docling: 2.149.0
- Docling Core: 2.106.0
- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.10

The function call `ProcessorInputs.get_mm_hashes()` (currently `vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:91-107` on `main`) emits ordinary content-addressed digests (computed when a caller omits `uuid`) and **caller-chosen `uuid` strings** (`part["uuid"]` / `multi_modal_uuids`) into the **same untagged string keyspace** (`mm_hash` / `identifier`). Because the two domains are not separated by a source tag or prefix, an unprivileged caller on the standard `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint can submit a request carrying a different media item of matching token count with `uuid` set to the predictable content digest `H` of a target media item, silently poisoning `MultiModalProcessorCache` and `EncoderCacheManager` for subsequent callers who **omit `uuid` entirely** (`docs/usage/security.md:676`). Even when the victim caller sets a secret per-tenant `cache_salt` as recommended in `docs/usage/security.md`, `cache_salt` only enters prefix-cache block hashes and does not prevent `MultiModalProcessorCache` or `EncoderCacheManager` from serving the aliased entry during prefill. Both caches (`MultiModalProcessorCache` and V1 `EncoderCacheManager`) are active in the default multimodal serving configuration, no opt-in flags are required. ## More Details & Potential Root Cause In `vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py` (`lines 91–107`): ```python if uuid_item is None or has_hash_factors: # NOTE: use provided hash string to hash with kwargs # if available for better performance. item = uuid_item if uuid_item is not None else item hashes.append( hasher.hash_kwargs( hash_algorithm, model_id=model_id, **{modality: item}, **hash_factors, ) ) else: # If there are no extra kwargs, use the client-provided UUID. hashes.append(uuid_item) ``` 1. **Ordinary content-addressed requests (`uuid_item is None`)**: `get_mm_hashes()` computes `H = hasher.hash_kwargs(hash_algorithm, model_id=model_id, **{modality: item}, **hash_factors)` (64-char hex `blake3` digest by default) and appends `H` with **no domain prefix**. 2. **Caller-chosen `uuid` requests (`uuid_item is not None`, default empty `hash_factors`)**: `get_mm_hashes()` executes `hashes.append(uuid_item)` **verbatim with no domain prefix** (note also that even when `has_hash_factors` is non-empty on one request and empty on another, `hasher.hash_kwargs(...)` likewise emits an unprefixed hex string into the same space). 3. **Shared downstream consumption**: The resulting string becomes both the `MultiModalProcessorCache` key (P0/P1) and `request.mm_features[i].identifier`, which indexes `EncoderCacheManager.cached` (`vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py:127`) and `("mm", identifier, offset)` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`. When an earlier request caches replacement media `M'` (with the same visual/audio token count as target media `M`) under `uuid = H(M)`, a subsequent ordinary request submitting `M` **without `uuid`** computes `mm_hash = H(M)` and hits the cached processor tensors and encoder embeddings of `M'`, silently steering generation to `M'`'s content. here is a brief Repro: ```python """Unit-level invariant check for untagged `mm_hash` domain collision in vLLM (`>= 0.27` / `main`): Verifies that `ProcessorInputs.get_mm_hashes()` (`vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py`) emits content-addressed digests (`uuid` omitted) and caller-chosen `uuid` values into the same untagged string keyspace on both the online bytes path (`MediaWithBytes`) and the in-process `PIL.Image` path. """ import io from PIL import Image from vllm.multimodal.media import MediaWithBytes from vllm.multimodal.parse import ImageProcessorItems, MultiModalDataItems from vllm.multimodal.processing.inputs import ProcessorInputs MODEL_ID = "Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct" def make_png_media(color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> MediaWithBytes[Image.Image]: img = Image.new("RGB", (224, 224), color) buf = io.BytesIO() img.save(buf, format="PNG") raw_bytes = buf.getvalue() decoded = Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_bytes)) return MediaWithBytes(decoded, raw_bytes) def main() -> None: media = make_png_media((240, 240, 255)) items = MultiModalDataItems({"image": ImageProcessorItems([media])}) # 1. Ordinary content-addressed request (`uuid` omitted, default `blake3` hasher) content_addressed = ProcessorInputs( prompt=[1], mm_data_items=items, mm_uuid_items=None, ) content_key = content_addressed.get_mm_hashes(MODEL_ID, "blake3")["image"][0] # 2. Request supplying a caller-chosen `uuid` (with default empty `hash_factors`) caller_uuid = ProcessorInputs( prompt=[1], mm_data_items=items, mm_uuid_items={"image": [content_key]}, ) uuid_key = caller_uuid.get_mm_hashes(MODEL_ID, "blake3")["image"][0] print(f"Content-addressed key (`uuid` omitted) : {content_key!r}") print(f"Caller-chosen `uuid` key : {uuid_key!r}") print(f"Untagged cross-domain collision : {content_key == uuid_key}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report and the unit-level repro — the cross-request aliasing you describe is serious. I'd like to take this on: I'll start by reproducing the collision with the repro in the issue, then look at separating the two identifier domains so a caller-chosen `uuid` can no longer alias a content-addressed digest.

issue.title: [Fix] Require control-plane auth on mesh HA management routes (fixes #45006)
issue.body:
## Summary

Mesh HA management routes (`/ha/*`) in `sgl-model-gateway` were protected only by the data-plane `auth_middleware` (Bearer == `--api-key`), which performs no role check. In a deployment with `--enable-mesh`, a data-plane API key, and control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`), any holder of the data-plane key could read cluster state/topology, write config entries that gossip to every peer, change the global rate limit, and trigger a graceful mesh leave — while the genuine control-plane Admin credential was rejected with 401 on the same routes.

This change wraps `mesh_routes` with the same `apply_control_plane_auth` already used for `admin_routes`/`worker_routes`: when control-plane RBAC is configured, only Admins can reach `/ha/*`; when it is not configured, the wiring falls back to the data-plane API key check, so behavior is unchanged.

Thank you @yyymk for the thorough report and the public disclosure — the reproduction steps and the control experiment made the intended fix direction clear.

Fixes #45006.

## Root cause

In `sgl-model-gateway/src/server.rs::build_app`, `admin_routes` and `worker_routes` go through `apply_control_plane_auth` (control-plane middleware when `--control-plane-api-keys`/JWT is configured, otherwise the data-plane fallback), but `mesh_routes` was attached only to `middleware::auth_middleware`, which checks the Bearer token against `--api-key` and does no role check.

## Change

```diff
-    // HA management routes
+    // HA management routes (control-plane authorization: Admin only when
+    // control-plane RBAC is configured, otherwise plain data-plane API key).
     let mesh_routes = Router::new()
         .route("/ha/status", get(get_cluster_status))
         ...
-        .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown))
-        .route_layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
-            auth_config.clone(),
-            middleware::auth_middleware,
-        ));
+        .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown));
+    let mesh_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(mesh_routes);
```

## Reproduction

Verified on current main (commit `4ec19ca`), built with Rust 1.90.0. Two mesh routers plus one mock worker, all on 127.0.0.1, following the issue's topology:

```bash
# mock worker on 127.0.0.1:39990 (see issue for mock_worker.py)
sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33800 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R1 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39530 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39531
# second router identical with --port 33801, --mesh-server-name R2, mesh :39531 -> peer 127.0.0.1:39530
```

Note: on current main, `/ha/config` values must be hex-encoded (hence `deadbeef`/`cafebabe` below); the 0.3.2 behavior in the issue accepted arbitrary strings.

### Before (unfixed binary)

```
=== [BEFORE] boundary (must be identical before/after) ===
POST /v1/completions user -> 200
GET /workers user -> 403
GET /workers admin -> 200
=== [BEFORE] /ha/* reads ===
GET /ha/status : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/health : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/workers : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/policies : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/rate-limit/stats : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
=== [BEFORE] /ha/* writes ===
POST /ha/rate-limit user -> 200
POST /ha/rate-limit admin -> 401
POST /ha/config user (hex value deadbeef) -> 200
POST /ha/config admin (hex value cafebabe) -> 401
```

The user-credential write persisted and was readable back on the same node:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config/authz_probe_BEFORE -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
{"key":"authz_probe_BEFORE","value":"deadbeef","format":"hex"}
```

And it gossiped to the peer — R2's mesh log shows R1's `NodeState.metadata` carrying the probe key (`deadbeef` = bytes `[222, 173, 190, 239]`):

```
smg_mesh::ping_server: ... Received Ping { state_sync: Some(StateSync { nodes: [
  NodeState { name: "R1", address: "127.0.0.1:39530", status: Alive, version: 4,
    metadata: {"global_rate_limit": [...], "authz_probe_BEFORE": [222, 173, 190, 239]} },
  ... ] }) }
```

### After (this PR)

```
=== [AFTER] boundary (must be identical before/after) ===
POST /v1/completions user -> 200
GET /workers user -> 403
GET /workers admin -> 200
=== [AFTER] /ha/* reads ===
GET /ha/status : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/health : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/workers : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/policies : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/rate-limit/stats : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
=== [AFTER] /ha/* writes ===
POST /ha/rate-limit user -> 403
POST /ha/rate-limit admin -> 200
POST /ha/config user (hex value deadbeef) -> 403
POST /ha/config admin (hex value cafebabe) -> 200
```

Admin round-trips still work end to end:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config/authz_probe_admin_AFTER -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
{"key":"authz_probe_admin_AFTER","value":"cafebabe","format":"hex"}
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
{"limit_per_second":9}
```

## Regression checks

- **Mesh peering intact** (gossip runs over the smg-mesh TCP protocol on the mesh port, never through the `/ha/*` HTTP routes; no in-repo HTTP caller of `/ha/*` exists). With the fix, both nodes see the full cluster:
  ```
  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/status -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
  {"node_name":"R1","node_count":2,"nodes":[{"name":"R1","address":"127.0.0.1:39530",...},
   {"name":"R2","address":"127.0.0.1:39531",...}],"stores":{"membership_count":2,...}}
  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
  {"status":"healthy","node_name":"R1","cluster_size":2,"stores_healthy":true}
  ```
- **Public health probes untouched** (`/liveness`, `/readiness`, `/health`, `/health_generate` are in `public_routes`): `GET /liveness` and `GET /health` return 200 with no credentials, before and after.
- **Inference path untouched**: `POST /v1/completions` with the data-plane key returns 200, before and after. (`/ha/health` is a mesh-topology management view, not the liveness probe.)
- **No control-plane RBAC configured**: `apply_control_plane_auth` falls back to the plain data-plane `auth_middleware`, so deployments without `--control-plane-api-keys`/JWT see no behavior change.

## Tests

- `cargo test --test security_tests` (sgl-model-gateway): **47 passed, 1 failed**. The single failure is `common::redis_test_server::tests::test_redis_server_start_stop`, which spawns an external `redis-server` binary that is not installed in this environment — unrelated to this change.
- Live two-router mesh verification matrix above (before/after), covering reads, state-changing writes, gossip propagation, admin round-trips, public probes, and peer connectivity.

issue.title: [Bug] Qwen3-MoE: a router stored quantized (compressed-tensors) is never loaded, and the server answers garbage without an error
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` builds the MoE router (`mlp.gate`) with the quantization config only when the format is ModelSlim, and with `quant_config=None` otherwise ([qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284)). A compressed-tensors checkpoint can store the router quantized too. `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` (38,425 downloads in the last 30 days) lists only `lm_head` in `ignore` and stores every layer's router as `mlp.gate.weight_packed`, `weight_scale` and `weight_shape`. SGLang builds an unquantized `ReplicatedLinear` whose only parameter is `weight`, so none of the stored names has a parameter, and `load_weights` skips them without a message ([qwen3_moe.py#L1246-L1247](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L1246-L1247); the warning for a name with no parameter, [#L1256](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L1256), is never reached because of that `continue`). The router weight is never written: loading layer 0's real tensors through SGLang's own load and post-load step, the router outputs NaN for all 128 experts, where the reference computed from the checkpoint's tensors reaches 9.5, while `self_attn.o_proj` of the same checkpoint (W4A16) matches the reference to a relative error of 0.002.

The server starts with default flags and raises no error. On one H20 with SGLang v0.5.23 (main `4003bf1` has the same code), every prompt is answered with backslashes or line breaks (`\\\\\\\\...`, `\r\n\r\n\r\n...`). GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy):

| | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| SGLang v0.5.23 | 0.0% (every answer invalid) |
| SGLang v0.5.23, router built with the quantization config | 85.7% |
| vLLM 0.33.0 (builds the Qwen3-MoE router with the quantization config) | 85.4% |

The change for the second row is one condition: pass `quant_config` to the router for `compressed_tensors` as well, so the checkpoint's `ignore` list decides per layer. Other compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints keep the router in BF16 and list it in `ignore`, so they are unaffected: of the eight below, only RedHatAI's stores the router quantized, and it is the only one whose config asks for a quantized router. On the most downloaded of them, `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (503,059 downloads), GSM8K is 89.0% as released and 90.1% with the change, and two release runs differ in their served answers as often as a release run and a run with the change do.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16 --port 30000
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "The capital of France is", "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}'
```

`repro.py` reads only `config.json` and the safetensors index of eight compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints, prints which router tensors each stores, and asks SGLang's compressed-tensors config what it would build for `model.layers.0.mlp.gate` if the router were given the config.

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Which compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints store the MoE router (mlp.gate) quantized, and what SGLang's
# compressed-tensors config would decide for it if Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock passed the config to the router. Reads
# config.json and model.safetensors.index.json only; no GPU.
import json

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import CompressedTensorsConfig
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.utils import should_ignore_layer
from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_moe import Qwen3MoeForCausalLM

REPOS = ["RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16", "cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit",
         "cyankiwi/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ-4bit", "stelterlab/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ",
         "stelterlab/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ", "dark-side-of-the-code/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ",
         "YuYu1015/Huihui-Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-abliterated-NVFP4", "null-space/Qwen3-235B-A22B-abliterated-FP8"]
for repo in REPOS:
    q = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "config.json")))["quantization_config"]
    q["packed_modules_mapping"] = dict(getattr(Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, "packed_modules_mapping", {}))
    cfg = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config(q)
    w = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "model.safetensors.index.json")))["weight_map"]
    stored = sorted({k.rsplit(".", 1)[1] for k in w if k.startswith("model.layers.0.mlp.gate.")})
    ignored = should_ignore_layer("model.layers.0.mlp.gate", ignore=cfg.ignore, fused_mapping=cfg.packed_modules_mapping)
    print(f"{repo:62s} stored router: {','.join(stored):35s} config says: {'BF16 (ignored)' if ignored else 'QUANTIZED'}")
```

</details>

Output on SGLang v0.5.23:

```
RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16           stored router: weight_packed,weight_scale,weight_shape config says: QUANTIZED
cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit                 stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
cyankiwi/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ-4bit                  stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
stelterlab/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ                     stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
stelterlab/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ                    stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
dark-side-of-the-code/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ         stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
YuYu1015/Huihui-Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-abliterated-NVFP4  stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
null-space/Qwen3-235B-A22B-abliterated-FP8                     stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
```

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 (served runs), main `4003bf1` (code links); vLLM 0.33.0 (comparison)

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report, @HollowMan6 — and for putting up #49187 so quickly. Your fix covers exactly what I had in mind (passing the compressed-tensors config to the router so the checkpoint's `ignore` list decides per layer), and it comes with the H20 GSM8K numbers, so I'll step aside here rather than open a duplicate PR. Happy to help review #49187 if that's useful.

issue.title: [Bug] #48399 drops SM120/SM121 from the DSV4.1 DeepGEMM indexer gates — 8x prefill regression on GB10 (torch fallback calls tolist() per layer)
issue.body:
# #48399 drops SM120/SM121 from the DSV4.1 DeepGEMM indexer — 8x prefill regression on GB10


## Summary

#48399 replaced `is_sm100_or_newer()` (device capability major >= 10) with
strict `current_arch().is_sm(10)` in `srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/
__init__.py`. SM120-family devices (GB10, compute capability 12.1) now fall
to `_torch_prefill`, whose `scoring.prefill_requests` calls `Tensor.tolist()`
once per layer — a synchronous D2H inside the layer loop. Measured on a
4x DGX Spark TP4 deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: **~125 ms/layer fixed
cost, 8x prefill throughput regression** (4096-token chunks: ~480 tok/s vs
~4000 tok/s before), independent of chunk size.

## Evidence

1. **Torch profiler trace** (TP-0, 18.4 s window, one 120k-token prefill):
   `cudaMemcpyAsync` 9.86 s (n=3117) under `aten::to/_to_copy`, host stack
   `full_topk.py::_torch_prefill -> scoring.py:400 prefill_requests ->
   Tensor.tolist()`. GPU kernels in the window total ~14 s — the time is
   host-side sync.
2. **The SM121 DeepGEMM path is healthy**: our fleet ran it in production for
   weeks on pins up to 8817f63c (paired qeval BROKE=0 across six adoption
   windows; decode 44-77 tok/s). Dual-container microbench on identical
   GB10 hardware: `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` NEW (0.2.6) vs LEGACY (0.2.3
   semantics) = 18.96 vs 18.90 ms at indexer scale — no kernel regression.
3. **Reproduction**: revert the one-line gate to `is_sm(10) or is_sm(12)` on
   any SM120-family GPU — prefill recovers.

## The dtype subtlety (why a naive revert crashes)

deep-gemm 0.2.6 asserts `weights.scalar_type() == (arch_major == 10 ?
torch::kBFloat16 : torch::kFloat32)` (attention.hpp:50). The dtype gates in
`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/index_logits.py` legitimately stayed strict
`is_sm(10)` after #48399 — so on SM121 the DeepGEMM path must run with the
**fp32** logits/weights contract. Restoring the PATH gate while keeping the
dtype gates strict works on GB10 (verified in production). If the intent of
#48399 was "SM120 keeps the torch indexer", note the per-layer `tolist()`
makes that fallback pathological for prefill — at minimum the torch path
should batch the D2H, and the arch dispatch deserves an explicit SM120
decision rather than the current silent demotion.

## Suggested fix (either)

- Restore `>= 10` (include SM120) for the path gates, keep dtype gates strict
  (fp32 contract outside arch 10), or
- Keep strict SM100 gating but fix `_torch_prefill`'s per-layer `tolist()`.

comment.body:
Thanks again for the detailed report — the fix is up in #49182.

What it does: restores the `>= 10` gate for the **dense** DeepGEMM paths only (`_use_deep_gemm_prefill` and `use_deep_gemm_decode`), so SM120/SM121 take the DeepGEMM prefill/decode path again instead of the torch fallback. I verified against the pinned sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.6 sources that the dense `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` / `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` kernels dispatch arch 12 with the fp32 weights/logits contract.

Deliberately unchanged: the dtype gates in `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/index_logits.py` stay strict SM100 (fp32 off SM100, per deep-gemm's assert), and the candidate/sparse-table gate stays strict SM100 too — deep-gemm's sparse mqa-logits kernels assert arch == 10, so widening that gate would only turn the dense-blocks fallback into a startup error on SM120.

The PR includes a CPU-runnable gate reproducer (verbatim before/after outputs in the description) and a new CPU unit test covering the gates on SM90/SM100/SM120/SM121/non-CUDA. One honest caveat, also stated in the PR: I had no SM120 hardware available, so end-to-end verification on GB10 is still needed — your production verification that reverting the gate recovers prefill is cited there.

issue.title: [Bugfix] Inherit target --revision/--code-revision for MTP draft; readable error for n_predict=0
issue.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61197: with `method="mtp"` and no explicit draft model, the draft is the target checkpoint itself, but the draft `ModelConfig` was built with the speculative config's own (unset) `revision`/`code_revision`, so config and weights resolved from the repo's default branch instead of the target's `--revision`. This PR inherits both from `target_model_config` (unless explicitly overridden), mirroring the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance. It also replaces a `ZeroDivisionError` with a readable `ValueError` when a draft checkpoint resolves to `n_predict=0`.

## Claims

- MTP draft config/weights now resolve from the target's `--revision`/`--code-revision` instead of the default branch (regression vs 0.29).
- Explicitly set speculative `revision`/`code_revision` still take precedence over the inherited values.
- Other speculative methods (e.g. `dspark`, separate `draft_model` checkpoints) are unaffected.
- A draft checkpoint with `n_predict=0` (missing `num_nextn_predict_layers`) now raises a readable `ValueError` instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

## Validation

Unit tests (mocked, no HF downloads / no GPU), from a fresh `main` checkout (`32b05ad`):

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py -q
# 21 passed (17 pre-existing + 4 new regression tests)
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_bailing_mtp_config.py -q
# 2 passed
ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py
# All checks passed
```

New regression tests (in `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`):
- `test_mtp_draft_inherits_target_revision`
- `test_mtp_draft_explicit_revision_wins`
- `test_explicit_draft_model_does_not_inherit_revision`
- `test_mtp_zero_n_predict_raises_readable_error`

A standalone reproducer confirmed the bug before the fix (draft got `revision=None` despite target `revision="pre-final"`, and `ZeroDivisionError` for `n_predict=0`) and the fixed behavior after.

Note on environment: this sandbox is CPU-only with no HF Hub access, so every test in this file also reports a teardown error from `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` in `tests/conftest.py` — this happens identically on the unmodified tree (17 passed / 17 teardown errors before my change), and HF-download-dependent tests elsewhere (e.g. `tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py`) fail for the same environmental reasons. Model evaluation is not applicable: this is a config-time-only change that does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior.

## Details

**Root cause:** in `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`, the `method == "mtp"` branch sets `self.model` from `target_model_config.model_weights or .model` and inherits `quantization`, but leaves `self.revision`/`self.code_revision` as `None`. The draft `ModelConfig(...)` built later passes `revision=self.revision` / `code_revision=self.code_revision`, so the draft resolved config and weights from the default branch rather than the target's pinned revision.

**Design decision:** inheritance is placed next to the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance and guarded by `is None` checks, so explicit values remain overrides. It intentionally applies only when no explicit draft model is given (i.e. the draft *is* the target checkpoint); a separately provided draft checkpoint is a different repo and keeps its own revision. The `n_predict == 0` guard sits at the top of the existing `elif n_predict is not None:` branch, so `dspark` (separate branch) and valid `n_predict > 0` behavior are unchanged.

issue.title: [Bugfix] Secure /scale_elastic_ep: API-key auth, bool rejection, 400 when elastic EP disabled
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #59088.

The `/scale_elastic_ep` endpoint had three bugs:

1. **API-key authentication bypass.** `AuthenticationMiddleware` only guards the `("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere")` path prefixes, while the elastic EP router is mounted at the server root — so the middleware never checked this endpoint. `/scale_elastic_ep` is state-changing: while a scale is in progress, `ScalingMiddleware` returns 503 for every request. Anyone with network access could trigger it without a key. This PR adds `/scale_elastic_ep` to `GUARDED_PREFIX`. The read-only `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` stays unguarded, analogous to `/health`.

2. **Boolean parameters accepted as counts.** `isinstance(True, int)` is `True`, so `{"new_data_parallel_size": true}` returned `200 "Scaled to True data parallel engines"`. Both `new_data_parallel_size` and `drain_timeout` now go through a `_require_positive_int` helper that explicitly rejects bools (keeping the same "must be a positive integer" 400 messages as before).

3. **500 for permanently impossible scaling.** On a server started without `--enable-elastic-ep`, the request fails deep in the engine (`AssertionError` from the `data_parallel_backend == "ray"` assert) and surfaces as a bare `500 "Scale failed"` with an empty log message. The handler now checks `parallel_config.enable_elastic_ep` up front and returns `400` with an actionable message ("Restart the server with --enable-elastic-ep to use /scale_elastic_ep"). 400 was chosen over 501 because the endpoint exists and is implemented — the request is invalid for this server's configuration — consistent with the handler's existing `ValueError` → 400 mapping (e.g. exceeding `--elastic-ep-max-dp-size`). The catch-all handler now uses `logger.exception`, so the server log carries the real traceback.

## Duplicate check

No existing PR addresses this: the issue timeline shows no cross-referenced PRs, and a search for open PRs mentioning `59088` in vllm-project/vllm returned none. This is not low-value busywork — it closes an authentication bypass on a state-changing serving endpoint plus two correctness issues in its validation.

## Test results

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/test_api_router.py` (5 tests):

- `test_rejects_boolean_data_parallel_size` / `test_rejects_boolean_drain_timeout` — boolean inputs are rejected with 400 (both fail on the unfixed code).
- `test_rejects_non_positive_and_non_integer` — 0, negatives, floats, and strings still rejected.
- `test_returns_400_when_elastic_ep_disabled` — disabled elastic EP yields 400 with the actionable message instead of 500 (fails on the unfixed code).
- `test_valid_request_still_scales` — valid integer input with elastic EP enabled still returns 200.

Commands run (repo `.venv`, Python 3.12, CPU-only):

- `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/test_api_router.py` → **5 passed**
- `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_authentication_middleware.py` → **20 passed**. This suite auto-discovers routes per supported task and asserts guarded routes require auth; for the `generate` task it now covers `/scale_elastic_ep` (401 without a token) and confirms `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` stays public.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all four touched/added files → clean

A TestClient-level repro (mocked engine client) additionally confirmed the before/after matrix: no-key request went from reaching the handler to `401`; boolean input from `200 "Scaled to True data parallel engines"` to `400`; disabled elastic EP from `500 "Scale failed"` to `400` with the actionable message; `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` remains reachable without a key.

## Model evaluation

No model evaluation needed: this change touches only the HTTP serving layer (auth gating, request validation, error codes). It does not alter model execution, token generation, accuracy, or serving performance.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during investigation and implementation. The final diff was reviewed line by line, and the executed test results are listed above.

issue.title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: route unquantized BF16/F16/F32 checkpoints off the MXFP4 expert path

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810.

A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no `quantization_config`. In `ModelConfig`, `is_fp4_experts` is initialized from the `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` env var (default `True`) and is only overridden when `try_detect_fp4_experts()` returns a non-`None` value. That detector returned `None` for any dtype other than the mxfp4-packed (`U8`/`I8`/`F4`) or FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3`) layouts — including unquantized `BF16`/`F16`/`F32`. As a result, an unquantized DSV4 checkpoint kept `is_fp4_experts=True` under default settings and the auto MoE-runner backend routed it to the `flashinfer_mxfp4` path, while the rest of the stack treated it as unquantized, crashing the first request with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py`: `try_detect_fp4_experts()` now returns `False` for unquantized routed-expert dtypes (`BF16`/`F16`/`F32`), so unquantized checkpoints take the unquantized expert path instead of falling back to the FP4-experts env default. Genuine MXFP4 (`U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`) and FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3` → `False`) detection is unchanged; unknown or unreadable headers still return `None` and fall back to the user/env default.
- `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`: new unit tests covering `BF16`/`F16`/`F32` → `False`, `U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`, `F8_E4M3` → `False`, and `None` for unreadable/empty checkpoint dirs.

## Reproducer (no GPU required)

A full GPU repro is infeasible here (needs 8x B300 plus a DSV4 BF16 checkpoint), so the bug is demonstrated at the config-routing layer where it lives. Save the script below as `repro_44810.py` in the repo root and run `python3 repro_44810.py`. It builds fake checkpoint dirs (a single safetensors shard whose header declares one routed-expert weight tensor of the given dtype) and drives the real `try_detect_fp4_experts()` plus the real `probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype()` (AST-extracted from the repo; the only stubs are `transformers`/`QuantizationConfig` class-level deps and `find_local_repo_dir`, which is unreachable for local dirs), then applies the same `None`-vs-env-default logic `ModelConfig` uses.

```python
import ast, json, os, re, struct, sys, tempfile, types
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

weight_utils_src = open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py").read()
tree = ast.parse(weight_utils_src)

def _wanted(n):
    if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
        return any(getattr(t, "id", "") == "_ROUTED_EXPERT_KEY_RE" for t in n.targets)
    return getattr(n, "name", None) == "probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype"

seg = [n for n in tree.body if _wanted(n)]
wmod = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils")
wmod.__dict__.update({"re": re, "json": json, "struct": struct, "os": os,
                      "Path": Path, "Optional": Optional,
                      "logging": __import__("logging")})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=seg, type_ignores=[]), "<wu>", "exec"), wmod.__dict__)

def make_pkg(name):
    m = types.ModuleType(name); m.__path__ = []; sys.modules[name] = m; return m

for pkg in ["sglang", "sglang.srt", "sglang.srt.configs",
            "sglang.srt.model_loader", "sglang.srt.utils"]:
    make_pkg(pkg)
sys.modules["sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils"] = wmod
sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils"].find_local_repo_dir = lambda *a, **k: None

dv4_tree = ast.parse(open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py").read())
fn_node = next(n for n in dv4_tree.body
               if getattr(n, "name", None) == "try_detect_fp4_experts")
dv4 = types.SimpleNamespace()
dv4.__dict__.update({"os": os, "logging": __import__("logging"), "Optional": Optional})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[fn_node], type_ignores=[]), "<dv4>", "exec"), dv4.__dict__)

KEY = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.w1.weight"

def make_ckpt(dtype_str):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    header = json.dumps({KEY: {"dtype": dtype_str, "shape": [2048, 4096]}}).encode()
    with open(os.path.join(d, "model.safetensors"), "wb") as f:
        f.write(struct.pack("<Q", len(header))); f.write(header)
    return d

for dtype in ["BF16", "F16", "F32", "U8", "I8", "F4", "F8_E4M3"]:
    detected = dv4.try_detect_fp4_experts(make_ckpt(dtype))
    is_fp4_experts = detected if detected is not None else True  # env default
    print(f"safetensors dtype={dtype:8s} -> try_detect_fp4_experts()={detected!s:5s}"
          f"  is_fp4_experts={is_fp4_experts}")
```

**Before** (also logs `Unexpected routed-expert safetensors dtype=BF16 for DeepSeek V4` to stderr):

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

**After**:

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

## Accuracy Tests

This change only affects config-time routing for DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints without an explicit `quantization_config`; no kernel or forward-path code is touched. The new unit tests assert the detection matrix above (the full sglang import chain is GPU/heavy-dep bound in this environment, so the test logic was additionally validated by executing the real extracted functions against fake checkpoint shards — all 9 cases pass). Please let CI run the new `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — config-time detection only; no inference-path changes.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

(Not applicable — config routing only; see note above.)

issue.title: [Bug] Model gateway silently drops `cache_salt` on chat completions
issue.body:
## Describe the bug

When sending a `/v1/chat/completions` request through `sgl-model-gateway`, the top-level `cache_salt` field is silently dropped before forwarding to the worker.

The SGLang Python backend supports this field, so the same request behaves differently when sent directly to the worker versus through the gateway. Requests intended to use separate cache namespaces can consequently reuse the default namespace.

## Reproduction

Send a request through the gateway:

    curl http://localhost:8889/v1/chat/completions \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{
        "model": "<served-model>",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
        "max_tokens": 1,
        "cache_salt": "tenant-a"
      }'

Inspect the JSON forwarded to the worker, for example using a mock HTTP backend. The forwarded request no longer contains `cache_salt`.

We also reproduced this without a model: deserializing the payload into the unmodified `openai-protocol 1.0.0` `ChatCompletionRequest`, normalizing it, and serializing it again removes `cache_salt`.

## Expected behavior

The gateway should preserve `cache_salt` and forward it unchanged to the worker.

## Suspected cause and suggested fix

The gateway currently pins [`openai-protocol = 1.0.0`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml). Its Chat request type does not preserve unknown extension fields.

Newer protocol versions already provide a flattened extension map in [`ChatCompletionRequest`](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/blob/main/crates/protocols/src/chat.rs). Please consider upgrading to a compatible version and adding a regression check for `cache_salt` forwarding.

## Related work

PR #21571 reported the same extension-field loss, explicitly including `cache_salt`, and proposed a request wrapper. It targeted `sglang-miles` and was closed without merging. This issue requests a fix for the gateway on `main`, preferably by updating the protocol dependency.

comment.body:
Thanks again for the clear report and the pointer to the newer protocol version, @shuoerw.

I opened a fix for this: #48845. Instead of upgrading the pinned `openai-protocol` dependency, it preserves the unknown top-level fields (like `cache_salt`) in the gateway itself and merges them back into the body forwarded to the worker, with a regression test that sends your payload through the gateway to a mock worker and asserts on the exact JSON forwarded. The PR description explains the approach and the trade-off — happy to switch to the dependency upgrade if you or the maintainers prefer that direction.

issue.title: [Fix] nixl: release transfer worker when room is aborted mid-wait
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44369.

In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, aborting a request after its KV
transfer handles were submitted did not bound the prefill transfer worker's
wait when a handle stayed healthy but non-terminal (`PROC`):
`NixlKVManager._await_handles()` only arms its settle deadline after an `ERR`
is observed, so with every handle `PROC` the deadline stays `None` and the
wait is unbounded. The abort notification marks the room `Failed` and
registers the deferred ACK target, but it neither wakes a worker already
inside `_await_handles()` nor drains the room's `_staging_outstanding`
count — so the deferred abort ACK never fires and the worker thread never
returns to its queue. With the default `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=4`,
four such aborted rooms can exhaust all prefill transfer workers.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`
  - `_await_handles()` now accepts an optional `room` and returns
    `(settled, any_failed, aborted)`. When the room is marked `Failed` while
    polling (e.g. a decode-side abort notification landed after the batch
    was submitted), the wait ends immediately with `aborted=True` instead of
    spinning forever on healthy non-terminal handles. The exception-path
    call site passes no room, so its already-bounded (`failure_seen=True`)
    behavior is unchanged.
  - `transfer_worker()` handles the aborted wait: it releases the chunk's
    staging count (guarded by the existing `staging_counted` flag, mirroring
    the failure path) and fires the deferred abort ACK via
    `_maybe_ack_drained_abort()`, then continues with the next chunk. The
    room stays `Failed`, exactly as the abort notification left it.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`
  - Two new regression tests (see below); one existing mock updated for the
    new 3-tuple return.

Design note: the ACK fires once the worker's accounting drains, matching the
deferred-ACK protocol's intent ("send the deferred ack once an aborted
room's chunks have drained"). The decode side keeps its release timeout as a
backstop, as before.

## Reproducer

Deterministic and GPU-free: a fake NIXL agent whose handle stays `PROC`,
driving the real `_handle_abort_notification()` and (Phase B) the real
`transfer_worker()`. Save as `repro_44369.py` and run with
`PYTHONPATH=python python repro_44369.py` from a checkout.

<details>
<summary>repro_44369.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproducer for sgl-project/sglang issue #44369 (GPU-free, no RDMA)."""
import inspect
from collections import defaultdict
from threading import Event, Thread
from time import sleep, time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import numpy as np

from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base.conn import KVPoll
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.conn import AbortNotification
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.utils import TransferKVChunk
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.nixl.conn import NixlKVManager

ROOM = 90210
HANDLE = object()


class FakeAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = "PROC"
        self.reads = 0

    def check_xfer_state(self, handle):
        self.reads += 1
        return self.state


def make_manager(agent):
    manager = NixlKVManager.__new__(NixlKVManager)
    manager.agent = agent
    manager.request_status = {ROOM: KVPoll.WaitingForInput}
    manager.req_to_decode_prefix_len = {}
    manager.transfer_infos = {}
    manager.exceptions = {}
    manager._staging_outstanding = defaultdict(int)
    manager._deferred_ack_targets = {}
    manager._deferred_ack_poisoned_rooms = set()
    manager.enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = True
    manager.enable_staging = False
    manager._staging_ctx = None
    manager.sent_acks = []
    manager.update_status = lambda room, status: manager.request_status.__setitem__(
        room, status
    )
    manager.record_failure = lambda room, reason: None
    manager._send_abort_ack = lambda room, target: manager.sent_acks.append(
        (room, target)
    )
    manager._reload_invalidated_peers = lambda infos: None
    return manager


def abort_message():
    return AbortNotification(
        room=ROOM, decode_ip="127.0.0.1", decode_port=54321, generation=7
    ).to_zmq()


def await_kwargs(manager):
    if "room" in inspect.signature(manager._await_handles).parameters:
        return {"room": ROOM}
    return {}


def wait_until_polling(agent):
    deadline = time() + 10
    while agent.reads == 0 and time() < deadline:
        sleep(0.001)
    assert agent.reads > 0


def phase_a():
    print("=== Phase A: direct _await_handles vs abort ===")
    agent = FakeAgent()
    manager = make_manager(agent)
    manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM] = 1
    entered, returned = Event(), Event()
    result = {}

    def wait_for_handle():
        entered.set()
        result["value"] = manager._await_handles(
            [HANDLE], failure_seen=False, **await_kwargs(manager)
        )
        returned.set()

    thread = Thread(target=wait_for_handle, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    assert entered.wait(5)
    wait_until_polling(agent)
    reads_before_abort = agent.reads
    assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message())
    assert manager.request_status[ROOM] == KVPoll.Failed
    woke = returned.wait(2.0)
    sleep(0.1)
    print(
        {

            "waiter_alive_after_abort": thread.is_alive(),
            "return_value": result.get("value"),

            "reads_after_abort": agent.reads,
        }
    )
    agent.state = "DONE"
    returned.wait(3)
    thread.join(2)


def phase_b():
    print("=== Phase B: transfer_worker vs abort (accounting + ACK) ===")
    agent = FakeAgent()
    manager = make_manager(agent)
    manager.is_mla_backend = False
    manager.is_hybrid_mla_backend = False
    manager.attn_tp_size = 1
    manager.transfer_source_rank = 0
    manager.kv_args = SimpleNamespace(kv_data_ptrs=[0x1000])
    manager.decode_kv_args_table = {
        "agent0": SimpleNamespace(
            decode_tp_size=1,
            requires_dcp_relayout=False,
            kv_xfer_segments=None,
            dst_homogeneous_mem_kind="VRAM",
            dst_kv_ptrs=[0x2000],
            gpu_id=0,
        )
    }
    manager.transfer_infos = {
        ROOM: {
            "req0": SimpleNamespace(
                room=ROOM,
                is_dummy=False,
                agent_name="agent0",
                dst_kv_indices=np.array([0], dtype=np.int64),
                dst_aux_index=np.array([0], dtype=np.int64),
                decode_prefix_len=0,
            )
        }
    }
    manager.send_kvcache = lambda *a, **k: HANDLE
    chunk = TransferKVChunk(
        room=ROOM,
        prefill_kv_indices=np.array([1], dtype=np.int32),
        index_slice=slice(0, 1),
        is_last_chunk=False,
        chunk_id=0,
        prefill_aux_index=None,
        state_indices=None,
    )
    state = {"n": 0}

    def fake_get():
        state["n"] += 1
        if state["n"] == 1:
            return chunk
        raise KeyboardInterrupt()

    worker_done = Event()

    def run_worker():
        try:
            manager.transfer_worker(SimpleNamespace(get=fake_get))
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            worker_done.set()

    t = Thread(target=run_worker, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    wait_until_polling(agent)
    assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message())
    finished = worker_done.wait(5.0)
    sleep(0.1)
    print(
        {
            "worker_finished_within_5s_after_abort": finished,
            "outstanding_after_abort": manager._staging_outstanding.get(ROOM, 0),
            "abort_ack_sent_after_abort": bool(manager.sent_acks),
            "acks": [(r, str(tgt)) for r, tgt in manager.sent_acks],
            "room_status": str(manager.request_status.get(ROOM)),
        }
    )
    agent.state = "DONE"
    worker_done.wait(3)
    t.join(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    phase_a()
    phase_b()
```

issue.title: [Bug] Model gateway silently drops `cache_salt` on chat completions
issue.body:
## Describe the bug

When sending a `/v1/chat/completions` request through `sgl-model-gateway`, the top-level `cache_salt` field is silently dropped before forwarding to the worker.

The SGLang Python backend supports this field, so the same request behaves differently when sent directly to the worker versus through the gateway. Requests intended to use separate cache namespaces can consequently reuse the default namespace.

## Reproduction

Send a request through the gateway:

    curl http://localhost:8889/v1/chat/completions \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{
        "model": "<served-model>",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
        "max_tokens": 1,
        "cache_salt": "tenant-a"
      }'

Inspect the JSON forwarded to the worker, for example using a mock HTTP backend. The forwarded request no longer contains `cache_salt`.

We also reproduced this without a model: deserializing the payload into the unmodified `openai-protocol 1.0.0` `ChatCompletionRequest`, normalizing it, and serializing it again removes `cache_salt`.

## Expected behavior

The gateway should preserve `cache_salt` and forward it unchanged to the worker.

## Suspected cause and suggested fix

The gateway currently pins [`openai-protocol = 1.0.0`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.toml). Its Chat request type does not preserve unknown extension fields.

Newer protocol versions already provide a flattened extension map in [`ChatCompletionRequest`](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/blob/main/crates/protocols/src/chat.rs). Please consider upgrading to a compatible version and adding a regression check for `cache_salt` forwarding.

## Related work

PR #21571 reported the same extension-field loss, explicitly including `cache_salt`, and proposed a request wrapper. It targeted `sglang-miles` and was closed without merging. This issue requests a fix for the gateway on `main`, preferably by updating the protocol dependency.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and the clear reproduction, @shuoerw — the pointer to the newer protocol version's flattened extension map is very helpful.

I'd like to work on this: I'll look into upgrading the gateway's `openai-protocol` dependency so `cache_salt` (and other engine extension fields) are preserved on chat completions, and add a regression check for `cache_salt` forwarding. Please let me know if you have any concerns or a preferred direction.

issue.title: fix(standard-pdf): share model-thread pool across pipeline instances

labels.name: repo-ff9d01dd
labels.description: AI triage found no CI-safety concern (advisory)
