issue.title: PY-15: ODT paragraphs styled with `style:list-style-name` (without `<text:list>`) are flattened to plain `TEXT`
issue.body:
**Type:** Bug / Structural List Loss (ODT backend parity with `msword_backend.py`)  
**Component:** `docling/backend/opendocument_backend.py` (module-level `_add_odf_paragraph` l.720–780, `_odf_paragraph_style_names` l.696–717; line numbers from the local checkout, `pyproject.toml` = 2.141.0, may differ in 2.140.0)  
**Companion:** Rust [`rs-45-odt-paragraph-style-list-name-lost`](https://github.com/docling-project/docling.rs/issues/826).  

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| `docling` | `2.140.0` (`docling-core 2.101.1`) |
| Test files | `repro/min_style_list_name.odt` and `repro/min_style_list_name.docx` (100% synthetic pair generated by `repro/make_repro.py`) |
| Corpus evidence | **424 / 632 ODT documents (67.1%)** contain **26,627 `<text:p>` list paragraphs** styled via `style:list-style-name` on `<style:style style:family="paragraph">`, all of which are flattened to `DocItemLabel.TEXT` instead of `DocItemLabel.LIST_ITEM`. |

---

## 1. Description of the Bug

Per ODF 1.2 (`style:list-style-name`), a paragraph `<text:p>` whose resolved paragraph style (`<style:style style:family="paragraph">`, directly or via `style:parent-style-name`) carries `style:list-style-name` pointing to a `<text:list-style>` is treated by LibreOffice as a list item even when not enclosed in a `<text:list>` container (spec section number not verified).

In `docling/backend/opendocument_backend.py`, `_add_odf_child` only calls `_add_odf_list` for `isinstance(element, OdfList)` (`<text:list>`). Standalone `<text:p>` elements go to `_add_odf_paragraph`, which only inspects the paragraph style names (via `_odf_paragraph_style_names`) for `Title` / `Subtitle`, never checks `style:list-style-name` on the paragraph style chain, and otherwise emits `DocItemLabel.TEXT`.

---

## 2. Minimal Reproducer & Output (`output/docling-python-2.140.0/`)

| Metric | `min_style_list_name.docx` | `min_style_list_name.odt` |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| `list_item` count | **5** (3 bullets + 2 enumerated) | **0** |
| `text` count | **1** (`"Requirements checklist:"`) | **6** (all 5 list items flattened to `text`) |

---

## 3. Suggested Fix in `docling/backend/opendocument_backend.py`

1. Add a module-level helper `_resolve_paragraph_list_style(odf_obj, style_name) -> str | None` that walks `style:parent-style-name` via `odf_obj.get_style("paragraph", name)` (the style lookup already used by `_odf_paragraph_style_names`) and returns the first non-empty `style:list-style-name`.
2. In `_add_odf_paragraph`, if the helper returns a valid `<text:list-style>` name, emit the paragraph as a list item (`doc.add_list_item(...)` inside a list group from `doc.add_list_group(...)`) using level 1 of that `<text:list-style>` (see `_odf_list_level_style`).


[python-15-odt-paragraph-style-list-name-lost.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33788662/python-15-odt-paragraph-style-list-name-lost.zip)

comment.body:
Thanks again for the thorough report and the synthetic repro pair — they made this straightforward to verify.

The fix is up in #4959: `_add_odf_paragraph` now resolves `style:list-style-name` through the full `style:parent-style-name` chain and emits such paragraphs as level-1 list items (grouped per list style, with numbering continuing across consecutive items), instead of flattening them to `TEXT`. On your `min_style_list_name.odt` the output goes from 6 `text` items to 1 `text` + 5 `list_item` — 3 bullets in one group and 2 numbered items (`1.`, `2.`) in another, matching the DOCX output in the issue.

5 new regression tests are included; the full ODT backend suite (67 tests) passes with no fixture ground-truth changes.

issue.title: Bug: `Element.click` reports the mouse-release error and hides the press failure when both fail
issue.body:
### Browser Use Version

0.13.11 (`c75e8476`). `browser_use/actor/element.py` is unchanged on current main (0.13.13, `aa093a84`; last change `95967882`).

### Bug Description, Steps to Reproduce, Screenshots

In `Element.click`, the `mouseReleased` dispatch runs in a `finally` block after the `mousePressed` dispatch. The comment there states the intent (`browser_use/actor/element.py:307-308`):

> A cancelled or timed-out press may already have reached Chrome.
> Always attempt release, then propagate the failure to the caller.

When the press fails and the release also raises, Python replaces the in-flight press exception with the release exception, and the outer handler (`element.py:348-350`) builds `RuntimeError(f'Failed to click element: {type(e).__name__}: {e}')` from the release exception. The caller sees only the release error; the press failure survives only as `__context__` of the `__cause__`.

For example, the page is busy, so the press gets no reply and click's own `wait_for(timeout=1.0)` times out, and then the browser connection drops. The caller gets `RuntimeError('Failed to click element: ConnectionError: WebSocket connection closed')`, which does not mention the timeout that made the click fail.

`element.py` is unchanged on current main (0.13.13, `aa093a84`; last change `95967882`).

Steps:
1. Install browser-use 0.13.11 (or main).
2. Run the code below with `pytest`. It drives the real `cdp_use` `CDPClient` (1.4.5) against a local websocket endpoint that answers geometry like Chrome, never answers `mousePressed`, and closes the connection on `mouseReleased`. No browser is needed.
3. The assertion fails with the message in the log below.

A possible fix: inside the `finally`, catch a release exception when a press exception is already propagating (log it, or attach it with `add_note`), and let the release error propagate only when the press succeeded.

### Failing Python Code

```python
import asyncio
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
import websockets
from cdp_use.client import CDPClient

from browser_use.actor.element import Element

VIEWPORT = {'pageX': 0, 'pageY': 0, 'clientWidth': 800, 'clientHeight': 600}


async def browser(ws):
    async for raw in ws:
        msg = json.loads(raw)
        method, params = msg['method'], msg.get('params', {})
        if method == 'Input.dispatchMouseEvent' and params.get('type') == 'mousePressed':
            continue  # the page is busy: no reply
        if method == 'Input.dispatchMouseEvent' and params.get('type') == 'mouseReleased':
            await ws.close()  # the browser connection is lost
            return
        result = {}
        if method == 'Page.getLayoutMetrics':
            visual = {**VIEWPORT, 'offsetX': 0, 'offsetY': 0, 'scale': 1, 'zoom': 1}
            size = {'x': 0, 'y': 0, 'width': 800, 'height': 600}
            result = {'layoutViewport': VIEWPORT, 'visualViewport': visual, 'contentSize': size,
                      'cssLayoutViewport': VIEWPORT, 'cssVisualViewport': visual, 'cssContentSize': size}
        elif method == 'DOM.getContentQuads':
            result = {'quads': [[10, 10, 20, 10, 20, 20, 10, 20]]}
        await ws.send(json.dumps({'id': msg['id'], 'result': result}))


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_press_failure_is_propagated():
    async with websockets.serve(browser, '127.0.0.1', 0) as server:
        client = CDPClient(f"ws://127.0.0.1:{server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]}")
        await client.start()
        try:
            element = Element(browser_session=SimpleNamespace(cdp_client=client), backend_node_id=1, session_id='s1')
            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError) as exc_info:
                await element.click()
        finally:
            await client.stop()
    assert 'TimeoutError' in str(exc_info.value), f'the press timeout was replaced: {exc_info.value}'
```

### LLM Model

Not applicable (no LLM involved)

### Operating System & Browser Versions

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, x86_64; the test uses a local CDP endpoint (no browser needed). cdp-use 1.4.5, Python 3.13.9.

### Full DEBUG Log Output

```shell
E   AssertionError: the press timeout was replaced: Failed to click element: ConnectionError: WebSocket connection closed
E   assert 'TimeoutError' in 'Failed to click element: ConnectionError: WebSocket connection closed'
```

comment.body:
Thank you for the excellent bug report — the root-cause analysis and the self-contained reproducer made this straightforward to fix.

I've opened a PR with the fix: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/pull/6174

The press/release sequence is now try/except/else: the release is still always attempted, but when the press already failed, a release failure is attached to the press error via `add_note` instead of replacing it. When the press succeeded, a release failure propagates exactly as before. I verified all four combinations (press/release fail/succeed) plus your reproducer, and added it as a regression test in `tests/ci/test_element_click_press_release_error.py`.

issue.title: perplexity: streaming with_structured_output emits JSON from inside an unclosed think block

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [ ] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [x] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

#32465 (where the reasoning parsers came from).
Previously filed as #41200, which was auto-closed because it was detected as a programmatic submission. Reposting through the official bug-report template.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

from langchain_perplexity.output_parsers import (
    ReasoningJsonOutputParser,
    ReasoningStructuredOutputParser,
)


class City(BaseModel):
    city: str


# sonar-reasoning models stream a <think> block before the JSON answer.
# Here the reasoning contains a draft answer that the model then rejects.
text = (
    '<think>Draft:\n\n{"city": "Paris"}\n\n'
    'No, Tokyo fits better.</think>\n{"city": "Tokyo"}'
)
chunks = [text[i : i + 4] for i in range(0, len(text), 4)]

for parser in (ReasoningJsonOutputParser(), ReasoningStructuredOutputParser(pydantic_object=City)):
    print(type(parser).__name__)
    print("  invoke:", parser.invoke(text))
    print("  stream:", list(parser.transform(iter(chunks))))

# Output:
# ReasoningJsonOutputParser
#   invoke: {'city': 'Tokyo'}
#   stream: [{}, {'city': ''}, {'city': 'Pari'}, {'city': 'Paris'}, {}, {'city': 'Tok'}, {'city': 'Tokyo'}]
# ReasoningStructuredOutputParser
#   invoke: city='Tokyo'
#   stream: [City(city=''), City(city='Pari'), City(city='Paris'), City(city='Tok'), City(city='Tokyo')]
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

When streaming `ChatPerplexity.with_structured_output(...)` with a reasoning model, JSON that appears inside a `<think>` block that hasn't closed yet gets emitted as output.

While the stream is in the middle of `<think>`, `strip_think_tags` has nothing to strip, because the closing tag hasn't arrived yet. The partial text then goes to `JsonOutputParser`, and `parse_json_markdown` picks up the fenced block inside the reasoning. So the stream yields `{"city": "Paris"}`, a draft the model rejected, before the real answer. With a Pydantic schema it's a fully validated `City(city='Paris')`, which a consumer can't tell apart from a real result. `invoke` is not affected.

Expected: the stream should only yield the final answer (`{"city": "Tokyo"}`), never JSON from inside the reasoning.

Proposed fix: in both `parse_result` methods, return `None` when `partial=True` and the stripped text still starts with `<think>`, meaning the reasoning block hasn't closed yet. `strip_think_tags` itself stays the same, so `test_strip_think_tags_no_closing_tag` still holds. I tried this locally and the streams above become `[{}, {'city': 'Tok'}, {'city': 'Tokyo'}]` and `[City(city='Tok'), City(city='Tokyo')]`. I'd add a streaming test for each parser.

I'd like to work on this if a maintainer can assign me.

### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Windows
> OS Version:  10.0.26200
> Python Version:  3.10.20 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:19:56) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.6.9
> langsmith: 0.8.18
> langchain_perplexity: 1.4.1
> langchain_protocol: 0.0.18
> langchain_tests: 1.1.9

### Social handles (optional)

https://x.com/SohamMishrxgl
https://www.linkedin.com/in/soham-mishra-0313103ab/

Hi, thanks for the clear report and reproducer.

I'd like to take this one. The streaming path leaks JSON from inside an unclosed `<think>` block because `strip_think_tags` can't remove the open block until the closing tag arrives, so partial JSON inside the reasoning text gets emitted as parsed output. I'll put together a fix in `ReasoningJsonOutputParser` / `ReasoningStructuredOutputParser` with regression tests.

Could you please assign this issue to me? Thanks!

issue.title: fix: require confirmation by default for PythonTools code-executing tools
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10053 (security: CWE-913, missing default confirmation gate for code-executing tools).

`PythonTools` code-executing tools (`run_python_code`, `save_to_file_and_run`, `run_python_file_return_variable`, `pip_install_package`, `uv_pip_install_package`) now require human confirmation by default: the orchestration loop pauses them (`tool_call_paused`) instead of executing a model-requested call immediately. Previously the loop executed every model-requested call at once, so prompt injection against an agent processing untrusted content could drive `exec()`/`runpy()`/subprocess in the host process with no pause.

Design is default-deny with opt-out, and scoped to the highest-risk tools only:
- No `requires_confirmation_tools` passed (or `None`) -> the 5 code-executing tools are gated; `read_file`/`list_files` unchanged.
- An explicit value (including `[]`) is used as-is, so automated/sandboxed setups can opt out deliberately with `PythonTools(requires_confirmation_tools=[])`.
- Per-tool `requires_confirmation` continues to work as the override (registration logic untouched); the fix reuses the existing `Toolkit.requires_confirmation_tools` mechanism (same pattern as `KnowledgeTools` gating `remove_content`).

The approach was discussed on the issue; happy to adjust if maintainers prefer a different direction (e.g. an Agent-level policy gate).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Breaking change

The default behavior changes: model-requested code-execution tool calls now pause for confirmation. Explicit opt-out is available (`requires_confirmation_tools=[]`).

---

## Checklist

- [x] Code complies with style guidelines
- [x] Ran format/validation scripts (`./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh`)
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (comments, docstrings)
- [ ] Examples and guides: Relevant cookbook examples have been included or updated (if applicable)
- [x] Tested in clean environment
- [x] Tests added/updated (if applicable)

### Duplicate and AI-Generated PR Check

- [x] I have searched existing [open pull requests](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pulls) and confirmed that no other PR already addresses this issue
- [ ] If a similar PR exists, I have explained below why this PR is a better approach
- [ ] Check if this PR was entirely AI-generated (by Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

---

## Additional Notes

Security considerations:
- This closes the default-open execution path reported in #10053 but is not a sandbox: the class docstring and `warn()` still document that `safe_globals`/`safe_locals`/`restrict_to_base_dir` are not security boundaries and that untrusted input needs a real sandbox (separate process/container, scrubbed env).
- `ShellTools`/`DaytonaTools` have the same shape of risk; intentionally left out of this PR to keep the change minimal and auditable -- happy to follow up if maintainers want the same default there.

Verification (all offline, no network/keys):
- Reproduced the issue PoC: pre-fix the marker file was written via `exec()`; post-fix the same default assembly yields `tool_call_paused` and no execution.
- New regression tests in `libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_python_tools.py`: default gating, explicit opt-out, explicit list respected, end-to-end pause, end-to-end opt-out execution -- 27/27 pass in that file; `./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh` pass.

issue.title: `RunnableRetry.batch(return_exceptions=True)` broadcasts one non-retryable item error to every output

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [x] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters

- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

This is related to #35475, but it follows a different failure path. #35475
concerns incorrect positional merging after partial retries. Here, the first
non-retryable item exception escapes `RunnableRetry._batch` as a batch-level
exception and is then copied into every output slot.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from collections import defaultdict

from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda


attempts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)


def work(item: str) -> str:
    attempts[item] += 1

    if item == "ok":
        return "output:ok"
    if item == "permanent":
        raise TypeError("do not retry me")
    if item == "transient" and attempts[item] == 1:
        raise ValueError("retry me")
    return "output:transient"


runnable = RunnableLambda(work).with_retry(
    retry_if_exception_type=(ValueError,),
    stop_after_attempt=2,
    wait_exponential_jitter=False,
)

result = runnable.batch(
    ["ok", "permanent", "transient"],
    return_exceptions=True,
)

serialized = [
    (type(value).__name__, str(value))
    if isinstance(value, BaseException)
    else value
    for value in result
]

print(dict(attempts))
print(serialized)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
{'ok': 1, 'permanent': 1, 'transient': 1}
[('TypeError', 'do not retry me'),
 ('TypeError', 'do not retry me'),
 ('TypeError', 'do not retry me')]


The successful result for `ok` is lost. The retryable `ValueError` for
`transient` is never retried. All three positions are reported as the
`TypeError` produced by `permanent`.

The async `RunnableRetry.abatch(..., return_exceptions=True)` path produces the
same result.

## Expected behavior

The successful input must retain `output:ok`, the permanent failure must retain its own `TypeError`, and the transient input must retain its own outcome (`ValueError` or its retried successful output). No item may acquire a sibling's error.

This report does not require a particular batch retry-scheduling policy. Existing upstream tests permit retrying failed siblings together.
```

### Description

When a retry-wrapped runnable processes a batch containing a successful item,
a non-retryable failure, and a retryable failure, the result depends on which
exception appears first.

If the non-retryable exception is selected as `first_exception`, it aborts the
retry loop for the whole batch. With `return_exceptions=True`, the outer batch
wrapper then returns that same exception in every output position. This
overwrites an already successful result and prevents another item with a
retryable exception from being retried.

### Root cause

The affected paths are:

- `RunnableRetry._batch` and the analogous `RunnableRetry._abatch` in
  `libs/core/langchain_core/runnables/retry.py`.
- `_batch_with_config` and the analogous async wrapper in
  `libs/core/langchain_core/runnables/base.py`.

`RunnableRetry._batch` calls the underlying batch with
`return_exceptions=True`, records successful results in `results_map`, selects
one `first_exception`, and raises it as a single Tenacity control signal. If
that exception is not accepted by `retry_if_exception_type`, it escapes
`_batch`; the function handles only `RetryError` locally.

The outer `_batch_with_config` now sees one exception for the entire batch.
When `return_exceptions=True`, it converts that batch-level exception to
`[e for _ in inputs]`, replacing every per-item outcome with the same
exception.

### System Info

OS: Linux 6.8.0 x86_64
Python: 3.10.12
langchain-core: 1.6.9

### Related Issues / PRs

#38223 concerns Responses streaming with Pydantic $defs; #40332 concerns an already-wrapped OpenAI tool dictionary returning before strict conversion. #26232 concerns a no-argument tool. This report isolates a bare object nested inside an MCP input schema, where the direct-property control is normalized and the deeper equivalent is not.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import asyncio

from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
from langchain.mcp import as_langchain_tool
from langchain_core.utils.function_calling import convert_to_openai_tool
from mcp.types import Tool

DIRECT = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"payload": {"type": "object"}},
    "required": ["payload"],
}

NESTED = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "wrapper": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"payload": {"type": "object"}},
            "required": ["payload"],
        }
    },
    "required": ["wrapper"],
}

async def convert(schema):
    mcp_tool = Tool(name="echo", description="Echo.", inputSchema=schema)
    langchain_tool = await as_langchain_tool(
        mcp_tool, Client(FastMCP("unused-controlled-server"))
    )
    return convert_to_openai_tool(langchain_tool, strict=True)["function"]["parameters"]

async def main():
    direct = await convert(DIRECT)
    nested = await convert(NESTED)
    print(direct["properties"]["payload"])
    print(nested["properties"]["wrapper"]["properties"]["payload"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
Expected: Equivalent bare object schemas receive consistent strict conversion, or unsupported shapes are rejected explicitly.
Actual: A direct payload object gains additionalProperties:false; the same object at wrapper.payload remains {"type":"object"}.
```

### Description

The issue is in MCP schema preprocessing in `_normalize_mcp_schema` and strict conversion in `_recursive_set_additional_properties_false`. Pass an MCP tool through `as_langchain_tool`, then call `convert_to_openai_tool(..., strict=True)`. Compare a direct `payload` defined as `{"type":"object"}` with the same definition nested at `wrapper.payload`.

MCP preprocessing normalizes only direct properties. The later strict traversal visits the deeper bare object but its condition for adding `additionalProperties:false` does not match that shape. The direct control is closed, while the nested object remains unchanged. This reports inconsistent conversion, not a live provider HTTP 400 or a guarantee that arbitrary open objects can be converted without changing their meaning.

mcp: 2.3.0

issue.title: fix(anthropic): forward http:// image URLs as url sources instead of downloading
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- http:// image URLs were downloaded by the proxy and sent to Anthropic as base64
- https:// URLs on the same path were forwarded untouched as url sources

How it solves it:

- http:// URLs are now forwarded as url sources, same as https://
- Bedrock invoke, Vertex AI and Snowflake still convert to base64, since those providers have no URL source

Intentional product change: callers whose http:// image host is reachable only by the proxy will now see a provider-side fetch error instead of a silent proxy download. Use https:// or data URLs when the provider cannot reach the host

## User Flow

Before: a developer sending an image over plain http gets silently different behavior than over https

1. They send POST /v1/chat/completions with `"image_url": {"url": "http://img-host/pic.png"}` on a model routed to Anthropic
2. The call returns 200, but the provider received `source: {"type": "base64", ...}` with bytes the proxy downloaded, and the image host logged a GET from the proxy
3. The same request with an https:// URL arrives at the provider untouched as `source: {"type": "url", ...}`

After: http:// is forwarded exactly like https://

1. They send the same POST with the http:// image URL
2. The provider receives `source: {"type": "url", "url": "http://img-host/pic.png"}`, and the image host sees no request from the proxy
3. If the provider cannot fetch that URL, its error reaches the caller instead of silent bytes

## Relevant issues

Fixes #43098

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Verification ran at the request-transformation layer, which is the layer this fix touches. No live provider call was made, since this environment has no provider credentials or external network. Download functions were stubbed to record calls instead of hitting the network

### Before (eff6fc1)

1. `create_anthropic_image_param("http://example.com/image.png")` invoked the download and returned `source: {"type": "base64", ...}`
2. `AnthropicConfig().inlines_remote_media(...)` returned True for an http:// image URL, so `async_transform_request` downloaded it before conversion
3. The same calls with https:// returned `source: {"type": "url", ...}` with no download attempted

### After (26684a6)

1. `create_anthropic_image_param("http://example.com/image.png")` returns `source: {"type": "url", "url": "http://example.com/image.png"}` with no download attempted
2. `inlines_remote_media` returns False for both schemes, so `async_transform_request` forwards both as url sources
3. `is_bedrock_invoke=True` (Bedrock invoke, Vertex AI, Snowflake) still converts both schemes to base64

New regression tests (5): `test_create_anthropic_image_param_with_http_url_forwards_url`, `test_create_anthropic_image_param_with_http_url_still_base64_for_bedrock`, `test_anthropic_messages_pt_with_http_url_image`, `test_inlines_remote_media_never_inlines_image_urls[http/https]`. Each bug-covering test was verified to fail on the pre-fix code and pass after the fix. Related suites (`test_prompt_factory.py`, `test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py`, `test_image_handling.py`, vertex-ai anthropic image tests) show no new failures against baseline

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Private http:// image hosts unreachable by the provider now fail at the provider instead of being fetched by the proxy

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

issue.title: [Bug] A silent DP rank leaves /flush_cache waiting without a deadline and blocks subsequent flush calls
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Searched related issues and PRs; related work and limitations are noted below.
- [ ] Reproduced on the latest version. The service observations are from the pinned v0.5.17 image; current main was inspected as source only.
- [x] Included reproduction steps and the available environment information.
- [x] Report written in English.

### Describe the bug

In the pinned v0.5.17 deployment with DP=2, suspending one scheduler rank leaves `/flush_cache` without an HTTP response until the client times out. `FanOutCommunicator.queueing_call` waits for all expected replies while holding its queueing lock, without an internal wait deadline. Subsequent calls on the **same communicator** cannot dispatch until the active call finishes.

This is a worker-failure/deadline limitation of an existing all-rank collection contract. Related PRs already discuss the trade-off; this report adds a real-service reproduction and the observed health behavior, rather than claiming the mechanism was previously unknown.

### Reproduction

Use a dedicated test service in the image below with two NPUs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/qwen3-0.6b --served-model-name qwen3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30130 \
  --device npu --attention-backend ascend --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.4 \
  --dp-size 2 --tp-size 1
```

1. After readiness, confirm `POST /flush_cache`, `GET /health` and a short generation request succeed.
2. In that test container's PID namespace, identify one scheduler rank with `ps -eo pid,stat,args`. Suspend that specific scheduler PID with `kill -STOP <scheduler-pid>`; keep the other rank and HTTP/tokenizer process running.
3. Run:

```bash
curl -sS --max-time 45 -X POST \
  -w '\nHTTP_CODE=%{http_code} TIME=%{time_total}\n' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30130/flush_cache
```

4. Resume the same PID with `kill -CONT <scheduler-pid>`, and check that a new flush succeeds. For the recovery observation, another flush was started while the rank was still stopped and allowed to remain pending across SIGCONT.

### Recorded results

These are measured real-service observations, not a model of the scheduler:

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline flush | HTTP 200, 0.006699 s |
| One rank stopped, flush | curl exit 28, HTTP code 000, 45.000981 s |
| Health probes during the quiet stopped-rank period | 503 / 200 / 503 |
| Four health probes with paced generation traffic during the same stopped-rank window | all 200 |
| Eight paced generation requests in that window | six HTTP 200 in under 0.1 s; two client timeouts |
| Flush started while stopped and spanning recovery | HTTP 200, total request time 41.384738 s |
| New flush after recovery | HTTP 200, 0.004737 s |

The 41.38 s figure includes waiting before SIGCONT; it is **not** a post-resume recovery latency. A second real-service variant stopped both ranks and also observed a 45 s flush timeout, with health checks returning 503.

A separate CPU integration test of the real communicator and control path supplied only one reply for fan-out 2: the first call stayed pending and a second caller did not dispatch (`dispatch_count=1`). Its transport/rank replies were declared fixtures. This is the direct measurement of same-communicator head-of-line blocking; no claim is made that every other control endpoint shares that lock.

### Code path and expected behavior

The relevant structure is:

```python
async with self._queueing_lock:
    # dispatch and initialize the per-call collector
    ...
    await self._result_event.wait()
    ...
```

The event is set when the expected reply count is reached. With a missing rank, the wait itself has no deadline. **Changing the count comparison from == to >= would not fix missing replies**; fewer than the expected count satisfies neither comparison.

On 2026-10-21, main at [`573b5716f5b4`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/573b5716f5b47c77a5fb5f2c24ae9b0e596dc3d1/python/sglang/srt/managers/communicator.py#L41-L57) still has the bare event wait inside the lock. This is source inspection, not a fresh full-service reproduction.

Expected behavior to discuss: an explicit control-call deadline and a defined worker-failure/recovery outcome, rather than relying solely on the HTTP client's timeout. Any solution needs to preserve response ownership: simply releasing the lock after timeout can allow late replies to be consumed by a later call. Partial results must not be reported as successful all-rank completion.

### Related work and limits

- #30022 explicitly acknowledged that a scheduler which never replies can keep a control slot held.
- #30606 addresses FIFO serialization.
- #42694 addresses cancellation and late-reply ownership; its description explicitly states that it does not add worker-failure recovery or a drain timeout.

issue.title: [Bug] A silent DP rank leaves /flush_cache waiting without a deadline and blocks subsequent flush calls
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Searched related issues and PRs; related work and limitations are noted below.
- [ ] Reproduced on the latest version. The service observations are from the pinned v0.5.17 image; current main was inspected as source only.
- [x] Included reproduction steps and the available environment information.
- [x] Report written in English.

### Describe the bug

In the pinned v0.5.17 deployment with DP=2, suspending one scheduler rank leaves `/flush_cache` without an HTTP response until the client times out. `FanOutCommunicator.queueing_call` waits for all expected replies while holding its queueing lock, without an internal wait deadline. Subsequent calls on the **same communicator** cannot dispatch until the active call finishes.

This is a worker-failure/deadline limitation of an existing all-rank collection contract. Related PRs already discuss the trade-off; this report adds a real-service reproduction and the observed health behavior, rather than claiming the mechanism was previously unknown.

### Reproduction

Use a dedicated test service in the image below with two NPUs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/qwen3-0.6b --served-model-name qwen3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30130 \
  --device npu --attention-backend ascend --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.4 \
  --dp-size 2 --tp-size 1
```

1. After readiness, confirm `POST /flush_cache`, `GET /health` and a short generation request succeed.
2. In that test container's PID namespace, identify one scheduler rank with `ps -eo pid,stat,args`. Suspend that specific scheduler PID with `kill -STOP <scheduler-pid>`; keep the other rank and HTTP/tokenizer process running.
3. Run:

```bash
curl -sS --max-time 45 -X POST \
  -w '\nHTTP_CODE=%{http_code} TIME=%{time_total}\n' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30130/flush_cache
```

4. Resume the same PID with `kill -CONT <scheduler-pid>`, and check that a new flush succeeds. For the recovery observation, another flush was started while the rank was still stopped and allowed to remain pending across SIGCONT.

### Recorded results

These are measured real-service observations, not a model of the scheduler:

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline flush | HTTP 200, 0.006699 s |
| One rank stopped, flush | curl exit 28, HTTP code 000, 45.000981 s |
| Health probes during the quiet stopped-rank period | 503 / 200 / 503 |
| Four health probes with paced generation traffic during the same stopped-rank window | all 200 |
| Eight paced generation requests in that window | six HTTP 200 in under 0.1 s; two client timeouts |
| Flush started while stopped and spanning recovery | HTTP 200, total request time 41.384738 s |
| New flush after recovery | HTTP 200, 0.004737 s |

The 41.38 s figure includes waiting before SIGCONT; it is **not** a post-resume recovery latency. A second real-service variant stopped both ranks and also observed a 45 s flush timeout, with health checks returning 503.

A separate CPU integration test of the real communicator and control path supplied only one reply for fan-out 2: the first call stayed pending and a second caller did not dispatch (`dispatch_count=1`). Its transport/rank replies were declared fixtures. This is the direct measurement of same-communicator head-of-line blocking; no claim is made that every other control endpoint shares that lock.

### Code path and expected behavior

The relevant structure is:

```python
async with self._queueing_lock:
    # dispatch and initialize the per-call collector
    ...
    await self._result_event.wait()
    ...
```

The event is set when the expected reply count is reached. With a missing rank, the wait itself has no deadline. **Changing the count comparison from == to >= would not fix missing replies**; fewer than the expected count satisfies neither comparison.

On 2026-10-21, main at [`573b5716f5b4`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/573b5716f5b47c77a5fb5f2c24ae9b0e596dc3d1/python/sglang/srt/managers/communicator.py#L41-L57) still has the bare event wait inside the lock. This is source inspection, not a fresh full-service reproduction.

Expected behavior to discuss: an explicit control-call deadline and a defined worker-failure/recovery outcome, rather than relying solely on the HTTP client's timeout. Any solution needs to preserve response ownership: simply releasing the lock after timeout can allow late replies to be consumed by a later call. Partial results must not be reported as successful all-rank completion.

### Related work and limits

- #30022 explicitly acknowledged that a scheduler which never replies can keep a control slot held.
- #30606 addresses FIFO serialization.
- #42694 addresses cancellation and late-reply ownership; its description explicitly states that it does not add worker-failure recovery or a drain timeout.
- #39562 concerns aggregating flush results; #40119 and #36152 concern exposing/forwarding the scheduler-side flush timeout. These are distinct from bounding the tokenizer-side reply wait when a rank cannot respond.

SIGSTOP is deliberate fault injection. No production frequency, irreversible deadlock, or permanent whole-service failure is claimed: resuming the rank allowed progress. Other control operations, real client-disconnect cancellation, and gateway behavior were not validated by this real-service run. Healthy responses occurred in the observed traffic window, not under all possible loads.

### Environment

Historical real-service runs were performed on 2026-10-11 with:
- SGLang v0.5.17, recorded commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`.
- Image: `quay.io/ascend/sglang:v0.5.17-cann9.0.0-910b`.
- Resolved image digest: `sha256:35852210819ac0d388bce69c24960189c0412a300dc3add13234b549ba00abda`.
- Ascend 910B3; Python 3.11.15; model: Qwen3-0.6B, mounted at `/models/qwen3-0.6b`.
- Full `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output was not captured in the historical archive; the information above is from the recorded image identity, launch arguments and logs. No fresh hardware run was performed for this submission.

issue.title: BUG: `agent.step()` returns an `ActionOutput` wrapper instead of the final answer (or `None`)
issue.body: **Problem** `MultiStepAgent.step` is documented to return "either None if the step is not final, or the final answer" (`agents.py:785`), and `CodeAgent._step_stream` says the same about its last yield (`agents.py:1644`). The "Run agents one step at a time" section of the memory tutorial (`docs/source/en/tutorials/memory.md`) relies on this: ```python final_answer = None while final_answer is None and step_number <= 10: ... final_answer = agent.step(memory_step) ``` But `_step_stream` always yields `ActionOutput(output=..., is_final_answer=...)` last (`CodeAgent`: `agents.py:1764`; `ToolCallingAgent`: `agents.py:1356`), and `step` returns that item unchanged (`return list(self._step_stream(memory_step))[-1]`, `agents.py:787`). So a final step returns `ActionOutput(output='42', is_final_answer=True)` instead of `'42'`, and a non-final step returns `ActionOutput(output=None, is_final_answer=False)`, which is not `None`. The tutorial loop therefore stops after the first step whether or not it was final, and prints the wrapper as the final answer. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Install smolagents from main (`96f33faa`). 2. Run the script below with `pytest`. It uses a scripted `Model` subclass so no API key is needed; the agent, the local Python executor and `step` are the real ones. ```python import time from smolagents import CodeAgent from smolagents.memory import ActionStep, TaskStep from smolagents.models import ChatMessage, MessageRole, Model from smolagents.monitoring import Timing class ScriptedModel(Model): """Returns fixed replies, so the example needs no API key.""" def __init__(self, replies): super().__init__(model_id="scripted") self.replies = iter(replies) def generate(self, messages, stop_sequences=None, response_format=None, tools_to_call_from=None, **kwargs): return ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.ASSISTANT, content=next(self.replies)) def run_step(agent, number): return agent.step(ActionStep(step_number=number, timing=Timing(start_time=time.time()))) def make_agent(*replies): agent = CodeAgent(tools=[], model=ScriptedModel(replies), verbosity_level=0) agent.python_executor.send_tools({**agent.tools}) # as in the memory tutorial agent.memory.steps.append(TaskStep(task="What is 6 * 7?")) return agent def test_final_step_returns_the_final_answer(): agent = make_agent('Thought: done.\n\nfinal_answer("42")\n') result = run_step(agent, 1) assert result == "42", f"expected the final answer, got {result!r}" def test_non_final_step_returns_none(): agent = make_agent("Thought: compute.\n\nx = 6 * 7\nprint(x)\n") result = run_step(agent, 1) assert result is None, f"expected None for a non-final step, got {result!r}" ``` **Actual behavior and error logs** ```shell E AssertionError: expected the final answer, got ActionOutput(output='42', is_final_answer=True) E assert ActionOutput(output='42', is_final_answer=True) == '42' E AssertionError: expected None for a non-final step, got ActionOutput(output=None, is_final_answer=False) E assert ActionOutput(output=None, is_final_answer=False) is None ``` Running the tutorial loop itself with the same scripted model prints: ```shell step 1 returned ActionOutput(output=None, is_final_answer=False) The final answer is: ActionOutput(output=None, is_final_answer=False) ``` **Expected behavior** As documented: `step()` returns the final answer (`'42'`) when the step is final, and `None` otherwise, so the tutorial loop keeps stepping until a final answer is produced. **Environment:** - OS: Linux - Python version: 3.13.9 - Package version: smolagents 1.27.0.dev0, commit `96f33faa` (current main) ``` smolagents 1.27.0.dev0 (installed from source at 96f33faa) ``` **Additional context (optional)** - `_run_stream` depends on the `ActionOutput` items (`agents.py:578-582`), so the fix probably belongs in `step`, e.g. unwrapping the last item: return `last.output` when `last.is_final_answer`, else `None`. - Unrelated to the bug but in the same tutorial snippet: `ActionStep(step_number=..., observations_images=[])` now raises `TypeError: ActionStep.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'timing'`. - Related but different: #1457 (distinguishing `FinalOutput(None)` from "no final answer"). --- ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the existing issues and have not found a similar bug report. - [x] I have provided a minimal, reproducible example. - [x] I have provided the full traceback of the error. - [x] I have provided my environment details. - [ ] I am willing to work on this issue and submit a pull request. (optional)

comment.body: I've opened a fix for this: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/pull/3042 — `MultiStepAgent.step` now returns the final answer when the last stream item is an `ActionOutput` with `is_final_answer=True`, and `None` otherwise, per the documented contract. Falsy final answers (`0`, `""`, `False`) are returned as-is since the flag, not truthiness, is the discriminator. Includes a regression test plus the reproducer with before/after outputs in the PR description. Happy to adjust if reviewers prefer a different shape.

issue.title: [Fix] grpc: Preserve max_new_tokens three-state semantics
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #44121 by giving native gRPC clients an explicit way to request the Python/HTTP `max_new_tokens: null` behavior without changing the Python server's default.

The original version of this PR mapped an unset proto field to JSON `null`. After checking the Python path in response to review feedback, that was not fully compatible: Python deliberately distinguishes an omitted field (default `128`) from an explicit `null` (no limit). This revision preserves all three states:

| gRPC request | Scheduler JSON | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| neither field set | key omitted | Python default: 128 |
| `max_new_tokens: N` | `"max_new_tokens": N` | explicit cap |
| `no_max_new_tokens_limit: true` | `"max_new_tokens": null` | no cap, bounded by context/memory |

`max_new_tokens` and `no_max_new_tokens_limit=true` are rejected when supplied together rather than silently choosing one.

Example:

```python
sampling_params = pb.SamplingParams(
    temperature=0,
    ignore_eos=True,
    no_max_new_tokens_limit=True,
)
```

## Implementation

- Adds the backward-compatible optional proto field `SamplingParams.no_max_new_tokens_limit`.
- Maps that flag to an explicit JSON `null` in the native gRPC request adapter.
- Leaves an unset `max_new_tokens` omitted, matching `SamplingParams.max_new_tokens = 128` in the Python server.
- Regenerates the checked-in `runtime.v1` Rust bindings with `cargo gen-api`.
- Covers `TextGenerate` and `Generate` for the default, explicit-cap, and unlimited states, plus conflicting-input validation.

## Validation

```text
cargo test -p sglang-grpc
20 passed, 0 failed

cargo test -p sglang-api-types
20 json_contract + 1 json_parity tests passed

cargo clippy -p sglang-grpc --all-targets -- -D warnings
clean

cargo fmt --all -- --check
clean
```

The branch is rebased onto the current `main`; the previous merge conflict with the tokenized multimodal gRPC changes is resolved while retaining their tests and behavior.

issue.title: MCP tools with nested open objects produce an invalid schema under strict=True

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [ ] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

#38223 concerns Responses streaming with Pydantic $defs; #40332 concerns an already-wrapped OpenAI tool dictionary returning before strict conversion. #26232 concerns a no-argument tool. This report isolates a bare object nested inside an MCP input schema, where the direct-property control is normalized and the deeper equivalent is not.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import asyncio

from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
from langchain.mcp import as_langchain_tool
from langchain_core.utils.function_calling import convert_to_openai_tool
from mcp.types import Tool

DIRECT = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"payload": {"type": "object"}},
    "required": ["payload"],
}

NESTED = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "wrapper": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"payload": {"type": "object"}},
            "required": ["payload"],
        }
    },
    "required": ["wrapper"],
}

async def convert(schema):
    mcp_tool = Tool(name="echo", description="Echo.", inputSchema=schema)
    langchain_tool = await as_langchain_tool(
        mcp_tool, Client(FastMCP("unused-controlled-server"))
    )
    return convert_to_openai_tool(langchain_tool, strict=True)["function"]["parameters"]

async def main():
    direct = await convert(DIRECT)
    nested = await convert(NESTED)
    print(direct["properties"]["payload"])
    print(nested["properties"]["wrapper"]["properties"]["payload"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
Expected: Equivalent bare object schemas receive consistent strict conversion, or unsupported shapes are rejected explicitly.
Actual: A direct payload object gains additionalProperties:false; the same object at wrapper.payload remains {"type":"object"}.
```

### Description

The issue is in MCP schema preprocessing in `_normalize_mcp_schema` and strict conversion in `_recursive_set_additional_properties_false`. Pass an MCP tool through `as_langchain_tool`, then call `convert_to_openai_tool(..., strict=True)`. Compare a direct `payload` defined as `{"type":"object"}` with the same definition nested at `wrapper.payload`.

MCP preprocessing normalizes only direct properties. The later strict traversal visits the deeper bare object but its condition for adding `additionalProperties:false` does not match that shape. The direct control is closed, while the nested object remains unchanged. This reports inconsistent conversion, not a live provider HTTP 400 or a guarantee that arbitrary open objects can be converted without changing their meaning.

### System Info

Python: 3.11.15
langchain-core: 1.6.12
langchain: 1.4.6
fastmcp: 4.1.1
mcp: 2.3.0

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and the offline reproducer — very helpful.

I can reproduce this on current master: `_recursive_set_additional_properties_false` in `langchain_core/utils/function_calling.py` visits the nested bare `{"type": "object"}` at `wrapper.payload` but never sets `additionalProperties: false` on it, because none of its trigger conditions hold for a completely bare object (`required` not in schema, no `properties` key at all, no `additionalProperties` key). The direct property only gets fixed because `_normalize_mcp_schema` normalizes direct properties first. The result is an invalid strict-mode schema whenever an MCP tool has a nested bare object.

I'd like to work on a fix for this.

issue.title: XMLOutputParser.parse is quadratic in the number of < characters (encoding_matcher regex)

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [x] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

#41149 is a correctness problem in the same regex. Previously filed as #41316, which the triage bot closed for lacking an issue type.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import re, time
from langchain_core.output_parsers import XMLOutputParser

for n in (16_000, 32_000, 64_000):
    s = "<" * n
    t = time.time()
    try:
        XMLOutputParser(parser="xml").parse(s)
    except Exception:
        pass
    print(n, f"{(time.time() - t) * 1000:.0f} ms")
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
No error. Timing on langchain-core 1.6.10:

16000  79 ms
32000  313 ms
64000  1244 ms

The regex alone (encoding_matcher.search on the same strings): 78 ms, 315 ms, 1243 ms.
```

### Description

`XMLOutputParser.encoding_matcher`, `re.compile(r"<([^>]*encoding[^>]*)>\n(.*)", re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)`, is searched over the model's whole output. On text with many `<` and no `>`, each `<` starts a scan to the end of the string, so the search is quadratic. All of the time in the reproduction is the regex; both `parser="xml"` and `parser="defusedxml"` run it. The text is model output, which the parser should treat as untrusted.

Possible fix: match only an XML declaration at the start, e.g. `re.match(r"\s*<\?xml[^>]*encoding[^>]*\?>\n(.*)", text, re.DOTALL)`, or bound the tag with `[^<>]` so a failed attempt cannot rescan past the next `<`. Either would also fix #41149.

Reproduced by hand on langchain-core 1.6.10 at 8ace87e; the regex is unchanged on main at the time of filing.

### System Info

langchain-core 1.6.10 (commit 8ace87e)
Python 3.14.2
macOS (darwin, arm64)

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and the benchmarks — the quadratic behavior in `encoding_matcher` is clear, and the `<` -without-`>` case confirms it's the regex, not the parsing, that dominates the time.

I'll take this one. My plan is to bound the tag so a failed attempt can't rescan past the next `<` (which should also fix the related #41149, where the current pattern eats valid elements), and I'll add a regression benchmark test showing linear time on the `"<" * n` input.

EngineCore encountered a fatal error. Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 361, in execute_model self._apply_mm_cache(scheduler_output) File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 354, in _apply_mm_cache req_data.mm_features = mm_cache.get_and_update_features( File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 228, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py", line 458, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 241, in get_and_update_item return self._shm_cache.get(address, monotonic_id) File "vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_object_storage.py", line 613, in get raise ValueError( ValueError: Data for address:id '4817824:4' has been modified or is invalid. vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause. ``` Every in-flight and later request then fails, and `/health` stops answering 200. `/pause?mode=keep` is documented to ignore `clear_cache` ("Ignored when mode=keep"), so tecnically a keep pause is not expected to touch any cache at all. ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep ``` Each round of the client below does an idle pause+resume, then sends 12 streamed requests with distinct 448 px images (4 run, 8 wait behind `--max-num-seqs 4`). 300 ms later it pauses and resumes, then sends 8 requests with distinct 1344 px images. Results on RTX A5000, one fresh server per row: | server | pause call | result | |---|---|---| | shm | `/pause?mode=keep` | engine dead in round 1 (3/3 servers) | | shm | `/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true` (1344 px images sent during the drain) | engine dead in round 1 (1/1) | | shm | `/pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false` | alive after 67 rounds; the same server then died in round 1 of the `mode=keep` arm | | lru | `/pause?mode=keep` | alive after 51 rounds |
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone client (stdlib only): /pause clears the shared-memory multimodal cache under requests that still hold handles into it, and the engine dies when one of them is scheduled. vLLM 0.31.0 with `--mm-processor-cache-type shm`. A request's image travels to the engine as an (address, monotonic_id) handle into the SHM ring buffer; the worker resolves it only when the request is first scheduled (v1/worker/worker_base.py:348-356 -> multimodal/cache/shm.py:241 -> shm_object_storage.py:608-614). `POST /pause` defaults to clear_cache=true (entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/api_router.py:34; its docstring says the flag is ignored for mode=keep) and AsyncLLM.pause_generation clears the frontend cache for every mode (v1/engine/async_llm.py:950-951). For the SHM cache that resets the ring buffer -- addresses and ids back to 0 (shm_object_storage.py:163-170) -- while requests queued behind --max-num-seqs still carry handles into it. New images written after the clear reuse those slots; when a kept request is scheduled its handle fails the id check, `ValueError: Data for address:id ':' has been modified or is invalid.` is raised in execute_model, and EngineCore exits (EngineDeadError; every later request fails, /health is no longer 200). Server: VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 Run: python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep Round: an idle /pause?mode=keep + /resume (nothing in flight, so it only resets the SHM ring); then 12 streamed chat requests, each with its own 448 px noise image (4 run, 8 wait behind --max-num-seqs 4); `--pause-after-ms` later the pause call; then /resume and at once 8 more requests with distinct 1344 px images. Arms (the pause call): keep /pause?mode=keep (clear_cache left at its default, true) keep_noclear /pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false (control) wait /pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true; the 8 large images are sent while the pause drains none no pause (control) Exit 1 when the engine dies (/health not 200, or a response carrying EngineDeadError / "EngineCore encountered"). """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import http.client import json import random import struct import sys import threading import time import urllib.parse import zlib from collections import Counter DEAD_MARKERS = ("EngineDeadError", "EngineCore encountered", "engine is dead", "Engine is dead") def png(seed: int, size: int) -> str: rnd = random.Random(seed) raw = bytearray() for _ in range(size): raw.append(0) raw += rnd.randbytes(size * 3) def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes: return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF) body = (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 1)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")) return "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(body).decode() class Client: def __init__(self, base: str, timeout: float): u = urllib.parse.urlparse(base) self.host, self.port, self.timeout = u.hostname, u.port or 80, timeout def _req(self, method: str, path: str, body=None, timeout=None) -> tuple[int, str]: c = http.client.HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=timeout or self.timeout) try: c.request(method, path, body=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = c.getresponse() return r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace") except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 return -1, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" finally: c.close() def health(self) -> int: return self._req("GET", "/health", timeout=10)[0] def chat(self, model: str, image: str, nonce: str, stream: bool, max_tokens: int) -> dict: body = {"model": model, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image}}, {"type": "text", "text": f"{nonce} Describe this image in detail."}]}]} st, text = self._req("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", body) err = None if st == 200 and stream: for line in text.splitlines(): if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]": try: d = json.loads(line[6:]) except ValueError: continue if "error" in d: err = json.dumps(d["error"])[:400] elif st != 200: err = text[:400] return {"status": st, "error": err} def run_round(cl: Client, model: str, arm: str, k: int, a) -> Counter: small = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + i, a.small_px) for i in range(a.streams)] large = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + 50 + i, a.large_px) for i in range(a.large)] out: Counter = Counter() lock = threading.Lock() def send(img, nonce, stream, mt, tag): res = cl.chat(model, img, nonce, stream, mt) with lock: if res["status"] == 200 and not res["error"]: out[f"{tag}:ok"] += 1 else: out[f"{tag}:fail"] += 1 if res["error"] and any(m in res["error"] for m in DEAD_MARKERS): out["engine_dead_response"] += 1 if out["samples"] < 3: out["samples"] += 1 print(f" [{arm} r{k}] {tag} status={res['status']} {res['error']}", flush=True) if a.prelude_clear: # Idle clear first (nothing in flight): the round's 448 px images then sit at the start of the SHM ring, # where the large images written after the mid-round clear land. Without it they would sit right after # the previous round's large images, which the new large images exactly refill, so no stale handle is # ever overwritten. cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=keep") cl._req("POST", "/resume") first = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(small[i], f"r{k}s{i}", True, a.max_tokens, "small"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.streams)] for t in first: t.start() time.sleep(a.pause_after_ms / 1000) second = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(large[i], f"r{k}L{i}", False, a.large_max_tokens, "large"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.large)] if arm in ("keep", "keep_noclear"): q = "/pause?mode=keep" + ("&clear_cache=false" if arm == "keep_noclear" else "") st, _ = cl._req("POST", q) out[f"pause_{st}"] += 1 time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 for t in second: t.start() elif arm == "wait": res = {} pt = threading.Thread(target=lambda: res.update(st=cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true")[0]), daemon=True) pt.start() time.sleep(0.05) for t in second: # rendered (and written to SHM) while the pause drains t.start() pt.join(a.timeout) out[f"pause_{res.get('st')}"] += 1 st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 else: time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) for t in second: t.start() for t in first + second: t.join(a.timeout + 5) h = cl.health() out[f"health_{h}"] += 1 if h != 200: out["engine_dead_health"] += 1 return out def main() -> int: p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("base", nargs="?", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") p.add_argument("--base-url", default=None) p.add_argument("--out", default=None) p.add_argument("--arms", default="keep", help="comma list of keep, keep_noclear, wait, none") p.add_argument("--arm-minutes", default="", help="e.g. keep_noclear=4,keep=10 (default --minutes)") p.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=10.0) p.add_argument("--max-rounds", type=int, default=100000) p.add_argument("--streams", type=int, default=12) p.add_argument("--small-px", type=int, default=448) p.add_argument("--large", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--large-px", type=int, default=1344) p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=96) p.add_argument("--large-max-tokens", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--pause-after-ms", type=int, default=300) p.add_argument("--pause-ms", type=int, default=100) p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=180) p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261016) p.add_argument("--no-prelude-clear", dest="prelude_clear", action="store_false", help="skip the idle pause+resume (cache clear) at the start of each round") a = p.parse_args() cl = Client(a.base_url or a.base, a.timeout) st, text = cl._req("GET", "/v1/models") model = json.loads(text)["data"][0]["id"] print(f"model={model} args={vars(a)}", flush=True) mins = {kv.split("=")[0]: float(kv.split("=")[1]) for kv in a.arm_minutes.split(",") if kv} summary = {"model": model, "args": vars(a), "arms": {}} dead_arm = None for ai, arm in enumerate(a.arms.split(",")): t_end = time.monotonic() + mins.get(arm, a.minutes) * 60 tot: Counter = Counter() rounds = 0 dead_round = None while time.monotonic() < t_end and rounds < a.max_rounds: c = run_round(cl, model, arm, ai * 10000 + rounds, a) rounds += 1 tot.update(c) print(f"[{arm}] round {rounds:4d} " + " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(c.items()) if k != "samples"), flush=True) if c["engine_dead_health"] or c["engine_dead_response"]: dead_round = rounds break tot.pop("samples", None) summary["arms"][arm] = {"rounds": rounds, "engine_died_in_round": dead_round, "counts": dict(tot)} print(f"== arm {arm}: {rounds} rounds, engine died in round {dead_round}", flush=True) if dead_round: dead_arm = arm break summary["engine_died_in_arm"] = dead_arm if a.out: with open(a.out, "w") as f: json.dump(summary, f, indent=1) print("BUG PRESENT: engine died in arm " + dead_arm if dead_arm else "not reproduced (engine alive)", flush=True) return 1 if dead_arm else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Possible fixes: skip the frontend cache clear for `mode=keep`, as documented; for abort/wait, clear only once no queued request holds a handle; make `clear()` respect the reader flags; or fail just the affected request instead of the engine? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body: Opened a fix PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62587 — it makes pause mode=keep ignore clear_cache as documented, with regression tests for keep/abort/wait. Thanks again for the thorough report and root-cause analysis.

issue.title: [Test][MRV2] Cover draftless thinking-budget row mapping

labels.name: repo-5faa5e07
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V1 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

issue.body:
Refs #59272.

## Summary

Replaces the original Model Runner V1 patch with Model Runner V2 coverage, as requested in review.

Model Runner V2 does not use the MRV1 `cu_num_tokens` dictionary that caused every request to map to row 0 on a draft-less speculative step. Its no-draft path sets `expanded_idx_mapping == idx_mapping`, giving each request one logits row, and `ThinkingBudgetState` applies forcing through that explicit row-to-request mapping.

This PR adds a two-request GPU regression test that reproduces the important boundary condition: both requests have exhausted their thinking budgets, the speculative step has no drafts, and both corresponding logits rows must independently force the reasoning end token. This protects the V2 invariant against the cross-request row corruption described in #59272.

## Why there is no implementation change

The reported failure is specific to the deprecated MRV1 layout calculation. The equivalent V2 path already has the correct mapping, so carrying the MRV1 fix forward would change a non-default runner without addressing the maintainer's request. The updated PR tests the supported implementation instead of claiming a V2 bug that is not present.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- The test is in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py` and requires CUDA/Triton; it could not be executed in the current macOS CPU-only environment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this update. The final diff and the V2 sampling/mapping path were reviewed before pushing.
