issue.title: [Bug] Client-declared mm_hashes controls multimodal prefix-cache identity: wrong-image KV reuse and cross-tenant image disclosure
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On multimodal deployments, the native `/generate` endpoint accepts a `mm_hashes` field: one hex string per image item, declared by the caller. In `tokenizer_manager.py` the caller value is applied directly to the item (`item.set_hash(int(hex_hash, 16))`), which short-circuits the internal content-based `hash_feature()` recompute. The comment there explains the intent: let an external KV router's routing decision agree with sglang's prefix-cache key for the same image.

In `schedule_batch.py`, `MultimodalDataItem.hash` determines the item's `pad_value`, and the image region of the token sequence is that pad value repeated. So the declared hash is the prefix-cache identity of the image segment: two requests whose items carry the same `mm_hashes` value produce matching token sequences for the image region, and the second request hits the first one's cached KV regardless of the actual image bytes.

The observable bug: a request that sends image B but declares a hash that was previously used for image A gets A's cached KV, and the model answers based on A. B's actual pixels are ignored. The response is a normal completion — no warning, no error, `finish_reason` is a regular stop. In our runs the third request below returned the first image's text with `cached_tokens` jumping from 15 to 193 (the 162-token image region served from cache), and completed faster than the uncached baselines.

Two notes on scope: the field has no flag gating or allowlist, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoints do not expose it, so this is native `/generate` only. Also, the Kimi embedding path already treats this as something to prevent — it rejects caller `mm_hashes` from redirecting cache identity (PR #34411) — while the generic path applies the caller value unconditionally.

### Reproduction

Tested with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct. Prepare two same-size images (512x256): image A, white background with black text `IMAGE-A-SECRET-7f3a9c`; image B, black background with white text `IMAGE-B-DISTRACT-2c1b4d`. The prompt text must be byte-identical across the three calls and must place the vision placeholder inside the model's chat template (`<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` for Qwen2.5-VL).

```python
import base64, requests

def gen(path, mm_hash):
    img = base64.b64encode(open(path, "rb").read()).decode()
    r = requests.post("http://<host>:8200/generate", json={
        "text": "<|im_start|>user\n<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>\n"
                "describe the image and transcribe all text in it<|im_end|>\n"
                "<|im_start|>assistant\n",
        "image_data": [img],
        "mm_hashes": [mm_hash],
        "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0},
    }, timeout=60)
    j = r.json()
    return j["text"], j["meta_info"]["cached_tokens"]

print(gen("A.png", "deadbeef00000001"))  # "IMAGE-A-SECRET-7f3a9c ...", cached_tokens 15
print(gen("B.png", "aaaa0000bbbb0002"))  # "IMAGE-B-DISTRACT-2c1b4d ...", cached_tokens 15
print(gen("B.png", "deadbeef00000001"))  # "IMAGE-A-SECRET-7f3a9c ...", cached_tokens 193
```

The third request sends image B but transcribes `IMAGE-A-SECRET-7f3a9c`, the content of the image cached under the declared hash. Swapping the roles (cache B first, then send A with the same hash) returns B's content the same way. Reproduced on 3/3 cold restarts.

The radix cache is shared across clients, so the aliasing is not limited to one connection: in a two-host check, a second client sending a plain gray image with the same declared hash received the first client's image content in the response (`cached_tokens` 190).

### Environment

SGLang at commit `b8a6adadfe8c292fbb673291dbd2a5d23232f500`, unmodified
Model: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, single RTX 4090
Launch: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8200 --disable-cuda-graph -attention-backend triton --mm-attention-backend triton_attn`
Linux, Python 3.10

comment.body:
I've opened a PR with the fix: #44653.

Caller-declared `mm_hashes` are now only honored when the server is launched with the new opt-in flag `--trust-caller-mm-hashes`; by default they're ignored and the content-based hash is recomputed, so a declared hash can no longer hijack another image's prefix-cache identity. The external-KV-router use case is preserved when the flag is set. The PR includes unit-level before/after verification (no GPU available here, so I verified the exact code paths with mock multimodal items) plus new regression tests — happy to run the Qwen2.5-VL end-to-end reproducer if you'd like it confirmed on GPU.

issue.title: [Bug] Preserve tool `title` in persistence and include it in streaming events
issue.body:
### Description

The `@tool` decorator supports a human-readable `title` for MCP tools. However, the configured title is currently not preserved when tool information is stored in the database, and it is not included in streaming event payloads.

This makes it difficult for AgentOS clients to display a friendly tool title. They must fall back to the technical tool/function name instead.

### Steps to Reproduce

agentos-->team

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

- The configured title is not persisted in the database.
- Streaming tool-related events do not include the tool title.
- AgentOS clients therefore cannot reliably display a human-friendly tool label during execution.

### Actual Behavior

issue.title: [Bug]: code-interpreter-js readLines is O(n²) on long output lines and blocks the event loop
issue.body:
### Sandbox ID or Build ID

N/A (client-side SDK bug, not specific to one sandbox)

### Environment

`@e2b/code-interpreter` 2.6.0 in production; also reproduced against `packages/code-interpreter-js/src/utils.ts` on `main` (2.9.0). Node 22.

### Timestamp of the issue

2026-10-09 22:25 UTC (first seen in production; reproducible at any time)

### Frequency

Happens every time

### Expected behavior

`runCode` takes time proportional to output size, so a long single-line output (base64 image, wide DataFrame, large JSON) doesn't block the caller's event loop.

### Actual behavior

`readLines` appends each chunk to the buffer (`buffer += decoder.decode(...)`) and then searches the whole buffer with `buffer.indexOf('\n')`. When a line has no newline, V8 has to rebuild the entire buffer into one string on every chunk, so the total cost grows with the square of the line length. All of that runs synchronously on the caller's main thread. In production, a single cell printing one ~40 MB line stalled our Node process's event loop for several seconds and added about 2 GB of memory.

### Issue reproduction

Copy `readLines` from `utils.ts` and feed it one newline-free line in 16 KB chunks:

```js
const CHUNK = 16 * 1024
for (const mb of [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]) {
  const chunk = new Uint8Array(CHUNK).fill(97); const n = (mb * 1024 * 1024) / CHUNK; let k = 0
  const stream = new ReadableStream({ pull(c) { k < n ? (c.enqueue(chunk), k++) : c.close() } })
  const t = performance.now(); for await (const _ of readLines(stream)) {}
  console.log(`${mb} MB: ${(performance.now() - t).toFixed(0)} ms`)
}
```

| Line size | Time |
|---|---|
| 1 MB | 8 ms |
| 2 MB | 20 ms |
| 4 MB | 76 ms |
| 8 MB | 263 ms |
| 16 MB | 1,153 ms |
| 32 MB | 5,152 ms |

### Additional context

This is e2b-dev/code-interpreter#251 (ENG-3808). That issue got stranded when the SDK moved into this monorepo in #1768, and the fix PR there (e2b-dev/code-interpreter#308) now conflicts with a deleted file. #1946 fixed UTF-8 decoding across chunks but kept the quadratic buffering. The fix proposed in #251 should work: search only the new chunk for `\n`, keep the partial pieces in an array, and `join` once per complete line. It also needs to keep #1946's streaming `TextDecoder`. We're running a patch like this on 2.6.0, and it handles 40 MB single-line output without stalling.

comment.body: I'd like to take this one. The O(n²) in `readLines` looks like a bounded fix (decode only the new chunk, search for `\n` in the new chunk, accumulate line fragments and join once per line). I'll reproduce with a benchmark first, fix JS + the equivalent Python sync/async paths, and open a PR with before/after numbers. Thanks for the detailed report!

issue.title: [Bug] NIXL PD abort can leave all default transfer workers waiting on healthy non-terminal handles
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, aborting a request after its KV transfer handles have been submitted does not cancel or bound the prefill transfer worker's wait for a handle that remains healthy but non-terminal (`PROC`).

The wait policy in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` is:

```python
deadline = time.time() + NIXL_ERR_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_S if failure_seen else None
while True:
    ...
    if all_settled:
        return True, any_failed
    if not any_failed:
        time.sleep(0)
        continue
```

Thus, a batch is bounded only after an `ERR` is observed. If every handle remains `PROC`, the deadline stays `None`.

The prefill worker calls this with `failure_seen=False` after submitting handles:

```python
settled, any_failed = self._await_handles(handles, failure_seen=False)
```

An externally triggered decode-to-prefill abort notification then runs:

```python
self.record_failure(room_to_be_aborted, ...)
self.update_status(room_to_be_aborted, KVPoll.Failed)
...
self._handle_deferred_abort_ack(notification)
```

This changes the room status and registers a deferred ACK target, but it does not cancel the submitted NIXL handles and does not interrupt a worker already inside `_await_handles()`.

The room was counted before this wait:

```python
if not kv_chunk.staging_counted:
    self._staging_outstanding[room] += 1
    kv_chunk.staging_counted = True
```

The count is decremented and the deferred ACK is sent only after the handles reach a terminal state. Consequently, a healthy but permanently non-terminal handle leaves:

- one transfer worker alive but blocked;
- `_staging_outstanding[room] == 1`;
- the deferred abort ACK unsent.

The default worker count is four:

```python
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE = EnvInt(4)
```

Four aborted rooms with non-terminal handles can therefore consume all default prefill transfer workers.

This is not a claim that every ordinary abort leaks memory or KV blocks. Prefill scheduler failure paths can release request resources independently. The specific defect is that abort does not terminate the transfer-worker lifetime, room staging accounting, or deferred ACK lifecycle when the underlying NIXL handle remains `PROC`.


### Reproduction

The following deterministic reproduction exercises the production abort-notification handling and `_await_handles()` with a fake NIXL agent whose submitted handle remains healthy but non-terminal. It does not depend on GPU RDMA and does not modify live services.

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from threading import Event, Thread
from time import sleep
from types import SimpleNamespace

from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base.conn import KVPoll
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.conn import AbortNotification
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.nixl.conn import NixlKVManager

ROOM = 90210
HANDLE = object()


class FakeAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = "PROC"
        self.reads = 0

    def check_xfer_state(self, handle):
        self.reads += 1
        return self.state


def make_manager(agent):
    manager = NixlKVManager.__new__(NixlKVManager)
    manager.agent = agent
    manager.request_status = {ROOM: KVPoll.WaitingForInput}
    manager.req_to_decode_prefix_len = {}
    manager.transfer_infos = {}
    manager.exceptions = {}
    manager._staging_outstanding = defaultdict(int)
    manager._deferred_ack_targets = {}
    manager._deferred_ack_poisoned_rooms = set()
    manager.enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = True
    manager.enable_staging = False
    manager._staging_ctx = None
    manager.failure_events = []
    manager.sent_acks = []
    manager.update_status = lambda room, status: manager.request_status.__setitem__(room, status)
    manager.record_failure = lambda room, reason: manager.failure_events.append((room, reason))
    manager._send_abort_ack = lambda room, target: manager.sent_acks.append((room, target))
    manager._reload_invalidated_peers = lambda infos: None
    manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM] = 1
    return manager


agent = FakeAgent()
manager = make_manager(agent)
entered = Event()
returned = Event()
result = {}


def wait_for_handle():
    entered.set()
    result["value"] = manager._await_handles([HANDLE], failure_seen=False)
    returned.set()


thread = Thread(target=wait_for_handle, daemon=True)
thread.start()
assert entered.wait(1)
sleep(0.1)
reads_before_abort = agent.reads

abort_message = AbortNotification(
    room=ROOM,
    decode_ip="127.0.0.1",
    decode_port=54321,
    generation=7,
).to_zmq()
assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message)
assert manager.request_status[ROOM] == KVPoll.Failed

sleep(0.2)
print({
    "state_after_abort": agent.state,
    "waiter_alive_after_abort": thread.is_alive(),
    "reads_before_abort": reads_before_abort,
    "reads_after_abort": agent.reads,
    "outstanding_after_abort": manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM],
    "abort_ack_sent_after_abort": bool(manager.sent_acks),
})

# Control: a terminal state immediately wakes this direct waiter.
agent.state = "DONE"
# This direct helper call does not itself perform worker accounting; the full
# transfer_worker() cleanup is covered by the four-worker result below.
assert returned.wait(3)
thread.join(1)
print({
    "control_state": agent.state,
    "control_return": result["value"],
    "direct_helper_outstanding": manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM],
    "direct_helper_ack_sent": bool(manager.sent_acks),
})
```

Observed on commit `51686cf8e7fee0ae773c5c9b8ede356507abef7b`:

```text
{
  'state_after_abort': 'PROC',
  'waiter_alive_after_abort': True,
  'reads_before_abort': 3213,
  'reads_after_abort': 11213,
  'outstanding_after_abort': 1,
  'abort_ack_sent_after_abort': False
}
{
  'control_state': 'DONE',
  'control_return': (True, False),
  'direct_helper_outstanding': 1,
  'direct_helper_ack_sent': False
}
```

A four-room variant using four queues and four workers produced:

```text
workers_alive_after_abort: 4
rooms_retained_after_abort: {91001: 1, 91002: 1, 91003: 1, 91004: 1}
abort_acks_sent_after_abort: 0

control_state: DONE
control_abort_acks_sent: 4
control_rooms_retained: {91001: 0, 91002: 0, 91003: 0, 91004: 0}
```

We also verified external API reachability with an isolated one-prefill/one-decode NIXL deployment. A streaming `/generate` request was submitted through the router, then `/abort_request` was called on both engine HTTP faces. Logs showed:

```text
# decode
Abort transfer queue request. decode_req.req.rid='audit-nixl-abort-001'
Sent abort notification for room 6899418207677453155 ...

# prefill
POST /abort_request HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
Prefill bootstrap failed ... Aborted by AbortReq.
Received abort notification for room 6899418207677453155, marked as Failed
```

That live test did not inject a network fault, so its handles terminated normally; it validates reachability rather than permanent exhaustion.

A normal API-key holder can also enter the abort lifecycle without the explicit admin endpoint. The engine checks `request.is_disconnected()` in non-streaming request paths and calls `abort_request(rid)`, while streaming responses use `create_abort_task()`. The current PD router runs the prefill/decode futures in the request handler task and explicitly propagates client disconnect as upstream cancellation. Therefore, configuring `admin-api-key` does not remove the disconnect-triggered path; it only restricts explicit `/abort_request` calls when both keys are configured.

### Evidence

Source audit on `51686cf8e7fee0ae773c5c9b8ede356507abef7b`:

- `NixlKVManager._await_handles()` is unbounded while all handles are healthy.
- `transfer_worker()` enters that wait after submitting all handles.
- `_handle_abort_notification()` only records failure, sets `KVPoll.Failed`, and registers the deferred ACK target.
- `_staging_outstanding[room]` is incremented before the wait and decremented only after terminal handles.
- deferred abort ACK is sent only after the outstanding count drains.
- `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` defaults to `4`.
- deferred decode KV release defaults to enabled with a 30-second timeout, but that timeout does not wake or clean up the prefill worker.

Dynamic evidence:

- Single-worker deterministic injection: waiter remains alive after abort, handle-state polling continues, outstanding count remains 1, no ACK is sent; `DONE` restores cleanup.
- Four-worker deterministic injection: all four workers remain alive, all four room counts remain 1, no ACK is sent; `DONE` wakes all workers and sends four ACKs.
- Isolated 1P+1D NIXL runtime test: external `/abort_request` reaches decode-side transfer abort and the prefill-side room notification handler.
- Router/engine source confirms ordinary API-key request creation plus client disconnect can enter automatic abort handling.

Not claimed as dynamically reproduced:

- a real UCX/NIXL network partition that keeps a submitted handle in `PROC` forever;
- permanent P-side KV-block retention;
- confidentiality or integrity impact from KV-page reuse after prefill-side release.

Those remain conditional follow-up scenarios. The confirmed defect is the abort lifecycle's inability to reclaim transfer workers and staging accounting while a healthy non-terminal handle persists.

### Impact

**Availability: High**

### Environment

```
$ docker exec sglang-v0519-prefill-134 python3 -m sglang.check_env
Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jul 15 2026, 23:46:41) [GCC 13.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe
GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.0
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88
CUDA Driver Version: 590.48.01
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: 0.5.19
sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18
flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.18
flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.18+cu130
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.12.1
numpy: 2.3.5
aiohttp: 3.14.3
fastapi: 0.141.1
huggingface_hub: 1.30.0
modelscope: 1.39.1
orjson: 3.12.0
pydantic: 2.13.5
python-multipart: 0.0.32

It bounds the prefill transfer worker's wait when the room is aborted mid-transfer and releases the staging count plus the deferred abort ACK. The PR description includes a GPU-free reproducer with before/after output. Would appreciate your review when you have a moment.

issue.title: fix(reading-order): bound page-separator candidate work and honor document_timeout
issue.body:
Fixes #4632.

## Root cause

`build_page_separators` (introduced in #4276) turns every thin vector shape on a page into a separator candidate, then runs `_merge_separator_candidates` — a fixpoint loop whose single pass is quadratic in the candidate count. A page with dense vector geometry (the reporter's venue seat map: tens of thousands of tiny rectangles) yields tens of thousands of candidates, nearly all too short to ever become separators, and the merge never finishes in practice. Measured on synthetic input: 2,000 candidates take 0.74s per pass, 4,000 take 2.75s (quadratic); the merge runs before the length filter that would discard all of them.

Separately, `document_timeout` was only enforced between page batches in `_build_document`. The assembly stage (`_assemble_document` → reading order) had no timeout checkpoint, so the runaway merge blocked the whole conversion forever.

## Changes

- `docling/models/postprocessing/reading_order_rb.py`
  - Skip separator extraction for a page when the raw candidate count exceeds `_MAX_SEPARATOR_CANDIDATES` (5000), with a warning. Reading order falls back to the pre-separator behavior for that page.
  - `build_page_separators(..., time_limit_s)` and a deadline in `_merge_separator_candidates`: candidate collection and the merge fixpoint abort to "no separators" once the budget is exhausted. A partial merge is never returned — an aborted fixpoint could leave overlapping zero-height rules that reintroduce the ordering-graph cycle #4276 fixed.
- `docling/models/stages/reading_order/readingorder_model.py`
  - `ReadingOrderModel.__call__(..., time_budget_s)`: passes the remaining per-page budget into separator extraction; records a `TIMEOUT` `ErrorItem` (component `DOC_ASSEMBLER`) when the budget is exceeded, so the result reports `PARTIAL_SUCCESS` per the documented `document_timeout` contract.
- `docling/datamodel/document.py`: `ConversionResult._conversion_deadline` (private, transient, same rationale as `_page_sizes_by_no` — the pipeline instance is shared across conversions).
- `docling/pipeline/standard_pdf_pipeline.py`: `_build_document` records the absolute deadline from `document_timeout`; `_assemble_document` passes the remaining budget to the reading-order model.

## Invariants preserved

- When `document_timeout` is unset or candidates stay below the cap, behavior is byte-identical to before (new parameters default to no-limit).
- Short fragments still merge into long rules (existing fragment tests unchanged; new test covers merging at moderate scale below the cap).

## Tests

- New in `tests/test_reading_order.py`: degenerate candidate count is skipped quickly (6,000 tiny rects → `[]` in well under a second), exhausted time budget aborts immediately (`time_limit_s` 0/negative), and fragment merging still works below the cap.
- `tests/test_reading_order.py` + `tests/test_reading_order_pdf_snapshots.py`: 34 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing CI-gated skip). `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files.
- Repro for the reported scenario (37,744 thin-rect candidates): `build_page_separators` now returns in ~0.4s instead of hanging.

comment.body: Hi @PeterStaar-IBM — a gentle follow-up on this one. The PR bounds the page-separator candidate work in the reading-order pipeline (building on the algorithm your #4276 updated) and honors `document_timeout`, with regression tests added in `tests/test_reading_order.py`. CI is fully green, DCO is signed, and mergify merge protections are satisfied. Would appreciate your review when you have a moment — thank you!

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

`allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B` cannot be loaded with default settings. During weight loading, the GDN layer's fused conv1d weight loader unconditionally indexes a per-section dimension list with `loaded_shard_id`, but that parameter's default value is `None`:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py
def _make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader(dims, tp_size, tp_rank):
    """Weight loader for loading separate HF conv weights into a fused conv1d.

    dims: list of original (un-sharded) dims per section,
          e.g. [key_dim, key_dim, value_dim]
    """
    sharded_dims = [d // tp_size for d in dims]

    def weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, loaded_shard_id=None):
        if loaded_weight.dim() == 2:
            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.unsqueeze(1)
        dim = dims[loaded_shard_id]        # <-- None when the caller does not pass a shard id
        shard_size = dim // tp_size
        tp_start = tp_rank * shard_size
        sharded_weight = loaded_weight[tp_start : tp_start + shard_size]
        offset = sum(sharded_dims[:loaded_shard_id])
        param.data[offset : offset + shard_size].copy_(sharded_weight)

    return weight_loader
```

The loader is registered with `set_weight_loader`/auto-loading, which invokes it **without** `loaded_shard_id`, so it raises immediately:

```
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not NoneType
```

The user-visible symptom is only `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`; the real cause is buried in EngineCore stderr. The message also gives no indication of which weight or which section was being loaded.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(model="allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B", max_model_len=4096, seed=42,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.85)      # no other arguments at all
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

The model loads. If the checkpoint genuinely cannot be mapped to the fused conv1d layout, the loader should fail with an actionable message naming the parameter and the expected shard ids, e.g.:

```
ValueError: cannot load conv1d weight '<param>' without loaded_shard_id;
expected one of {0: key_dim, 1: key_dim, 2: value_dim}
```

## Actual behavior

Model init → `initialize_model` → `load_model` → `default_loader.load_weights` → `olmo_hybrid.py:480` / `:379` → `utils.py:_load_param` → `olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py:517` → `TypeError`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89), 47.4 GiB
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B`

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore stderr)

```text
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 545, in load_model
  self.model_runner.load_model(load_dummy_weights=load_dummy_weights)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/model_loader/base_loader.py", line 75, in load_model
  self.load_weights(model, model_config)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py", line 481, in load_weights
  loaded_weights = model.load_weights(self.get_all_weights(model_config, model))
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/olmo_hybrid.py", line 480, in load_weights
  return loader.load_weights(weights)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 460, in load_weights
  autoloaded_weights = set(self._load_module("", self.module, weights))
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 325, in _load_param
  weight_loader(param, weight_data)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py", line 517, in weight_loader
  dim = dims[loaded_shard_id]
        ~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not NoneType
```

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator (the point happened to carry `mamba_cache_dtype` variants), then isolated standalone: **default arguments alone reproduce it**, so this is not a flag combination issue. 2/2 attempts, identical stack.
- Impact: the model is effectively unusable on this build. Any stack that uses the `olmo_gdn_linear_attn` fused conv1d loader and relies on auto-loading (rather than passing explicit shard ids) hits the same `None`.
- Line-number caveat: the traceback line numbers above are from the installed 0.31.0 wheel; the function body is quoted from the matching source tree so the defect is identifiable regardless of minor line drift.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
Thanks again for the detailed report — a quick update from my side. While preparing the fix I found that open PR #55858 (opened 2026-09-08, before this issue was filed) already addresses exactly this bug with the same approach: recovering the shard id from the mapped weight tensor when it isn't passed explicitly, with a regression test covering the `AutoWeightsLoader` path.

To avoid a duplicate PR I'll withdraw my claim here and step back — the review there is already underway with TP=1/TP=2 H200 validation reported by the author. Happy to help review or test there if maintainers want an extra pair of eyes.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

`allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B` cannot be loaded with default settings. During weight loading, the GDN layer's fused conv1d weight loader unconditionally indexes a per-section dimension list with `loaded_shard_id`, but that parameter's default value is `None`:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py
def _make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader(dims, tp_size, tp_rank):
    """Weight loader for loading separate HF conv weights into a fused conv1d.

    dims: list of original (un-sharded) dims per section,
          e.g. [key_dim, key_dim, value_dim]
    """
    sharded_dims = [d // tp_size for d in dims]

    def weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, loaded_shard_id=None):
        if loaded_weight.dim() == 2:
            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.unsqueeze(1)
        dim = dims[loaded_shard_id]        # <-- None when the caller does not pass a shard id
        shard_size = dim // tp_size
        tp_start = tp_rank * shard_size
        sharded_weight = loaded_weight[tp_start : tp_start + shard_size]
        offset = sum(sharded_dims[:loaded_shard_id])
        param.data[offset : offset + shard_size].copy_(sharded_weight)

    return weight_loader
```

The loader is registered with `set_weight_loader`/auto-loading, which invokes it **without** `loaded_shard_id`, so it raises immediately:

```
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not NoneType
```

The user-visible symptom is only `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`; the real cause is buried in EngineCore stderr. The message also gives no indication of which weight or which section was being loaded.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(model="allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B", max_model_len=4096, seed=42,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.85)      # no other arguments at all
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

The model loads. If the checkpoint genuinely cannot be mapped to the fused conv1d layout, the loader should fail with an actionable message naming the parameter and the expected shard ids, e.g.:

```
ValueError: cannot load conv1d weight '<param>' without loaded_shard_id;
expected one of {0: key_dim, 1: key_dim, 2: value_dim}
```

## Actual behavior

Model init → `initialize_model` → `load_model` → `default_loader.load_weights` → `olmo_hybrid.py:480` / `:379` → `utils.py:_load_param` → `olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py:517` → `TypeError`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89), 47.4 GiB
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B`

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore stderr)

```text
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 545, in load_model
  self.model_runner.load_model(load_dummy_weights=load_dummy_weights)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/model_loader/base_loader.py", line 75, in load_model
  self.load_weights(model, model_config)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py", line 481, in load_weights
  loaded_weights = model.load_weights(self.get_all_weights(model_config, model))
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/olmo_hybrid.py", line 480, in load_weights
  return loader.load_weights(weights)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 460, in load_weights
  autoloaded_weights = set(self._load_module("", self.module, weights))
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py", line 325, in _load_param
  weight_loader(param, weight_data)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py", line 517, in weight_loader
  dim = dims[loaded_shard_id]
        ~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not NoneType
```

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator (the point happened to carry `mamba_cache_dtype` variants), then isolated standalone: **default arguments alone reproduce it**, so this is not a flag combination issue. 2/2 attempts, identical stack.
- Impact: the model is effectively unusable on this build. Any stack that uses the `olmo_gdn_linear_attn` fused conv1d loader and relies on auto-loading (rather than passing explicit shard ids) hits the same `None`.
- Line-number caveat: the traceback line numbers above are from the installed 0.31.0 wheel; the function body is quoted from the matching source tree so the defect is identifiable regardless of minor line drift.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and reproducer!

I'd like to take this one. The root cause is in `_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py`): the `WeightsMapper` hands the shard id (0/1/2 for q/k/v conv1d) to the auto-loader as a tensor attribute (`shard_id` on the loaded weight), but the inner `weight_loader` only reads its explicit `loaded_shard_id` argument, which `_load_param` never passes — so it arrives as `None` and `dims[None]` blows up.

The fix: have the loader fall back to `getattr(loaded_weight, "shard_id", None)` (the same pattern other fused loaders in `vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py` already use), and raise an actionable error naming the valid shard ids when neither source provides one. I'll put up a PR shortly.

The fix is up: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61808 — the non-inplace `final_state` is now allocated with `N * T` rows to match the kernel's per-token `(bos + i_t)` write pattern (and the per-token `h0` load indexing).

issue.title: Fix symbolic Decimal coefficient pinned to "0" (follow-up to #448)
issue.body:
Follow-up to #448 (and #460).

#460 fixed the coefficient digits being drawn from the wrong range (ASCII codepoints instead of digit values), which was the main cause of symbolic Decimals collapsing to zero. However, the coefficient still materializes as a concrete `"0"`: `_make_decimal` routes the digits through `Decimal`'s tuple constructor, whose digit loop (`for digit in value[1]`) cannot enumerate a symbolic-length tuple, so `digits` is always empty and `_int` becomes `"0"`.

This change builds the proxy directly (the same pattern `_dec_from_triple` uses) with a symbolic digit string constrained to the model's invariant (at least one digit, no leading zeros), and bounds a symbolic exponent to the default context's `[Emin, Emax]`.

Before: `crosshair check` on `post: a != Decimal("2")` reports "Not confirmed".
After: it finds a concrete counterexample (`f(Decimal('2.0'))`).

- `decimallib_test.py` + `decimallib_ch_test.py`: 13/13 pass (`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`).
- New regression test `test_symbolic_decimal_reaches_nonzero_coefficients` fails without the fix and passes with it.

comment.body: Hi @pschanely — just a friendly check-in on this follow-up PR to #448. No rush at all; if a fuller reproducer or more context on the symbolic Decimal coefficient behavior would help, I'm happy to provide it. Thanks for taking a look!

issue.title: [Bug] Hybrid attention models can fail to start with speculative decoding and --disable-radix-cache
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Adding `--disable-radix-cache` can make a hybrid model that works with speculative
decoding fail while setting up its caches. This happens when the target and draft
weights fit, but the default state-cache size exceeds the memory left for caches.
Hybrid models mix standard attention with layers such as Mamba or gated delta
networks, which also need memory to store their state.

I reproduced this on SGLang v0.5.21 with
`Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` on a DGX Spark with one GB10.
It should also reproduce on any supported hardware with hybrid models that use
the same state-cache sizing code, if the target and draft weights fit but leave
too little memory for the saved state and temporary draft state of the default
48 requests.

The runs below show the failure when radix caching is disabled and the workaround
of setting a smaller request limit. Only the last run sets `--max-running-requests`:

| Mode | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Target model only, radix caching enabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and a test chat returns the correct answer. |
| Target model only, radix caching disabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and all eight test chats return the correct answers. |
| NEXTN, five steps, radix caching enabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and a test chat returns the correct answer. |
| Same NEXTN command, with only `--disable-radix-cache` added | Startup fails after both target and draft weights load. |
| Failing command plus `--max-running-requests 10` | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and all eight test chats return the correct answers. |

The target-only runs work with either radix setting. With speculative decoding
enabled and radix caching disabled, the server loads both the target and draft
weights successfully, then fails during cache sizing with the following error:

```text
ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=0.82. Raise --mem-fraction-static above 0.686 (minimum viable = 1 - available/pre = 0.6853). If using speculative decoding, draft weights are now counted.
```

The suggested fix is confusing because the command already uses
`--mem-fraction-static 0.82`, above the suggested minimum of `0.686`. Both sets
of weights fit. The failure happens when SGLang then reserves too much memory
for the state cache, leaving none for the KV cache used by attention layers.

I would expect SGLang to choose a default state-cache size that fits the available
memory and leaves room for the KV cache, without needing an explicit request limit.

The cause appears to be in `KVCacheConfigurator._handle_max_mamba_cache`.
For these speculative runs, SGLang sets `--max-running-requests` to 48 when it
is omitted. With radix caching disabled, the cache planner treats that default
as a limit chosen by the user and sizes the state pool around it. For Qwen's
default FP32 state and six draft tokens, the saved state and temporary draft
state together need about 24.68 GiB.

Without speculative decoding, `--max-running-requests` stays unset, so the
planner fits the state cache to the available memory even with radix caching
disabled. There are also no draft weights or temporary draft states to reserve.
The target-only, radix-disabled run gets an effective limit of 114 requests;
that is calculated from the available memory, not a fixed default.

With speculative decoding and radix caching enabled, the planner fits the
state pool to the available memory. That Qwen run gets 41 state slots,
allows eight active requests, and serves successfully.

This has also been reproduced with other models that use the same state-cache
sizing code.

The GPU tests described here were run on a GB10.

Related reports:

- [#38846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38846) discusses showing
  the actual request limit after it is reduced to fit the state cache.
- [#24364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24364) reports running out
  of memory while allocating hybrid state on WSL2, including runs with explicit
  request limits. In this report, the failure occurs with the automatic limit.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on both v0.5.21 and main. I tested main at commit
`3a9cae27edec392ff8cc9f09d1164f557c653f42` with the dependencies required by that commit.

The following command reproduces the failure. I tested it on one GB10 using
the unmodified `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` image:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --revision c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

Removing only `--disable-radix-cache` makes the command
work. Leave `--max-running-requests` unset in both cases. To try the workaround, keep
`--disable-radix-cache` and add `--max-running-requests 10`.

Removing the three `--speculative-*` options also makes the command work,
with radix caching still disabled and `--max-running-requests` still unset.

### Environment

The environment below is from the v0.5.21 image used for these tests.
I also reproduced the failure on main at the commit listed under Reproduction,
using PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, Transformers 5.19.0, and
FlashInfer 0.7.1.

Recorded `check_env` output from v0.5.21:

```text

comment.body: I've opened a fix in #44375: with `--disable-radix-cache`, the mamba state pool is now only sized from `--max-running-requests` when the flag was explicitly passed. The speculative-decoding auto-default (48) falls through to the existing ratio-based auto-fit, so the state pool fits the available memory and leaves room for the attention KV cache — matching the radix-enabled path. An explicit `--max-running-requests` (e.g. the `--max-running-requests 10` workaround) still sizes the pool directly. Thanks again for the thorough root-cause analysis — it made the fix straightforward to verify.

issue.title: [Bug] NIXL PD abort can leave all default transfer workers waiting on healthy non-terminal handles
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, aborting a request after its KV transfer handles have been submitted does not cancel or bound the prefill transfer worker's wait for a handle that remains healthy but non-terminal (`PROC`).

The wait policy in `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` is:

```python
deadline = time.time() + NIXL_ERR_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_S if failure_seen else None
while True:
    ...
    if all_settled:
        return True, any_failed
    if not any_failed:
        time.sleep(0)
        continue
```

Thus, a batch is bounded only after an `ERR` is observed. If every handle remains `PROC`, the deadline stays `None`.

The prefill worker calls this with `failure_seen=False` after submitting handles:

```python
settled, any_failed = self._await_handles(handles, failure_seen=False)
```

An externally triggered decode-to-prefill abort notification then runs:

```python
self.record_failure(room_to_be_aborted, ...)
self.update_status(room_to_be_aborted, KVPoll.Failed)
...
self._handle_deferred_abort_ack(notification)
```

This changes the room status and registers a deferred ACK target, but it does not cancel the submitted NIXL handles and does not interrupt a worker already inside `_await_handles()`.

The room was counted before this wait:

```python
if not kv_chunk.staging_counted:
    self._staging_outstanding[room] += 1
    kv_chunk.staging_counted = True
```

The count is decremented and the deferred ACK is sent only after the handles reach a terminal state. Consequently, a healthy but permanently non-terminal handle leaves:

- one transfer worker alive but blocked;
- `_staging_outstanding[room] == 1`;
- the deferred abort ACK unsent.

The default worker count is four:

```python
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE = EnvInt(4)
```

Four aborted rooms with non-terminal handles can therefore consume all default prefill transfer workers.

This is not a claim that every ordinary abort leaks memory or KV blocks. Prefill scheduler failure paths can release request resources independently. The specific defect is that abort does not terminate the transfer-worker lifetime, room staging accounting, or deferred ACK lifecycle when the underlying NIXL handle remains `PROC`.


### Reproduction

The following deterministic reproduction exercises the production abort-notification handling and `_await_handles()` with a fake NIXL agent whose submitted handle remains healthy but non-terminal. It does not depend on GPU RDMA and does not modify live services.

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from threading import Event, Thread
from time import sleep
from types import SimpleNamespace

from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base.conn import KVPoll
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.conn import AbortNotification
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.nixl.conn import NixlKVManager

ROOM = 90210
HANDLE = object()


class FakeAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = "PROC"
        self.reads = 0

    def check_xfer_state(self, handle):
        self.reads += 1
        return self.state


def make_manager(agent):
    manager = NixlKVManager.__new__(NixlKVManager)
    manager.agent = agent
    manager.request_status = {ROOM: KVPoll.WaitingForInput}
    manager.req_to_decode_prefix_len = {}
    manager.transfer_infos = {}
    manager.exceptions = {}
    manager._staging_outstanding = defaultdict(int)
    manager._deferred_ack_targets = {}
    manager._deferred_ack_poisoned_rooms = set()
    manager.enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = True
    manager.enable_staging = False
    manager._staging_ctx = None
    manager.failure_events = []
    manager.sent_acks = []
    manager.update_status = lambda room, status: manager.request_status.__setitem__(room, status)
    manager.record_failure = lambda room, reason: manager.failure_events.append((room, reason))
    manager._send_abort_ack = lambda room, target: manager.sent_acks.append((room, target))
    manager._reload_invalidated_peers = lambda infos: None
    manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM] = 1
    return manager


agent = FakeAgent()
manager = make_manager(agent)
entered = Event()
returned = Event()
result = {}


def wait_for_handle():
    entered.set()
    result["value"] = manager._await_handles([HANDLE], failure_seen=False)
    returned.set()


thread = Thread(target=wait_for_handle, daemon=True)
thread.start()
assert entered.wait(1)
sleep(0.1)
reads_before_abort = agent.reads

abort_message = AbortNotification(
    room=ROOM,
    decode_ip="127.0.0.1",
    decode_port=54321,
    generation=7,
).to_zmq()
assert manager._handle_abort_notification(abort_message)
assert manager.request_status[ROOM] == KVPoll.Failed

sleep(0.2)
print({
    "state_after_abort": agent.state,
    "waiter_alive_after_abort": thread.is_alive(),
    "reads_before_abort": reads_before_abort,
    "reads_after_abort": agent.reads,
    "outstanding_after_abort": manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM],
    "abort_ack_sent_after_abort": bool(manager.sent_acks),
})

# Control: a terminal state immediately wakes this direct waiter.
agent.state = "DONE"
# This direct helper call does not itself perform worker accounting; the full
# transfer_worker() cleanup is covered by the four-worker result below.
assert returned.wait(3)
thread.join(1)
print({
    "control_state": agent.state,
    "control_return": result["value"],
    "direct_helper_outstanding": manager._staging_outstanding[ROOM],
    "direct_helper_ack_sent": bool(manager.sent_acks),
})
```

Observed on commit `51686cf8e7fee0ae773c5c9b8ede356507abef7b`:

```text
{
  'state_after_abort': 'PROC',
  'waiter_alive_after_abort': True,
  'reads_before_abort': 3213,
  'reads_after_abort': 11213,
  'outstanding_after_abort': 1,
  'abort_ack_sent_after_abort': False
}
{
  'control_state': 'DONE',
  'control_return': (True, False),
  'direct_helper_outstanding': 1,
  'direct_helper_ack_sent': False
}
```

A four-room variant using four queues and four workers produced:

```text
workers_alive_after_abort: 4
rooms_retained_after_abort: {91001: 1, 91002: 1, 91003: 1, 91004: 1}
abort_acks_sent_after_abort: 0

control_state: DONE
control_abort_acks_sent: 4
control_rooms_retained: {91001: 0, 91002: 0, 91003: 0, 91004: 0}
```

We also verified external API reachability with an isolated one-prefill/one-decode NIXL deployment. A streaming `/generate` request was submitted through the router, then `/abort_request` was called on both engine HTTP faces. Logs showed:

```text
# decode
Abort transfer queue request. decode_req.req.rid='audit-nixl-abort-001'
Sent abort notification for room 6899418207677453155 ...

# prefill
POST /abort_request HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
Prefill bootstrap failed ... Aborted by AbortReq.
Received abort notification for room 6899418207677453155, marked as Failed
```

That live test did not inject a network fault, so its handles terminated normally; it validates reachability rather than permanent exhaustion.

A normal API-key holder can also enter the abort lifecycle without the explicit admin endpoint. The engine checks `request.is_disconnected()` in non-streaming request paths and calls `abort_request(rid)`, while streaming responses use `create_abort_task()`. The current PD router runs the prefill/decode futures in the request handler task and explicitly propagates client disconnect as upstream cancellation. Therefore, configuring `admin-api-key` does not remove the disconnect-triggered path; it only restricts explicit `/abort_request` calls when both keys are configured.

### Evidence

Source audit on `51686cf8e7fee0ae773c5c9b8ede356507abef7b`:

- `NixlKVManager._await_handles()` is unbounded while all handles are healthy.
- `transfer_worker()` enters that wait after submitting all handles.
- `_handle_abort_notification()` only records failure, sets `KVPoll.Failed`, and registers the deferred ACK target.
- `_staging_outstanding[room]` is incremented before the wait and decremented only after terminal handles.
- deferred abort ACK is sent only after the outstanding count drains.
- `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` defaults to `4`.
- deferred decode KV release defaults to enabled with a 30-second timeout, but that timeout does not wake or clean up the prefill worker.

Dynamic evidence:

- Single-worker deterministic injection: waiter remains alive after abort, handle-state polling continues, outstanding count remains 1, no ACK is sent; `DONE` restores cleanup.
- Four-worker deterministic injection: all four workers remain alive, all four room counts remain 1, no ACK is sent; `DONE` wakes all workers and sends four ACKs.
- Isolated 1P+1D NIXL runtime test: external `/abort_request` reaches decode-side transfer abort and the prefill-side room notification handler.
- Router/engine source confirms ordinary API-key request creation plus client disconnect can enter automatic abort handling.

Not claimed as dynamically reproduced:

- a real UCX/NIXL network partition that keeps a submitted handle in `PROC` forever;
- permanent P-side KV-block retention;
- confidentiality or integrity impact from KV-page reuse after prefill-side release.

Those remain conditional follow-up scenarios. The confirmed defect is the abort lifecycle's inability to reclaim transfer workers and staging accounting while a healthy non-terminal handle persists.

### Impact

**Availability: High**

### Environment

```
$ docker exec sglang-v0519-prefill-134 python3 -m sglang.check_env
Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jul 15 2026, 23:46:41) [GCC 13.3.0]

GPU 0: NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe

I'd like to take this one. I'll look at bounding `_await_handles()` so an externally triggered abort interrupts the wait and releases the room's staging count plus the deferred abort ACK even when the submitted handle stays healthy but non-terminal, and I'll add a regression test based on your fake-agent repro. issue.title: [Bug] Hybrid attention models can fail to start with speculative decoding and --disable-radix-cache
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Adding `--disable-radix-cache` can make a hybrid model that works with speculative
decoding fail while setting up its caches. This happens when the target and draft
weights fit, but the default state-cache size exceeds the memory left for caches.
Hybrid models mix standard attention with layers such as Mamba or gated delta
networks, which also need memory to store their state.

I reproduced this on SGLang v0.5.21 with
`Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` on a DGX Spark with one GB10.
It should also reproduce on any supported hardware with hybrid models that use
the same state-cache sizing code, if the target and draft weights fit but leave
too little memory for the saved state and temporary draft state of the default
48 requests.

The runs below show the failure when radix caching is disabled and the workaround
of setting a smaller request limit. Only the last run sets `--max-running-requests`:

| Mode | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Target model only, radix caching enabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and a test chat returns the correct answer. |
| Target model only, radix caching disabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and all eight test chats return the correct answers. |
| NEXTN, five steps, radix caching enabled | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and a test chat returns the correct answer. |
| Same NEXTN command, with only `--disable-radix-cache` added | Startup fails after both target and draft weights load. |
| Failing command plus `--max-running-requests 10` | Server starts, health and model-list checks pass, and all eight test chats return the correct answers. |

The target-only runs work with either radix setting. With speculative decoding
enabled and radix caching disabled, the server loads both the target and draft
weights successfully, then fails during cache sizing with the following error:

```text
ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=0.82. Raise --mem-fraction-static above 0.686 (minimum viable = 1 - available/pre = 0.6853). If using speculative decoding, draft weights are now counted.
```

The suggested fix is confusing because the command already uses
`--mem-fraction-static 0.82`, above the suggested minimum of `0.686`. Both sets
of weights fit. The failure happens when SGLang then reserves too much memory
for the state cache, leaving none for the KV cache used by attention layers.

I would expect SGLang to choose a default state-cache size that fits the available
memory and leaves room for the KV cache, without needing an explicit request limit.

The cause appears to be in `KVCacheConfigurator._handle_max_mamba_cache`.
For these speculative runs, SGLang sets `--max-running-requests` to 48 when it
is omitted. With radix caching disabled, the cache planner treats that default
as a limit chosen by the user and sizes the state pool around it. For Qwen's
default FP32 state and six draft tokens, the saved state and temporary draft
state together need about 24.68 GiB.

Without speculative decoding, `--max-running-requests` stays unset, so the
planner fits the state cache to the available memory even with radix caching
disabled. There are also no draft weights or temporary draft states to reserve.
The target-only, radix-disabled run gets an effective limit of 114 requests;
that is calculated from the available memory, not a fixed default.

With speculative decoding and radix caching enabled, the planner fits the
state pool to the available memory. That Qwen run gets 41 state slots,
allows eight active requests, and serves successfully.

This has also been reproduced with other models that use the same state-cache
sizing code.

The GPU tests described here were run on a GB10.

Related reports:

- [#38846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38846) discusses showing
  the actual request limit after it is reduced to fit the state cache.
- [#24364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24364) reports running out
  of memory while allocating hybrid state on WSL2, including runs with explicit
  request limits. In this report, the failure occurs with the automatic limit.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on both v0.5.21 and main. I tested main at commit
`3a9cae27edec392ff8cc9f09d1164f557c653f42` with the dependencies required by that commit.

The following command reproduces the failure. I tested it on one GB10 using
the unmodified `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` image:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --revision c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --disable-radix-cache
```

Removing only `--disable-radix-cache` makes the command
work. Leave `--max-running-requests` unset in both cases. To try the workaround, keep
`--disable-radix-cache` and add `--max-running-requests 10`.

Removing the three `--speculative-*` options also makes the command work,
with radix caching still disabled and `--max-running-requests` still unset.

### Environment

The environment below is from the v0.5.21 image used for these tests.
I also reproduced the failure on main at the commit listed under Reproduction,
using PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, Transformers 5.19.0, and
FlashInfer 0.7.1.

Recorded `check_env` output from v0.5.21:

```text

issue.title: [Bug] Daily run metrics exclude runs from sessions created on previous days
issue.body:
### Description

Daily run metrics in Agno OS appear to be calculated based on the session creation date instead of the actual run execution date.

When a session is created on one day and reused on subsequent days, new runs belonging to that session are not included in the daily metrics for the days on which they actually occurred.

This leads to missing runs, inaccurate token usage statistics, and potentially permanently incomplete historical metrics.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an agent session on Day 1 (e.g., October 10).
2.  Execute one run in that session.
3. On Day 2 (e.g., October 14), reuse the same session_id.
4. Execute two additional runs.
5. Open the Agno OS metrics dashboard and inspect the daily run counts.

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

- October 10: 1 run
- October 14: 2 runs

Total: 3 runs

Each run should be counted on its actual execution date, regardless of when its parent session was created.

### Actual Behavior

- October 10: The initial run is counted.
- October 14: The two additional runs are missing from the daily metrics.

Runs associated with sessions created on October 14 are counted normally.

Depending on when metrics are calculated, the missing runs may either be absent from the aggregated metrics entirely or incorrectly attributed to the original session creation date.

The underlying runs are not necessarily lost from storage. The problem concerns their aggregation into daily metrics.

### Screenshots or Logs (if applicable)

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
- Agno 3.0.11
- PGSQL storage
```

### Possible Solutions (optional)

_No response_

### Additional Context

Suggested fix

- Aggregate runs based on their own execution timestamps, independently of session creation dates.
- Use session records only to resolve metadata such as user_id, agent/team/workflow identifiers, and session type.
- Calculate daily token usage from run-level metrics rather than cumulative session metrics.
- Preserve session creation counts based on session creation dates, while calculating run counts based on run execution dates.
- Provide a way to rebuild historical daily metrics from persisted runs.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report with clear repro steps — this looks like a real bug. I'll take this one and investigate a fix.

issue.title: PY-10-docling: encrypted PDF is indistinguishable from a corrupt PDF with the default docling-parse backend (follow-up of #1920 / #3757)
issue.body:
**Type:** Bug (incomplete fix)
**Component:** `docling/backend/docling_parse_backend.py` (l.332-343 on `ffce1917`) — message originates in `docling-parse`
**Target repo:** `docling-project/docling` (new issue, follow-up of closed #1920; see "Upstream status")
**Upstream status (checked 2026-10-14):** no open issue or PR on this point; #1920 is closed by #3757 (pypdfium2 only). Re-checked on `ffce1917` (2.138.0-16): the `docling-parse` path is unchanged, pypdfium2 `password` at `pypdfium2_backend.py` l.699-705.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| docling (checkout) | 2.138.0-16, commit `ffce1917` |
| docling installed (PyPI) | 2.138.0 (probe output below was produced on 2.135.0-14, behaviour unchanged in the code) |
| docling-parse | 7.22.2 |
| OS / Python | Windows 11 / 3.14 |
| Fixture | `tests/data/pdf_password/sources/2206.01062_pg3.pdf` (upstream fixture; opening password `1234`) |

## Context & Description

Issue #1920 asked that `ConversionError` keep the underlying exception so applications can classify "PDF is encrypted". PR #3757 (merged Jul 13, release 2.113) chains the cause (`document.py` l.112-127, comment: "an encrypted PDF surfaces the underlying `PdfiumError`"; `document_converter.py` l.694-697 `raise ConversionError(...) from get_input_rejection_cause(...)`).

That only holds for the **pypdfium2** backend. The **default** PDF backend is `ThreadedDoclingParseDocumentBackend` (`document_converter.py` l.311). It wraps the native failure as `DocumentLoadError` with the detail of a `RuntimeError` whose text is `Failed to load document with key ...` (`docling_parse_backend.py` l.331-340). The text says nothing about a password, and the exception type is the same as for a corrupt file. A caller cannot tell "needs a password" / "wrong password" from "broken file".

## Evidence

`repro/probe_errors.py` converts the fixture with both backends and prints the `__cause__` chain (output: `output/python-2.135.0-14-probe.txt`):

| Backend | Password | Result | Innermost cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| docling-parse (default) | none | ConversionError | `RuntimeError: Failed to load document with key key=...` |
| docling-parse (default) | wrong (`nope`) | ConversionError | `RuntimeError: Failed to load document with key key=...` (identical) |
| docling-parse (default) | `1234` | OK | — |
| pypdfium2 | none | ConversionError | `PdfiumError: Failed to load document (PDFium: Incorrect password error).` |
| pypdfium2 | wrong | ConversionError | same as above |
| pypdfium2 | `1234` | OK | — |

Other formats do classify it: the iWork backend raises `DocumentLoadError("... is password-protected; Docling cannot read encrypted iWork documents. Remove the password ...")` (`iwork_backend.py` l.254-258).

## Suggested Fix

Either (a) `docling-parse` raises a distinct error / message for encrypted input (e.g. a dedicated exception subclass, or "password required" vs "incorrect password"), 
and the docling wrapper forwards it; or (b) the docling wrapper probes the file when `docling-parse` fails (for example a cheap check of the `/Encrypt` trailer entry) 
and raises `DocumentLoadError` with an explicit "password-protected" message, as the iWork backend already does. Option (a) also gives the required-vs-wrong distinction 
that pypdfium2 does not give either.

## Suggested Tests

- Extend `tests/test_pdf_password.py` (it already has both backends and the fixture): without password and with a wrong password, assert the exception chain or message identifies an encrypted document for **both** backends.

[python-10-docling-parse-encrypted-pdf-cause.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33443091/python-10-docling-parse-encrypted-pdf-cause.zip)

comment.body:
Thanks for the thorough write-up and the reproducer, this is a great catch — the default backend really shouldn't report an encrypted PDF the same way as a corrupt file.

I'd like to take this on. I'll start with a reproducer against the current `main`, then work on the fix in `docling_parse_backend.py` (detecting the encrypted input and surfacing an explicit password-protected error, mirroring what the iWork backend already does), plus regression tests in `tests/test_pdf_password.py` covering both backends.

issue.title: No way to restrict OCR to scanned pages since bitmap_area_threshold removal (#3710)
issue.body:
### Bug

Since 2.116.0 ([#3710](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/pull/3710)), passing `bitmap_area_threshold` in `OcrOptions` raises a validation error, and the conversion fails even when `do_ocr=False`:

```
1 validation error for EasyOcrOptions
bitmap_area_threshold
  Extra inputs are not permitted
```

`force_full_page_ocr` was deprecated with a compatibility bridge, but `bitmap_area_threshold` was removed outright. Existing configurations (e.g. docling-serve clients sending `ocr_custom_config`) break on upgrade, with no warning and nothing in the changelog.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from docling.datamodel.pipeline_options import EasyOcrOptions

EasyOcrOptions(bitmap_area_threshold=0.97)  # ValidationError
```

### Missing functionality

Before 2.116.0, `bitmap_area_threshold` could be used to OCR **only scanned pages**: with a high value (e.g. `0.97`), a page was OCR'd in full only when bitmaps covered at least that share of it, and smaller images (logos, icons, photos without text) were skipped (see also #2101).

None of the new `OcrMode` values can express this:

- `FULL_PAGE` OCRs every page, including born-digital ones.
- `LAYOUT_REGIONS` OCRs every region.
- `PDF_AWARE_LAYOUT_REGIONS` / `DEFAULT` OCR every cluster that overlaps a bitmap, whatever its size, so logos get OCR'd.

On documents with many logos or images this wastes compute for no gain.

### Proposal

Either of these would restore the use case:

- a new mode, e.g. `OcrMode.SCANNED_PAGES`: full-page OCR when bitmap coverage ≥ a threshold, otherwise no OCR on that page; or
- a `min_bitmap_coverage` / `min_region_area` option that `PDF_AWARE_LAYOUT_REGIONS` respects.

`BaseOcrModel._deduplicate_rects` already computes page bitmap coverage, so the building block exists.

Separately: accepting `bitmap_area_threshold` with a deprecation warning, instead of raising an error, would avoid breaking existing configurations.

### Version

```
Docling version: 2.138.0
Docling Core version: 2.101.1
Docling IBM Models version: 4.0.3
Docling Parse version: 7.22.3
Python: cpython-312 (3.12.15)
Coming through docling-serve: 1.37.0
```

I'd like to take this one. My plan: restore backward compatibility for `bitmap_area_threshold` in the OCR options — accept it with a deprecation warning (same treatment `force_full_page_ocr` already got) instead of raising a `ValidationError`, so existing configurations like docling-serve clients sending `ocr_custom_config` stop breaking on upgrade. I'll also look at the scanned-pages-only use case while I'm in there.

### Submission checklist

### Package (Required)

- [x] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic

- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

_No response_

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult
from langchain_core.tools import tool

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import ContextEditingMiddleware
from langchain.agents.middleware.context_editing import ClearToolUsesEdit

# An sensitive args that we want to clear after the tool execution
SSN = "123-45-6789"
CALL = {"type": "tool_call", "id": "call-1", "name": "lookup_account", "args": {"ssn": SSN}}


@tool
def lookup_account(ssn: str) -> str:
    """Look up an account by SSN."""
    print(f"lookup_account called with ssn={ssn}")
    return f"Account for {ssn}: balance $100"


class FakeModel(BaseChatModel):
    encoding: str = "tool_call"
    seen: list = []  # every model call's input messages

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "fake"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):
        return self

    def _generate(self, messages, **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        # collect the message history to debug
        self.seen.append(list(messages))
        if len(self.seen) - 1 == 0:  # turn 1: call the tool
            msg = (
                AIMessage(content_blocks=[dict(CALL)])
                if self.encoding == "content_block"
                else AIMessage(content="", tool_calls=[dict(CALL)])
            )
        else:
            msg = AIMessage("done")
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=msg)])


def run(encoding: str) -> list:
    model = FakeModel(encoding=encoding)
    agent = create_agent(
        model,
        tools=[lookup_account],
        middleware=[
            ContextEditingMiddleware(
                edits=[ClearToolUsesEdit(trigger=1, keep=0, clear_tool_inputs=True)],
                token_counter=lambda messages: 1000,
            )
        ],
    )
    agent.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage("go")]})
    return model.seen[-1]  # post-clear request the model received on turn 2


# invoke tool by use the tool_call field
res1 = run("tool_call")
assert SSN not in str(res1), f"SSN leaked"
# invoke tool by only use the content block
res2 = run("content_block")
assert SSN not in str(res2), f"SSN leaked"
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
First we can see each run() can successfully invoke the target tool lookup_account. But after clear the tool input, only the run("tool_call") can be clear out successfully.

lookup_account called with ssn=123-45-6789
lookup_account called with ssn=123-45-6789
Traceback (most recent call last):
    assert SSN not in str(res2), f"SSN leaked in content_block: {res2}"
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError: SSN leaked in content_block
```

### Description

When `clear_tool_inputs=True` is set on `ClearToolUsesEdit`, the agent should automatically clear the tool input information after the invoked tool executes. However, when the tool call is encoded as a `content_block`, the tool call information is not cleared. As a result, the tool inputs remain in every subsequent model request, which can lead to an unnecessary increase in token cost (and continued exposure of the input values).

### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Linux
> OS Version:  #149~20.04.1-Ubuntu SMP Wed Apr 16 08:29:56 UTC 2025
> Python Version:  3.11.17 (main, Oct  1 2026, 20:17:42) [GCC 14.3.0]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.6.10
> langchain: 1.4.4
> langsmith: 0.14.8
> langchain_openai: 1.7.1
> langchain_protocol: 0.0.19
> langchain_tests: 1.1.9
> langchain_text_splitters: 1.1.3
> langgraph_sdk: 0.4.7

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

comment.body:
Thanks for the clear bug report and the minimal, runnable reproducer — the inconsistency is clear: `ClearToolUsesEdit` with `clear_tool_inputs=True` strips tool inputs from `AIMessage.tool_calls` but leaves them in place when the tool call is encoded as a `content_block`, so the sensitive inputs keep being re-sent on every subsequent model request.

I'd like to take this one. The fix is bounded to the clearing logic in the context-editing middleware: also clear the `args` of tool-call entries inside `content_blocks` (covering both tool-call encodings), with regression tests for both paths. I'll open a PR once assigned.

issue.title: fix: require confirmation by default for PythonTools code-executing tools
issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10053 (security: CWE-913, missing default confirmation gate for code-executing tools).

`PythonTools` code-executing tools (`run_python_code`, `save_to_file_and_run`, `run_python_file_return_variable`, `pip_install_package`, `uv_pip_install_package`) now require human confirmation by default: the orchestration loop pauses them (`tool_call_paused`) instead of executing a model-requested call immediately. Previously the loop executed every model-requested call at once, so prompt injection against an agent processing untrusted content could drive `exec()`/`runpy()`/subprocess in the host process with no pause.

Design is default-deny with opt-out, and scoped to the highest-risk tools only:
- No `requires_confirmation_tools` passed (or `None`) -> the 5 code-executing tools are gated; `read_file`/`list_files` unchanged.
- An explicit value (including `[]`) is used as-is, so automated/sandboxed setups can opt out deliberately with `PythonTools(requires_confirmation_tools=[])`.
- Per-tool `requires_confirmation` continues to work as the override (registration logic untouched); the fix reuses the existing `Toolkit.requires_confirmation_tools` mechanism (same pattern as `KnowledgeTools` gating `remove_content`).

The approach was discussed on the issue; happy to adjust if maintainers prefer a different direction (e.g. an Agent-level policy gate).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Breaking change

The default behavior changes: model-requested code-execution tool calls now pause for confirmation. Explicit opt-out is available (`requires_confirmation_tools=[]`).

---

## Checklist

- [x] Code complies with style guidelines
- [x] Ran format/validation scripts (`./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh`)
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (comments, docstrings)
- [ ] Examples and guides: Relevant cookbook examples have been included or updated (if applicable)
- [x] Tested in clean environment
- [x] Tests added/updated (if applicable)

### Duplicate and AI-Generated PR Check

- [x] I have searched existing [open pull requests](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pulls) and confirmed that no other PR already addresses this issue
- [ ] If a similar PR exists, I have explained below why this PR is a better approach
- [ ] Check if this PR was entirely AI-generated (by Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

---

## Additional Notes

Security considerations:
- This closes the default-open execution path reported in #10053 but is not a sandbox: the class docstring and `warn()` still document that `safe_globals`/`safe_locals`/`restrict_to_base_dir` are not security boundaries and that untrusted input needs a real sandbox (separate process/container, scrubbed env).
- `ShellTools`/`DaytonaTools` have the same shape of risk; intentionally left out of this PR to keep the change minimal and auditable -- happy to follow up if maintainers want the same default there.

Verification (all offline, no network/keys):
- Reproduced the issue PoC: pre-fix the marker file was written via `exec()`; post-fix the same default assembly yields `tool_call_paused` and no execution.
- New regression tests in `libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_python_tools.py`: default gating, explicit opt-out, explicit list respected, end-to-end pause, end-to-end opt-out execution -- 27/27 pass in that file; `./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh` pass.
