issue.title: fix(router): keep OpenAI tool-calling requests on OpenAI-protocol deployments
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- One model name mixes `openai/...` and `anthropic/...` deployments
- OpenAI-format tool requests sometimes land on the Anthropic deployment
- The Anthropic deployment then mistranslates or rejects the tool call

How it solves it:

- Router matches OpenAI-format tool requests to OpenAI-protocol deployments
- Only narrows the pool when such a deployment exists in the group
- Groups without one behave exactly as before, translation included

## User Flow

Before: tool calls intermittently fail for a mixed-protocol model group

1. They put an `openai/...` and an `anthropic/...` deployment behind one model name
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with OpenAI-format `tools`
3. Roughly half the requests fail, because the router picked the Anthropic deployment and the tool contract broke in translation

After: the same requests consistently reach the OpenAI-protocol deployment

1. Same config, same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with OpenAI-format `tools`
2. Every request goes to the `openai/...` deployment; the Anthropic one is skipped for these requests
3. Tool calls succeed consistently instead of failing intermittently

## Relevant issues

Fixes #43685

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

No live provider keys are available in this environment, so the proof below exercises the user-facing behavior directly: which deployment the router selects for the reporter's exact config, with no network involved. Shared setup: a Router with one model group holding `openai/claude-4.6-sonnet` and `anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet` (simple-shuffle), request carries OpenAI-format `tools`.

### Before (118ce3cc)

1. Select a deployment 400 times (200 sync, 200 async) for the tool-calling request
2. Observed: `{'openai/claude-4.6-sonnet': 200, 'anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet': 200}` - the Anthropic deployment was picked about half the time, reproducing the issue

### After (7912074a)

1. Same script, same config, same request
2. Observed: `{'openai/claude-4.6-sonnet': 400}` - the Anthropic deployment is never selected for OpenAI-format tool requests

Mutation check on the new tests: disabling the filter makes 4 tests fail (including both sync and async router wiring tests); removing the no-OpenAI-deployment fallback makes the translation-preservation test fail; restoring the code makes all pass. Full `tests/unit/router_utils/test_router_utils_common_utils.py` plus `tests/unit/test_router/test_router.py`: 828 passed, 11 skipped.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- When no deployment in the group speaks the OpenAI protocol, candidates are left untouched so existing provider translation keeps working; the issue also asked for a clear gateway-side error in that case, but erroring would break setups that rely on translation today
- Filtering keys off the `{"type": "function", "function": {...}}` tool shape, so Anthropic-format inbound tool requests are unaffected

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

issue.title: fix(anthropic): forward http:// image URLs as url sources instead of downloading
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- http:// image URLs were downloaded by the proxy and sent to Anthropic as base64
- https:// URLs on the same path were forwarded untouched as url sources

How it solves it:

- http:// URLs are now forwarded as url sources, same as https://
- Bedrock invoke, Vertex AI and Snowflake still convert to base64, since those providers have no URL source

Intentional product change: callers whose http:// image host is reachable only by the proxy will now see a provider-side fetch error instead of a silent proxy download. Use https:// or data URLs when the provider cannot reach the host

## User Flow

Before: a developer sending an image over plain http gets silently different behavior than over https

1. They send POST /v1/chat/completions with `"image_url": {"url": "http://img-host/pic.png"}` on a model routed to Anthropic
2. The call returns 200, but the provider received `source: {"type": "base64", ...}` with bytes the proxy downloaded, and the image host logged a GET from the proxy
3. The same request with an https:// URL arrives at the provider untouched as `source: {"type": "url", ...}`

After: http:// is forwarded exactly like https://

1. They send the same POST with the http:// image URL
2. The provider receives `source: {"type": "url", "url": "http://img-host/pic.png"}`, and the image host sees no request from the proxy
3. If the provider cannot fetch that URL, its error reaches the caller instead of silent bytes

## Relevant issues

Fixes #43098

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Verification ran at the request-transformation layer, which is the layer this fix touches. No live provider call was made, since this environment has no provider credentials or external network. Download functions were stubbed to record calls instead of hitting the network

### Before (eff6fc1)

1. `create_anthropic_image_param("http://example.com/image.png")` invoked the download and returned `source: {"type": "base64", ...}`
2. `AnthropicConfig().inlines_remote_media(...)` returned True for an http:// image URL, so `async_transform_request` downloaded it before conversion
3. The same calls with https:// returned `source: {"type": "url", ...}` with no download attempted

### After (26684a6)

1. `create_anthropic_image_param("http://example.com/image.png")` returns `source: {"type": "url", "url": "http://example.com/image.png"}` with no download attempted
2. `inlines_remote_media` returns False for both schemes, so `async_transform_request` forwards both as url sources
3. `is_bedrock_invoke=True` (Bedrock invoke, Vertex AI, Snowflake) still converts both schemes to base64

New regression tests (5): `test_create_anthropic_image_param_with_http_url_forwards_url`, `test_create_anthropic_image_param_with_http_url_still_base64_for_bedrock`, `test_anthropic_messages_pt_with_http_url_image`, `test_inlines_remote_media_never_inlines_image_urls[http/https]`. Each bug-covering test was verified to fail on the pre-fix code and pass after the fix. Related suites (`test_prompt_factory.py`, `test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py`, `test_image_handling.py`, vertex-ai anthropic image tests) show no new failures against baseline

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Private http:// image hosts unreachable by the provider now fail at the provider instead of being fetched by the proxy

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

Would appreciate your review when you have a moment — thank you!

issue.title: [Bug] Native gRPC Generate caps output at 128 tokens when max_new_tokens is unset
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On the native gRPC server (`--grpc-port`), a `Generate` request whose `sampling_params.max_new_tokens` is unset stops at 128 tokens. `sampling_params_to_map` in `rust/sglang-grpc/src/utils/request_utils.rs` skips unset fields, so `SamplingParams` falls back to its default of 128. An HTTP client can ask for no limit with `"max_new_tokens": null`. Proto3 has no null, so a gRPC client cannot. `smg_grpc_servicer` already maps an unset `max_new_tokens` to `None`. Suggested fix: pass `max_new_tokens: null` to the scheduler when the field is unset. ### Reproduction ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000 --grpc-port 30001 --context-length 4096 ``` With Python stubs generated from `proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto`: ```python import grpc, sglang_pb2 as pb, sglang_pb2_grpc as pb_grpc stub = pb_grpc.SglangServiceStub(grpc.insecure_channel("127.0.0.1:30001")) request = pb.GenerateRequest( input_ids=[7985, 220, 19, 15, 15, 4244, 911, 35517, 13], # "Write 400 words about rivers." sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams(temperature=0, ignore_eos=True), stream=True, ) meta = {} for response in stub.Generate(request): meta = response.meta_info or meta print(meta["completion_tokens"]) # 128 ``` Same 9-token prompt with `ignore_eos`: | Request | completion_tokens | | --- | --- | | gRPC `Generate`, `max_new_tokens` unset | 128 | | HTTP `/generate`, `"max_new_tokens": null` | 4085 | | `/v1/chat/completions`, no `max_tokens` | 4077 | Reproduced on 0.5.21. The same code is on main (7dc2930). ### Environment
python3 -m sglang.check_env ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.1, V13.1.115 CUDA Driver Version: 580.178.04 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.21 sglang-kernel: 0.4.7 flashinfer_python: 0.6.18 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: Module Not Found numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.4 fastapi: 0.142.2 huggingface_hub: 1.33.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.40.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b2 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.2.0 uvicorn: 0.54.0 uvloop: 0.23.0 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.7 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 1.11.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-23 0 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1048576 ```

comment.body:
Thanks for filing this with such a precise pointer to the root cause — this looks like a real bug.

I'd like to work on a fix. My plan: in `sampling_params_to_map` (`rust/sglang-grpc/src/utils/request_utils.rs`), treat an unset `max_new_tokens` as no-limit (mirroring the HTTP `null` behavior) instead of letting it fall through to the 128-token `SamplingParams` default. I'll open a PR with a regression test once implemented.

An HTTP client can ask for no limit with `"max_new_tokens": null`. Proto3 has no null, so a gRPC client cannot. `smg_grpc_servicer` already maps an unset `max_new_tokens` to `None`. Suggested fix: pass `max_new_tokens: null` to the scheduler when the field is unset. ### Reproduction ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000 --grpc-port 30001 --context-length 4096 ``` With Python stubs generated from `proto/sglang/runtime/v1/sglang.proto`: ```python import grpc, sglang_pb2 as pb, sglang_pb2_grpc as pb_grpc stub = pb_grpc.SglangServiceStub(grpc.insecure_channel("127.0.0.1:30001")) request = pb.GenerateRequest( input_ids=[7985, 220, 19, 15, 15, 4244, 911, 35517, 13], # "Write 400 words about rivers." sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams(temperature=0, ignore_eos=True), stream=True, ) meta = {} for response in stub.Generate(request): meta = response.meta_info or meta print(meta["completion_tokens"]) # 128 ``` Same 9-token prompt with `ignore_eos`: | Request | completion_tokens | | --- | --- | | gRPC `Generate`, `max_new_tokens` unset | 128 | | HTTP `/generate`, `"max_new_tokens": null` | 4085 | | `/v1/chat/completions`, no `max_tokens` | 4077 | Reproduced on 0.5.21. The same code is on main (7dc2930). ### Environment
python3 -m sglang.check_env ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.1, V13.1.115 CUDA Driver Version: 580.178.04 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.21 sglang-kernel: 0.4.7 flashinfer_python: 0.6.18 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: Module Not Found numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.4 fastapi: 0.142.2 huggingface_hub: 1.33.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.40.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b2 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.2.0 uvicorn: 0.54.0 uvloop: 0.23.0 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.7 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 1.11.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-23 0 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1048576 ```

issue.title: Chandra parser: a layout block with several parts is split into unrelated top-level items
issue.body:
# Chandra parser: a layout block with several parts is split into unrelated top-level items ### Bug Chandra returns one `
` for each layout block. So it gives **one bbox for each block**. `parse_chandra_html()` maps a `Text` block that contains an ``, or more than one `

`, to **several separate items directly under `body`**: - The first part gets the bbox of the **whole block**, so its bbox is larger than its content. - The other parts get **no bbox and no parent** that links them to the block. Nothing in the document tells which block they came from, or where they are on the page. A `Form` block with the same content does not have this problem. It gets a `FieldRegionItem` that holds the block bbox, and the parts are its children. This happens in real documents for signature and stamp blocks, for example *company name → signature image → name and title*. The name and title text then has no position and no link to the signature. No text is lost. Only the link from the text to its block, and its position, is lost. ### Steps to reproduce The script below uses only synthetic HTML in Chandra's format. It does not need a model or a server. Page size 1000×1000 makes the bbox values equal to the `data-bbox` values.

repro.py ```python from docling_core.types.doc import Size from docling.utils.chandra_utils import parse_chandra_html PAGE = Size(width=1000, height=1000) # Chandra coordinates are 0-1000, so bbox = data-bbox def dump(title: str, html: str) -> None: doc = parse_chandra_html(content=html, original_page_size=PAGE, page_no=1) print(f"### {title}") print("print_element_tree():") doc.print_element_tree() print("iterate_items():") for item, level in doc.iterate_items(): bbox = item.prov[0].bbox.as_tuple() if item.prov else None print(f" level={level} {item.self_ref} parent={item.parent.cref} bbox={bbox}") print() BLOCK = 'data-label="{label}" data-bbox="100 700 500 900"' # 1. Text block: text, an image with its own bbox, text dump("1. Text block: text + + text", f'

Approved by Example Ltd.
' '
Jane Doe, Manager

') # 2. Same content as two paragraphs, no image: the image is not the cause dump("2. Text block: two

, no image", f'

Approved by Example Ltd.

' '

Jane Doe, Manager

') # 3. The image has no bbox of its own: the picture takes the block bbox dump("3. Text block: without data-bbox + text", f'


Jane Doe, Manager

') # 4. Comparison: the same content as a Form block keeps a located container dump("4. Comparison: Form block", f'

Approved by Example Ltd.

' '

Jane Doe, Manager

') ```
**Output:** ```text ### 1. Text block: text + + text print_element_tree(): 0: unspecified with name=_root_ 1: text: Approved by Example Ltd. 2: picture 3: text: Jane Doe, Manager iterate_items(): level=1 #/texts/0 parent=#/body bbox=(100.0, 700.0, 500.0, 900.0) <- bbox of the whole block level=1 #/pictures/0 parent=#/body bbox=(110.0, 760.0, 300.0, 840.0) <- its own bbox level=1 #/texts/1 parent=#/body bbox=None <- no bbox, no link to the block ### 2. Text block: two

, no image print_element_tree(): 0: unspecified with name=_root_ 1: text: Approved by Example Ltd. 2: text: Jane Doe, Manager iterate_items(): level=1 #/texts/0 parent=#/body bbox=(100.0, 700.0, 500.0, 900.0) level=1 #/texts/1 parent=#/body bbox=None ### 3. Text block: without data-bbox + text print_element_tree(): 0: unspecified with name=_root_ 1: picture 2: text: Jane Doe, Manager iterate_items(): level=1 #/pictures/0 parent=#/body bbox=(100.0, 700.0, 500.0, 900.0) <- picture takes the block bbox level=1 #/texts/0 parent=#/body bbox=None ### 4. Comparison: Form block print_element_tree(): 0: unspecified with name=_root_ 1: field_region 2: text: Approved by Example Ltd. 3: text: Jane Doe, Manager iterate_items(): level=1 #/field_regions/0 parent=#/body bbox=(100.0, 700.0, 500.0, 900.0) level=2 #/texts/0 parent=#/field_regions/0 bbox=None level=2 #/texts/1 parent=#/field_regions/0 bbox=None ``` (I added the `<-` comments.) ### Expected behavior The parts of one layout block stay together under one parent, as they do for a `Form` block: ```text body └── ├── TextItem 'Approved by Example Ltd.' ├── PictureItem (its own bbox) └── TextItem 'Jane Doe, Manager' ``` The block bbox should describe the block, not only its first part. ### Possible fix The parts of a block need a container that can hold the block bbox. Today only a `DocItem` has `prov`, and a `GroupItem` cannot hold a bbox. I see two options: **Option 1: add `prov` to `GroupItem` (docling-core), then use a group for each block that splits (docling).** - The block bbox goes on the group, as it goes on the `FieldRegionItem` for a `Form` block. The parts are children of the group. - The meaning is correct: a group is a neutral container for mixed content (text and pictures). - This is a larger change in docling-core. For example, `DoclingDocument.concatenate()` changes the page numbers in `prov` only for a `DocItem`, and `iterate_items(page_nrs=…)` filters by page only for a `DocItem`. Both would need to handle groups too. **Option 2: use an empty `TextItem` as the container (docling only).** - The container has the block label and the block bbox. The parser already does this for a labeled block with several runs (an empty `TextItem` that holds an `InlineGroup`). - It needs no docling-core change. - But a `TextItem` that contains a `PictureItem` is a new tree shape, and `export_to_html()` writes an empty `

` before the parts. With both options, a block with one item does not change. Only blocks that split get a container. I am glad to open a PR. I would like your view first, because `test_chandra_mixed_structure_and_rich_table_cells` asserts today's flat output. **Questions:** 1. Do you accept a change to the flat output for blocks that split? 2. Which option do you prefer? 3. For option 1: is `prov` on `GroupItem` something docling-core would consider? ### Docling version docling 2.138.0 (docling-slim 2.138.0), docling-core 2.101.1. Also reproduced on `main`. ### Python version Python 3.12.3

comment.body: The fix is up: https://github.com/docling-project/docling/pull/4808 — multi-part `Text` blocks now map to an empty `TextItem` container holding the block bbox, with the parts as children (mirroring the `Form` → `FieldRegionItem` pattern). Single-part blocks are unchanged, and `test_chandra_mixed_structure_and_rich_table_cells` is updated to the new structure as you anticipated. Thanks again for the excellent reproducer.

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [x] langchain-openai

- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

_No response_

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langchain_core.messages.content import create_plaintext_block, create_text_block

msg = HumanMessage(content_blocks=[create_text_block("Summarise this."), create_plaintext_block(text="hello world")])
# {'type': 'text-plain', 'mime_type': 'text/plain', 'text': 'hello world', ...}

from langchain_aws.chat_models.bedrock_converse import _messages_to_bedrock
_messages_to_bedrock([msg], None, provider="anthropic")
# ValueError: Unsupported data content block type: 'text-plain'. Supported types are: 'image', 'file', 'video'.

from langchain_google_genai import ChatGoogleGenerativeAI
ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model="gemini-2.5-flash", api_key="x")._prepare_request(messages=[msg])
# ValueError: Data content block must contain 'url', 'base64', or 'data' field.

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", api_key="x")._get_request_payload([msg])
# ValueError: Block of type text-plain is not supported.
```

```shell
    parts = _convert_to_parts(message.content, model=model)
  File ".../langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py", line 732, in _convert_to_parts
    raise ValueError(msg)
ValueError: Data content block must contain 'url', 'base64', or 'data' field.

# langchain-openai
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py", line 3828, in _get_request_payload
    payload = super()._get_request_payload(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
  File ".../langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py", line 2044, in _get_request_payload
    else _convert_message_to_dict(m)
  File ".../langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py", line 478, in _convert_message_to_dict
    "content": _format_message_content(message.content, api=api, role=message.type)
  File ".../langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py", line 426, in _format_message_content
    formatted_block = convert_to_openai_data_block(block, api=api)

ValueError: Block of type text-plain is not supported.
```

### Description

Tested with `langchain-core` 1.6.8, `langchain-aws` 1.8.1, `langchain-google-genai` 4.4.0 and `langchain-openai` 1.7.0.

`PlainTextContentBlock` documents `text` as optional "if the data is provided as base64", and `create_plaintext_block(text=...)` builds exactly this block. But the Bedrock, Gemini and OpenAI converters each read a `text-plain` block's `url`, `base64`/`data` or `file_id`, and ignore or reject inline `text`, with three different errors (see the example; each call is an internal request builder that `invoke` uses and that runs offline).

Expected: a `text-plain` block that carries inline `text` is sent as text, the way a `text` block is, or the standard-block docs say it is not supported for sending. Today the block that the library's own factory creates cannot be sent to any of the three providers.

`langchain-anthropic` 1.7.5 accepts the same block and sends it as a text document (`{'type': 'document', 'source': {'type': 'text', 'media_type': 'text/plain', 'data': 'hello world'}}`), so this is also inconsistent across providers.

Workaround: send a `text` block.

The converters live in `langchain-aws`, `langchain-google-genai` and `langchain-openai`; I am filing this here because the block type is defined in `langchain-core`. Happy to split it per package.

> langchain_google_genai: 4.4.0

Thanks for the thorough report and minimal reproducer — the inconsistency is clear: a `text-plain` block created by the library's own `create_plaintext_block(text=...)` can't be sent through the Bedrock, Gemini, or OpenAI converters, while langchain-anthropic handles the same block as a text document.

I'd like to take this one. The fix is bounded to the data-block converters: when a `text-plain` block carries inline `text`, send it as text the way a `text` block is sent (langchain-core's `convert_to_openai_data_block` in `block_translators/openai.py`, plus the equivalent handling in the Bedrock and Gemini converters), with regression tests per converter. I'll open a PR once assigned.

issue.title: [Bug]:
issue.body:
### Description

When auto_router/complexity_router with classifier_type: llm_v2 (Fuse v2) is used from an agent client that calls /v1/responses with previous_response_id (VS Code GitHub Copilot BYOK in our case), only the turns that carry a human message get classified. Every tool-continuation request in between skips the classifier and goes to complexity_router_default_model.

Result: the classifier correctly picks the capable solver for the task (e.g. REASONING → gpt-6.1-sol), but the rest of the agent loop (reading tool results, writing the plan/code) runs on the default/efficient model (gpt-6-luna).

In one Plan-mode session: 22 requests, 3 routed to the capable model (the human turns), 19 to the default model (all tool continuations).

Request shape of the continuation turns
{
  "model": "some_router",
  "previous_response_id": "<resp id – decodes to litellm:custom_llm_provider:azure_ai;model_id:<capable deployment id>;...>",
  "input": [
    { "type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_...", "output": "..." },
    { "type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_...", "output": "..." }
  ]
}
No instructions, no system message, no user message. The full context lives server-side and is referenced only via previous_response_id.

Routing decision logged for these requests
"routing_decision": {
  "cause": "default_fallback",
  "router_type": "complexity",
  "routed_model": "gpt-6-luna",
  "conversation_continuing": false
}
UI shows: Default model, no route matched.

**Root cause (from reading the code)**

In complexity_router.py, _classify_and_route() calls _extract_current_ask_and_system_prompt(...). For these requests, user_message is None (only tool output), so it returns early with cause="default_fallback" before any classifier or continuation logic runs.

llm_v2.py only contains the judge prompt / schema / quality-gap policy and has no continuation or route-reuse logic.

The Fuse v2 PR ([#41272](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/41272)) describes the design as: ask the judge at the start of each task, then reuse the model choice. Not re-classifying tool outputs is fine, but falling to the default model instead of reusing the original choice contradicts that design.

Notes:

conversation_continuing is false even though previous_response_id is set and points to a response produced by the capable deployment.
Session grouping in the logs works (via litellm_trace_id / previous_response_id), but router session affinity keys on metadata session_id, which this client does not send, so affinity does not help either.
Setting re-classification to "every request" does not change anything, because the early return happens first.

**Expected behavior**
For /v1/responses requests with previous_response_id and no human ask, the router should reuse the deployment/tier that produced the referenced response (it's already encoded in the LiteLLM response id), or at least treat the request as conversation_continuing=true and apply the prior routing decision. It should not fall to complexity_router_default_model.

### Config

```yaml
{
  "model": "auto_router/complexity_router",
  "complexity_router_config": {
    "classifier_type": "llm_v2",
    "<efficient/capable solver + judge config here>": "..."
  },
  "complexity_router_default_model": "gpt-6-luna"
}
```

### LiteLLM Version

v1.103.1

### Steps to Repro

Create an auto router with Fuse v2:
{  "model": "auto_router/complexity_router",  "complexity_router_config": {    "classifier_type": "llm_v2",    "<efficient solver>": "gpt-6-luna",    "<capable solver>": "gpt-6.1-sol",    "<judge model>": "<judge>"  },  "complexity_router_default_model": "gpt-6-luna"}
Point an agent client that uses /v1/responses with previous_response_id at the router (e.g. VS Code GitHub Copilot BYOK, model = some_router).
Send a task that the judge classifies as needing the capable solver (e.g. a planning/refactor task in Agent or Plan mode).
The first request contains a user message → llm_v2_classifier runs → routed to gpt-6.1-sol. The model returns tool calls.
The client sends the tool results back as a new request: input = only function_call_output items + previous_response_id pointing to the Sol response (no user/system message).
Check the request logs / routing_decision for this request.
Observed: cause: "default_fallback", conversation_continuing: false, routed to gpt-6-luna ("Default model, no route matched"). Every subsequent tool continuation in the loop also goes to the default model. Only the next human turn is classified again.

Expected: Tool continuations reuse the model chosen for the task (gpt-6.1-sol), since previous_response_id references a response from that deployment.

### Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Routing: load balancing, fallbacks, retries, cooldowns

### How are you deploying?

Helm chart, componentized (recommended)

comment.body:
Thanks for the unusually thorough root-cause write-up, @mehmetcankamar — pinpointing the early return in `_extract_current_ask_and_system_prompt` makes the fix direction clear.

I'd like to take this one. I'll work on a fix so tool-continuation requests carrying `previous_response_id` (with no human ask) reuse the prior routing decision instead of falling back to `complexity_router_default_model`, plus regression tests for the continuation path. Will open a PR once it's ready.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--revision pre-final` and

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

startup fails:

```
File ".../vllm/config/speculative.py", line 1489, in __post_init__
    and self.num_speculative_tokens % n_predict != 0
ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero
```

For `method="mtp"`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` copies `model` (and `quantization`) from the target model config, but the draft `ModelConfig` is created with `revision=self.revision`, which is `None` unless set explicitly in the speculative config. The MTP draft therefore loads config (and weights) from the repo's default branch instead of the target's revision.

Passing the revision explicitly fixes it:

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"revision":"pre-final"}'
```

### Expected behavior
For `method="mtp"` (draft = target checkpoint), the draft should inherit the target's `revision` (and `code_revision`) when not set, the same way it inherits `model` and `quantization`.

### Additional notes
- If `n_predict` resolves to 0, the divisibility check should raise a readable error instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
The fix is up for review: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61210

It makes the MTP draft inherit revision/code_revision from the target model config (unless explicitly overridden), so the draft resolves config/weights from the target's --revision instead of the default branch, and it raises a readable ValueError instead of ZeroDivisionError when the draft checkpoint resolves to n_predict=0. Happy to adjust based on your feedback — thanks again for the detailed report!

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--revision pre-final` and

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

startup fails:

```
File ".../vllm/config/speculative.py", line 1489, in __post_init__
    and self.num_speculative_tokens % n_predict != 0
ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero
```

For `method="mtp"`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` copies `model` (and `quantization`) from the target model config, but the draft `ModelConfig` is created with `revision=self.revision`, which is `None` unless set explicitly in the speculative config. The MTP draft therefore loads config (and weights) from the repo's default branch instead of the target's revision.

Passing the revision explicitly fixes it:

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"revision":"pre-final"}'
```

### Expected behavior
For `method="mtp"` (draft = target checkpoint), the draft should inherit the target's `revision` (and `code_revision`) when not set, the same way it inherits `model` and `quantization`.

### Additional notes
- If `n_predict` resolves to 0, the divisibility check should raise a readable error instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: Raise on user tool name collision with base tools
issue.body:
## Problem

When `add_base_tools=True`, `MultiStepAgent._setup_tools` registers the user's tools first and then merges the base tools over them with `self.tools.update(...)`. A user tool whose `name` collides with a base tool (`web_search`, `visit_webpage`, or `python_interpreter` on `ToolCallingAgent`) is **silently replaced** — no warning, no error. The agent keeps running, but the user's tool is unreachable: the system-prompt schema, the `CodeAgent` executor namespace (`send_tools`) and `execute_tool_call` all route to the built-in tool instead.

Thanks @effson for the clear report on #2885 — a user tool being silently swapped for a built-in one is a nasty footgun.

## Root cause

```python
self.tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in tools}
if add_base_tools:
    self.tools.update(
        {name: cls() for name, cls in TOOL_MAPPING.items() ...}  # overwrites silently
    )
```

`_validate_tools_and_managed_agents` only checks the user-passed tools, managed agent names, and the agent's own name, so the collision with base tools (which share the same `self.tools` routing namespace) is never caught.

## Fix

`_setup_tools` now computes the names of the base tools to be added from `TOOL_MAPPING` keys first — respecting the existing `python_interpreter`/`ToolCallingAgent` filter, so a user tool named `python_interpreter` on `CodeAgent` is still allowed — and checks them for collisions **before instantiating** any base tool, so a missing optional dependency can no longer mask the clear error. The check covers both user tool names and managed agent names (`set(self.tools) | set(self.managed_agents)`), since managed agents share the executor namespace (`{**self.tools, **self.managed_agents}`) with tools and would otherwise shadow a base tool there. On collision it raises a `ValueError` naming the colliding name(s); the error message suggests renaming or passing `add_base_tools=False`.

## Breaking change (release note)

Anyone who currently passes their own `web_search`/`visit_webpage` (or a managed agent with such a name) together with `add_base_tools=True` silently gets the built-in tool today; after this change agent construction raises a `ValueError` instead. This is the intended trade — a loud error beats a silently swapped tool — but it changes upgrade behavior for that pattern. Mitigation: rename the tool/managed agent, or pass `add_base_tools=False`.

## Tests

- `test_user_tool_colliding_with_base_tool_name_raises`: covers `web_search`/`visit_webpage` collisions on `CodeAgent`, the `python_interpreter` collision on `ToolCallingAgent`, the allowed `python_interpreter` case on `CodeAgent` (no such base tool is added there), normal coexistence of a non-colliding user tool with base tools, and the `add_base_tools=False` path.
- `test_managed_agent_colliding_with_base_tool_name_raises` (new): a managed agent named `web_search` with `add_base_tools=True` raises; a non-colliding managed agent works fine alongside base tools.
- `test_collision_check_runs_before_base_tool_instantiation` (new): with a `TOOL_MAPPING` entry whose constructor raises `ImportError` (simulating a missing optional dependency), the collision still raises the clear `ValueError` first.
- Collision tests: 3 passed. Full `tests/test_agents.py`: no new failures vs the pristine checkout (the 11 failures + 2 errors are pre-existing environment issues — missing optional deps/models).

Fixes #2885
